name: Ruling A — Mass Battle Tree A must be removed
statement: Jordan ruled (2026-08-23) that Mass Battle Tree A (systems/mass_battle/sim/, ~1,900 lines) is deprecated and must be removed in favour of Tree B (tests/sim/mass_battle/, the canon engine per the earlier J2 ruling). Execution is blocked: Tree A is faction-scale, Tree B is cell-scale, and the strategic-to-cell adapter (faction.Mil -> Unit) was never designed — its own docstring admits "[GAP: no canonical spec for faction.Mil -> Unit construction]". Five test guards fire on naive deletion (test_j2_mass_battle_seam.py, test_mass_battle_systems_movement.py, test_import_cycle_game_state_npe.py, test_degree_ladder_single_owner.py, test_pipeline_reach.py).

name: Ruling B — TN is always 7, including threadwork
statement: Jordan ruled TN is always 7 everywhere, including threadwork. The ruling is already true in behaviour and false only in declaration: engine/autoload/dice_engine.py:75-84's roll_pool stores tn and never reads it (hardwired TN-7 face rule at :53-61), so every non-7 TN declaration has been a no-op. Two live non-conforming sites remain: threadwork/sim/operations.py:48-50 (TN_BINDING=8, TN_POP=8, TN_POP_BINDING=9, dead) and the DEPRECATED combat/sim/combat.py's WEAPON_TN_BASE + _weapon_tn (5-8). The continuous engine (dice_engine.py:87-101, _CONTINUOUS_PARAMS) DOES read tn and must also be fixed to keep the two entry points agreeing.
formula: roll_pool(pool_size, tn=7, ...) — tn stored on RollResult, never read; face rule hardwired for TN 7

name: Ruling C — one single pool document for all subsystems
statement: Jordan ruled that all pools live in one document every subsystem calls. Eight live formulas exist (three invisible to a name-based sweep: a Pool class's static .size, an inline expression in knots.py, and a doc-only Knot formula that contradicts the code). The document must decide the attribute/doubling, the constant (+6/+3/+3/+0/+0), the floor (5/5/1/5/none/none/1), whether History is capped, and whether the mass-battle aggregate belongs at all (different quantity, same word). The formula the document must also name: engine/autoload/sigma_leverage.py:284 rounds the pool to an integer BEFORE the fractional-capable continuous engine sees it, defeating fractional pools at the point of use (ED-IN-0187, ledger-recorded, unapplied).
formula: effective_pool = max(1, int(round(pool)))  # sigma_leverage.py:284 — defeats fractional pools

name: Mass Battle Tree A ruling history — three-deep and self-contradicting
statement: Three rulings on Tree A's fate, none reconciled before the 2026-08-23 re-ruling: 2026-08-03 (J2, Jordan) — canon is Tree B, Tree A "is retired, not kept alongside"; 2026-08-04, one day later — the evacuation keep-set pins massbattle.py as 'keep'; 2026-08-06 — vector audit ED-IN-0148 finds it still present and load-bearing. CURRENT.md recorded J2 as resolved; it was never executed and was contradicted the next day without either surface seeing the other. Root cause: no subsystem row exists for this seam on which "this was ruled and here is what changed" could be recorded (S3).

name: Conviction taxonomy supersession — 13 canonical supersedes legacy 9
statement: npc_behavior_v30.md:30 states outright that the legacy 9-Conviction set (Faith, Order, Reason, Equity, Precedent, Autonomy, Continuity, Community, Warden) is superseded by the canonical 13: Reason and Continuity are deprecated labels, and Autonomy is renamed Liberty. This is a dated, documented, canonical ruling that was never propagated into systems/characters/sim/conviction.py, which still ships the legacy 9 as its runtime validator (conviction.py:44-49) — even while a comment directly above the tuple (:40-43) already asserts the canonical set is the 13 of PP-684.

name: Conviction roster given single owner — fixed on main, 2026-08-24
statement: Between the 2026-08-23 suite and its 2026-08-24 rebase, main gave Convictions one owner: references/descriptor_registry.yaml:conviction_roster -> tools/export_descriptors.py (blocking --check) -> engine/engine_params/descriptors.json -> engine.substrate.descriptors.CONVICTIONS, which conviction.py and npe.py now read instead of retyping. Re-measured: 13 names on both sides, 0 used-but-not-in-roster, 0 in-code-but-unused (was 7 and 3). resolve_conviction now raises on an unknown name instead of silently returning magnitude=0. knots.py now passes 'Honor' instead of 'Loyalty'. An AST sweep (test_conviction_roster_single_owner.py) guards recurrence.

name: Resonant Style Insinuation axis — ratified deliberate substitution, not drift
statement: The social-contest armature's fourth axis is Insinuation, not canon's Solidarity — a substitution ratified by Jordan at Gate C (2026-07-02, ED-1062), with the reason recorded in-file: Solidarity is Knot-gated and relational, and a third-party adjudicator is not Knot-bound to either orator so cannot be moved by it. social_contest_v30.md:174 states the distinction in canon prose. This overturns an earlier sweep's flagship claim that Resonant Style is a "four-way" conflict; it is an OVERLAP with a correctly-named boundary and must not be merged.

name: Settlement ledger tag families — D3 RATIFIED, unpropagated
statement: Ruling D3 (RATIFIED) resolves the settlement ledger's family-vocabulary conflict as "keep the built five (Precedent/Grudge/Debt/Reputation/Leverage); re-express Compact as a Debt subtype." It was never propagated: the design doc still calls Compact "a fifth family", and ledger_add does not validate kind against TAG_KINDS at all, so an unratified "Compact" kind passes through unchecked from the pr119 governance prototype harness.

name: Faction.L IS Mandate — explicit convention, not a defect
statement: Faction.L is Mandate by explicit convention, cited five times across the tree (e.g. parliamentary_bridge.py:72, "Mandate==Faction.L pre-LPS-1"), evaluating to nonzero values at world start (Church 5.0, Crown 5.0, Hafenmark 4.0, Varfell 4.0). An earlier sweep's claim that "Mandate computes to 0 for every faction" was overturned on inspection — it cited the convention as evidence against itself. What genuinely has no implementation is the ratified LPS-1 aggregate (clamp(round(7T/(T+6)))), which remains a counterfactual about unbuilt code.
formula: LPS-1 aggregate (unbuilt): clamp(round(7*T/(T+6)))

name: Scripted hooks and sequences allowed; scripting entire arcs is not
statement: Among fifteen rulings from the 2026-08-18 fieldwork-architecture session, Jordan ruled that scripting narrative hooks and sequences is allowed while scripting entire arcs is not. A later precedent critique (suite-05, proposal 2) identifies this as independently matching the academic remedy for "diffuse causality" (Ryan, on Prom Week): a purely weighted/summed system cannot produce a legible because-clause, but a hooked one can — the sum decides whether, the hook supplies why. Named examples of legitimate hooks: the coup counter, the assassination fuse, the Crown Claim condition table, the Church-Influence theocratic threshold.

name: Church-dominance threshold is one graduated milestone table, not four rivals
statement: An earlier sweep reported the Church-dominance threshold as four conflicting values (40/60/65/100). On inspection this is a single graduated milestone table — 28 start, 40 Church Assertive, 55 Institutional Reach, 65 Church Dominant, 80 Church Ascendant, 100 Theocracy — plus a separate Mass Seizure availability gate at CI >= 60. Four different gates in one system, not four rival values for one gate. Overturned; do not escalate to Jordan.

name: Niflhel dissolution — CANONICAL strike, propagated
statement: The Niflhel strike is real, CANONICAL (2026-04-19), registered in deprecated_terms_registry.yaml, and settlement_layer_v30.md's §4.7/§4.8 are both headed "(Niflhel Dissolution)". An earlier sweep's claim that it survives unstruck in 9 files was overturned: the string matches 136 files (mostly expected historical/registry references), and genuine unreframed organisational residue is narrow.

name: Five competing conviction rosters (13/9/8/7/7)
statement: Five distinct conviction rosters coexist in the tree, as of the 2026-08-23 sweep (fixed on main 2026-08-24, see H1-006): the canonical 13 (conviction_axis_matrix_v30.md, all 46 registry entries); the legacy 9 (conviction_track_v1.md, and conviction.py's live runtime gate before the fix); the legacy 7 (conviction_track_v1.md §3, and names_index.yaml -> definitions.yaml -> lexicon.json -> the dashboard); the NPE 8 (npe.py:80, quoting investigation_systems_v30.md:84 as canon); and the "Seven Convictions" of complete_systems_reference.md:23 (its supersession banner scoped only to combat, so its §1.1 stands as live canon). Union across all five is 21 names; only Faith and Order appear in all five. No registry primitive anywhere can express "these thirteen and no others", which is why the collision was invisible for months (S1 in suite-03 §9).

name: knots.py scars 'Loyalty' — a member of no roster
statement: Prior to the 2026-08-24 conviction-roster fix, the only production write path to apply_conviction_scar — the ED-912 Close-Knot Scar in knots.py:349-353 — passed conviction='Loyalty', a member of neither the coded 9 nor the canonical 13. It returned magnitude=0 silently. The regression test (test_knots_ed912.py:103-116) asserted only the intent flag knots.py sets on itself three lines earlier, never the recorded state, so it passed while the mechanism it existed to verify silently no-oped — a test that cannot observe the failure it excludes (CLAUDE.md §0.1 pt 2). Fixed on main 2026-08-24: knots.py now passes 'Honor' (see H1-059 for the caveat that this substitution is itself an uncited session call).

name: Resonant Style / pressure-point naming — Solidarity vs Loyalty
statement: Beneath the (ratified, non-conflicting — H1-007) Insinuation/Solidarity distinction, a genuine two-name conflict survives on one member: a 2026-07-21 registry addition (names_index.yaml:112-115, ppt.* namespace) re-canonises the name Loyalty for the same slot a 2026-05-08 rename had already fixed to Solidarity, carrying legacy:[] as if nothing had changed. Since descriptor_registry.yaml:177 also retired resonance_style on a premise it then flags as factually false in the same entry (NEEDS-JORDAN, open since 2026-07-07 — see H1-027), three further namings of the same four concepts appeared after that retirement.

name: The prescribed fix for the Authority-pressure-point collision manufactures a new one
statement: references/name_collision_database.yaml:421-425 prescribes renaming "Authority (pressure point)" to Sanction, to resolve its collision with the Authority conviction name. That rename is unusable: faction_layer_v30.md:455-461 is a live five-tier Parliamentary Sanction ladder (Censure / Embargo / Blockade / Combined / Outlawry). The collision database's own prescribed fix collides with an existing live mechanic of the same name.

name: alias_registry transcribes a deprecation map into its own inverse
statement: alias_registry.yaml:648-663 lists Virtue, Faith, Scholastic, Equity and Honor — five of the canonical thirteen convictions — as deprecated legacy labels, in a record whose own note field enumerates all thirteen as canonical four lines below. Mechanism: conviction_taxonomy_v30.md: 274-281 is a two-column map (e.g. "Virtue Ethics -> Virtue", "Divine Command -> Faith"); the registry transcribed the target (right-hand) column into the legacy (left-hand) slot. Targets replaced sources. It is regenerated by vocab_store.py, so --check faithfully republishes the error, and it ships to lexicon.json and the dashboard. Fix site is definitions/vocab_source.yaml, not the generated file.

name: PP-684 mis-superseded Ethical Framework, an orthogonal axis
statement: npc_behavior_system_v1.md:19-23 distinguishes Conviction (what an NPC wants to do) from Ethical Framework (inherited from the NPC's faction — what the NPC is rewarded for doing). PP-684 §6 aliased the Ethical Framework labels into the Conviction taxonomy as if they were the same axis. Collapsed to one axis, every character becomes internally consistent and every institutional-betrayal arc in the roster (a devout person serving a cynical institution) loses its mechanism. character_canon_v30.md D2 has quietly ignored the supersession for 3.5 months, retaining the labels as "descriptive disposition tags" with live Ob modifiers — an unratified but arguably correct instinct.

name: Authority" names both a Conviction and a Resonant Style, same file
statement: Authority" is both a conviction (used by 14 characters) and a resonant style (2 characters) on two different mechanical axes, defined in the same file. Not itself a defect — each definition is individually correct — but a legibility hazard that will bite a reader who assumes a shared name means a shared concept, the specific error class this suite's method section names as costliest.

name: The ratified Territory tier has zero code representation
statement: scale_hierarchy_v1.md (RATIFIED, 2026-07-13) establishes a Territory tier between Settlement and Province, and valoria_political_hierarchy_v30.md:48 correctly deprecates "territory" for the T1-T17 tier in favour of "province" (registry.py:262's province_id=e['territory'] is the correct PP-726 rename, per its own docstring). The sharper, real defect: the Territory dataclass in engine/autoload/game_state.py (keyed T1-T17) actually holds what the ratified model calls Provinces. The ratified model's real Territory tier has zero representation anywhere in code. The collapse is Territory<->Province, not Territory<->Settlement as an earlier sweep framed it.

name: T15/T16 mirror holes in two 16-member territory rosters
statement: world.territories (via create_world, seed=1) and the settlement registry's province references each hold exactly sixteen members, but not the same sixteen. T15 is in the world (owner=None, accord=1.0) but hosts no settlements at all. T16 is not in world.territories but hosts one settlement, S-037 "Schoenland City", owned by "Schoenland" — a faction the world does not contain (the four are Church, Crown, Hafenmark, Varfell). Because the counts match (16=16), no count-based check can see the mismatch; it is a single swapped identifier. Fourteen live sites index world.territories[...] directly and would raise KeyError on the T16 settlement's province id. NPC-012 Rikard's registry entry independently corroborates T16/Schoenland (territory field reads "T16 (Schoenland)"), and two other characters (NPC-001 Edeyja, NPC-075 Orm) live in T15, the province with nothing to interact with.

name: Accord — T9 yields 5, outside ACCORD_MAP's keyspace
statement: Territory.accord (bucketed) and province_accord() diverge at T2/T6/T8/T9, and T9 specifically yields an Accord bucket of 5, outside ACCORD_MAP's legal keyspace of {0,1,2,3,4}. Already filed as B9/OI-37 with a one-line patch (return min(4, ...)) and instrumented by a live probe; D4 already picked the winner among the four competing Accord range definitions.

name: 43% of settlements have no type represented in canon's type tables
statement: Type histogram across 37 loaded settlements: Town 15, Village 14, Seat 2, Fortress 2, City 2, Fortress-City 1, Cathedral-City 1. Village (the most common type), Fortress-City and Cathedral-City are absent from the design doc's type tables that assign facility slots, Local Actor counts and radiation modifiers. Port, Cathedral, Mine and Outpost have zero instances on the map at all, while the Calamity table keys its "frontier falls first" rule to Outpost, naming three settlements that are actually a Village and two Towns. Already filed as E6 with a fix authored and cross-confirmed by a baseline audit and a 500-seed run.

name: Mandate-Weight formula has no defined value for the two highest-value non-capitals
statement: settlement_layer_v30.md:160 defines base(Type), the Weight term of the ratified Mandate formula, including Village while citing two tables that lack it, and omitting Fortress-City and Cathedral-City entirely. S-014 Ehrenfeld and S-036 Himmelenger — the two highest-value non-capital settlements — therefore have no defined Weight in the ratified Mandate formula: an arithmetic hole in a live formula, not a taxonomy tidiness issue.

name: Settlement ledger tag-family vocabulary — five rival lists, union 11, intersection 4
statement: Five surfaces enumerate the settlement memory-ledger's tag families with different memberships: code (5: Precedent/Grudge/Debt/Reputation/Leverage), the Goldenfurt slice, design doc §1.6, §9, and the grounded event-card deck. Union across all five is 11 distinct names; intersection is 4. Leverage appears in code and in Goldenfurt but in neither design doc that enumerates the set. Ruled by D3 (see H1-008) but unpropagated.

name: da.* Domain Action emitter registry is stale — code emits what the registry says nothing does
statement: references/module_contracts.yaml:814-817 states the da.* Domain Action family has "ZERO emitter code". systems/factions/sim/parliamentary_transfer.py:230 emits da.public_governance on every parliamentary territory transfer, a live-every-season path. The registry note is stale, not a design conflict — a doc-vs-code case where the code is correct and the contract file needs updating (per CLAUDE.md §0.05, code is the mechanism).

name: resonance_style retired on a premise its own entry calls factually false
statement: descriptor_registry.yaml:177 retires resonance_style as "never canonically enumerated" and then corrects itself in the same entry: "the premise is factually FALSE — npc_behavior_v30.md §1.3's Resonant Style Taxonomy is CANONICAL... NEEDS-JORDAN" — flagged 2026-07-07, still open as of the 2026-08-23 sweep. Eighteen NPCs and a UI enum carry resonant_style values despite the registry entry declaring the concept does not exist.

name: Twenty distinct authored faction strings map to no code faction
statement: Twenty distinct faction strings appear across the 46 npc_registry.yaml characters. Four match a faction STARTING_STATS knows (Church 6, Crown 3, Varfell 2, Hafenmark 1 — twelve characters). The other sixteen strings, on thirty-four characters, have no counterpart: Restoration Movement (4), Loewenritter (4), Guilds (4), Altonia (3), Crown (Royal Family) (3), Crown (Inner Circle) (3), Independent (Southernmost Wardens) (2), and others. Most read as intentional sub-organisation texture, but there is no sub-faction primitive, so e.g. Crown, Crown (Ministry), Crown (Royal Family) and Crown (Inner Circle) are four unrelated strings to any consumer. Two records also encode a dual-loyalty/liaison relationship inside the name field, which no reader can decompose.

name: Unquoted YAML comment truncates two npc_registry faction fields on every parse
statement: NPC-081 and NPC-082 write faction: Hafenmark (Inner Council #4) and faction: Varfell (Jarl Council #5). Unquoted YAML treats " #" as an inline comment start, so both parse silently truncated with unbalanced parens: 'Hafenmark (Inner Council' and 'Varfell (Jarl Council'. The file reads correctly to a human; the parser disagrees and says nothing. Same defect class as ED-IN-0121 and survives for the same reason: zero Python loaders read this file in production, so nothing checks it.

name: npc_registry.yaml schema block omits six fields in live use
statement: The registry's own opening schema block declares required/optional fields that describe only 16 of 22 top-level fields actually used. Six fields in live use are declared nowhere: source (on all 46), resonant_style (18), cultural_label (17 top-level), certainty (8), title (7), self_other_initial (2). The narrative-texture fields — the ones that make a character sound like somebody — are precisely the undeclared ones.

name: cultural_label and self_other_initial stored at two nesting depths, zero overlap
statement: cultural_label appears top-level on 17 entries and nested under convictions on 26, with zero records carrying it in both places; self_other_initial splits 2 top-level / 26 nested, likewise zero overlap. A reader of either single path silently sees 40% or 60% of the data with no error. The value vocabulary is partitioned by depth too — einhir_traditional and altonian_imperial appear only top-level; ecclesiastical, varfell_alpine and altonian appear only nested — and altonian / altonian_imperial are an unnormalised near-duplicate pair. Union across both depths gives good coverage (43 of 46), which is exactly why the split matters: the content exists, the shape hides it.

name: ConvictionState has no field for a conviction's authored weight
statement: The registry carries weighted identity convictions (e.g. {conviction: Warden, weight: 0.4}, 81 weighted primaries across the file). systems/characters/sim/conviction.py's ConvictionState (:108-123) stores scars, resonant_active, in_crisis, pending_belief_revisions, last_scar_season, log — and no baseline weight field anywhere in the coded conviction model. Even with the taxonomy ruling settled, a weighted profile authored in the registry has nowhere to land at runtime.

name: npc_registry entry and runtime NPC dataclass share only two fields
statement: The registry's field set does not fit the NPC dataclass (systems/world/sim/npe.py:114-134) field by field. first_name, role, goals, arc_trajectory, resonant_style, birthplace, ts, coherence, stats{cognition,focus,endurance,social}, cultural_label, self_other_initial, title, notes have no NPC field; NPC's stance, worldview, compromise_category, volatility, deviation_roll have no registry source. Exactly two fields map directly — faction and territory — and both are also the two fields with the worst data quality (20 unmapped faction strings, 7-of-46 territory coverage with a format mismatch). This is why the "single missing artifact is a loader" framing is wrong: the destination type does not exist yet.

name: Settlement.npc_ids has no writer; get_npcs_in_territory has no callers
statement: Settlement.npc_ids (registry.py:87) has no writer anywhere in engine/ or systems/ except from_dict and a non-production test-harness fixture (goldenfurt_fixture.py:89). npe.py::get_npcs_in_territory (:375-377) has zero callers of any kind. Both ends are CODED-BUT-UNREACHED, blocked entirely on the person-layer loader (H1-045): there is no place a settlement-scoped writer could pull NPCs from, and a per-territory registry field does not resolve which settlement within a multi-settlement territory an NPC belongs to (a distinct unmade decision).

name: The Treaty system is wholly inert and could not work correctly if wired
statement: An AST sweep for process_treaty_expirations, register_treaty and get_active_treaties across every live .py returns zero callers anywhere, including tests. A defect waits inside it regardless: treaty.py:137-138 does "roll = rng.random() if rng else 0.95  # default to high-lapse if no rng; lapsed = roll < lapse_rate", but canonical lapse rates are 0.90-0.95, so with no rng the roll is fixed at 0.95 and "0.95 < 0.90..0.95" is always False — no treaty can ever lapse via that path, and the comment states the exact opposite of what the code does. Separately, register_treaty keys the store by tuple(sorted(parties)) while game_state.py:190 documents and rebuilds the World's treaty store as frozenset-keyed — a save/restore key-type asymmetry. crown_initiative.py (317 lines) contains no treaty-formation code at all; its one mention is a precondition check in a docstring.

name: Settlement memory ledger has zero production callers, and validates nothing
statement: systems/settlements/sim/ledger.py (75 lines) implements Precedent/Grudge/Debt/Reputation/Leverage tags, deduped and TTL'd, deliberately living on the settlement rather than the governor so they survive succession ("the player->world persistence guarantee", per the file's own docstring). An AST sweep finds ledger_add/ledger_has/ledger_get/ledger_sweep each called exactly once, all from Settlement.add_tag/.has_tag/.tags/registry.py:207 — and those wrapper methods are called by NOTHING anywhere, including tests. The only writers of any kind are the non-production tools/sim_harness/adapters/pr119_governance/ prototype cluster, which writes an unratified "Compact" kind through ledger_add unchecked, because ledger_add never validates kind against TAG_KINDS at :47-58. No settlement has ever recorded a precedent, grudge, debt, reputation or leverage hook, because nothing can.

name: The seasonal Mandate penalty is coded as permanent, and its own note says temporary
statement: systems/social_contest/sim/parliamentary_vote.py:207-219: on a §10 Total Victory or Total Defeat, the losing coalition's dominant faction takes Mandate -1 via a direct adjust("L", ...) world write, with the note "[one-season penalty; temporary-modifier restoration deferred to season_manager]". engine/autoload/season_manager.py defines exactly two functions (advance_season, check_arc_boundary); Faction.reset_seasonal (game_state.py:134-136) clears exactly two booleans. There is no temporary-modifier machinery anywhere in the engine. The penalty is therefore permanent and compounds across the campaign — confirmed live (ECHO_TRANSPORT default ON) in the 2026-08-22 session-master-log's coverage-closing pass, not merely a docstring claim.

name: mass_seizure writes a canonical Accord index into a continuous field
statement: mass_seizure.py:293 writes t.accord = float(starting_accord) — a canonical 0-4 index — directly into Territory.accord, a continuous field on the ACCORD_MAP scale ({0:1.0, 1:2.5, 2:4.0, 3:5.5, 4:7.0}). The sibling site does it correctly: parliamentary_transfer.py:278 is terr.accord = ACCORD_MAP[accord_level]. A seizure intended at Accord level 2 stores 2.0 where canon means 4.0, and reads back through canonical_accord() as the wrong bucket. game_state.py:65-70 warns in its own words that modules "MUST bucket through these helpers". The site's own comment half-admits it: "Convert int accord to ACCORD_MAP-style continuous if needed; for now, set directly." mass_seizure has zero test coverage of any kind, unlike its six sibling stubs in the same package. This is a live wrong-scale write bug, not merely a missing call site.

name: ED-874's Domain Action resolver is ratified and has zero implementations
statement: ED-874's text says it "supersedes the bare-stat-pool-vs-Ob dice approach" for Domain Actions. It has zero implementations: every faction action still uses the superseded method. Two sharpenings — tools/validate_ed_citations.py names ED-874 as NONEXISTENT and uses it as its own fixture for a bad citation, and its only home on main is the byte-faithful capture of the evacuated engine/params/ tree, which CLAUDE.md §5/§0.05 rules is history, not canon: where prose disagrees with code, the code wins. So "implement ED-874" is not obviously the remedy; the ruling itself needs re-examination under §0.05.

name: The Suppress domain-action step can never fire in any campaign season
statement: apply_seasonal_ci(world) is called with no kwargs, and Suppress's gate is "if suppress_attempted and suppress_success:" — both always false-default, so Step 4 Suppress cannot fire in any campaign season with the current caller. This makes the standing two-doc Suppress-obstacle conflict (Ob = Mandate vs floor(Mandate/2)+1, diverging up to 3 points) moot until a caller is wired — a genuine Jordan ruling is still needed once it is (see H1-049).

name: Governor succession — three layers deep, nothing emits it
statement: state.succession is named in articulation.py:119's consumer roster and nowhere emitted; the only occurrences are that consumer roster and a test. key_graph.json names its producer as faction_politics, which exists only as a design doc. Below that: Faction carries no leader field of any kind, so the Key's required payload (prior_leader_id, new_leader_id) has no coded source at all. The gap is not a missing emitter — it is a missing entity, three layers deep: no leader field, no succession event, no Key.

name: Faction.adjust bypasses the Key bus on 30 of 31 call sites
statement: Thirty of thirty-one Faction.adjust call sites write faction stats directly, bypassing the Key bus entirely, even though the tree has already ruled the governing principle: "a request for a computed answer stays a call; an announcement that something HAPPENED is a Key" — and the live precedent for the shape already exists at echo_transport.py:454-457. The pre-identified first migration: faction_action.py:485-489 says the loser-Legitimacy write "belongs to faction_state reacting to this emission" and should attach as apply= on the already-firing scene.battle_concluded Key. This is a read/write-asymmetry hazard under CLAUDE.md §0.1 pt 1 (write timing moves to the accounting boundary) and should extend the existing .adjust( census in test_faction_l_reconstruction.py:140 into a shrink-only ratchet rather than mint a new guard.

name: Authored per-settlement Legitimacy/Popular-Support seed table has no loader
statement: faction_state_authoring_v30.md §8:323-338 authors per-settlement starting L/PS seeds (Crown 5/5, Church 5/5, Hafenmark 4/4, Varfell 4/4, Guilds 3/3, Restoration Movement 0/0, Loewenritter 0/0), stating they "seed each controlled settlement's L/PS at game start." populate_from_geography reads only the geography YAML, which carries no L/PS keys, so all 37 settlements load at 0/0. This inverts the apparent remedy: the defect is not "L/PS is unauthored", it is that an authored canonical table has no loader — a roughly ten-line fix, not a design item. The table's provenance chain points at the evacuated engine/params/ tree.

name: Schoenland (T16/S-037) is authored, adjacency-linked, and absent from the playable world
statement: S-037 "Schoenland City" (province T16, owner_faction "Schoenland") is coherently attested across three surfaces — the settlement registry, an adjacency edge ({from: T1, to: T16, type: coastal}), and NPC-012 Rikard's registry entry (territory "T16 (Schoenland)", faction "Independent (Schoenland)") — and is absent from world.territories, STARTING_OWNER, and the four known factions. game_state.py carries two territory sets eight lines apart, ALL_PLAYABLE_15 (15 entries) and STARTING_OWNER (16), neither of which includes T16. This is a region authored across the content layer and never added to the geography layer, not a typo in one file. See H1-021 for the T15 mirror side of the same defect.

name: The NPC-registry loader is blocked on five unmade decisions, not one missing function
statement: Loading references/npc_registry.yaml against the live engine is blocked on five decisions, not absence of a loader function: (1) only 7 of 46 entries carry a territory, and world.npcs is territory-keyed, so 39 authored people cannot be placed; (2) the 7 that do are formatted "T15 (Southernmost)" against the live map's bare 'T1'..'T15','T17' keys, and one names T16, which is not in the map at all; (3) 20 distinct faction strings for four parliamentary factions have no mapping to STARTING_STATS (see H1-028); (4) ConvictionState has no weight field for the registry's 81 weighted primaries (see H1-032); (5) the registry's field set does not correspond to the NPC dataclass field-by-field, with only faction and territory mapping directly (see H1-033). The model loader itself (registry.py::populate_from_geography) already exists as an in-tree pattern to copy (deterministic, no RNG draw, every field-mapping cited, illegal values raised). This corpus's population/loader question is Design Gap 1 / Question Q1 ("what is a character at runtime") and is also the subject of the personnel-muster baseline's Phase P0 plan (see baseline_ref) — this record adds the specific blocking decisions the baseline plan's proposal options do not enumerate.

name: NPC settlement membership is ambiguous — per-settlement field, per-territory registry data
statement: Settlement.npc_ids is a per-settlement field, but the registry's only locational field (territory) is per-territory, and several territories host multiple settlements (1-3, mean 2.3 per province). Even once a person is placed at a territory, which settlement within it holds them is an unmade decision — distinct from, and downstream of, the loader gap itself (H1-045).

name: religious_building stored twice, in two keyspaces, never synced
statement: religious_building is stored on the settlement (registry.py:82, keyed by sid) and separately on the territory (infrastructure.py:81, keyed by territory id), never synced. Adjudicated as narrower than it first looked: canon says the field belongs on the settlement, and the Goldenfurt Chapel gate that depends on it lives in the zero-caller prototype cluster and is fed by its own fixture (where it does fire) — production never reads the field either way. An inert field, not a broken narrative arc.
status_evidence: proposals/2026-08-23-suite-03-competing-vocabularies.md (not enumerated as a live V-item; carried at MASTER L9 grade)

name: temperaments.py read/write asymmetry on the drift store
statement: systems/settlements/sim/temperaments.py reads via _drift_store() (no world argument) at :117 but writes via _drift_store(world) at :153-158 — a getter/setter pair reading and writing through different code paths, the exact read/write-asymmetry hazard CLAUDE.md §0.1 point 1 names as the highest-priority thing to grep for before trusting a "change" claim.

name: Suppress obstacle formula — two ratified surfaces disagree, and only Jordan can pick
statement: conviction_track_v30.md:204 (Church Mandate framing) and faction_layer_v30.md:699 (floor(Mandate/2)+1) give two ratified, disagreeing formulas for the Suppress obstacle, diverging up to 3 points. Currently moot in practice because the Suppress caller passes no kwargs and can never fire (H1-040), but the conflict itself is real and unresolved code-vs-doc-vs-doc, and is explicitly named as needing Jordan (not resolvable by §0.05, since the code implements neither value).
formula: Ob = Mandate  |  Ob = floor(Mandate/2) + 1

name: Seven of thirteen canonical convictions were silent no-ops in the pre-fix runtime gate
statement: Prior to the 2026-08-24 single-owner fix (H1-006), conviction.py:191-193 returned magnitude=0 for any name outside its coded 9-tuple, with no exception or warning. Seven authored conviction names were therefore unscarrable: Authority (14 characters — the single most-used conviction in the entire cast), Utility (9), Liberty (6), Honor (5), Scholastic (3), Virtue (2), Identity (2). Seventeen of 46 characters had an unscarrable primary conviction, and twelve — Sigrid, Halvar, Gerik, Dalla, Alexios, Almud, Kolbrun, Vidar, Njal, Nessa, Joren, Zoe — could not be scarred on any conviction they carried at all, making the entire conviction-scarring mechanic silently inert for them. Named as Tier-0 next action #1 in HANDOFF_IN.md prior to the fix.

name: Goldenfurt's authored settlement numbers are not loadable — its own demonstration vise runs wrong
statement: The Goldenfurt slice's spec authors facility_tier=1, religious_building="Chapel", subnational={Guild,Church,RM,Niflhel} for settlement S-006. The production loader reads only the geography YAML, which carries none of these, so the loaded S-006 has facility_tier=0, ap=2, religious_building='None', subnational={}. The slice's own demonstration point — "3 AP cannot serve all three [factions]" — runs at 2 AP instead of 3, off by a third before a card is even drawn, and its Chapel-gated Geneva-trap arc cannot fire at all.

name: succeed_governor is coded-but-unreached, and circularly blocked
statement: No succession or appointment event exists in the season loop; nothing writes Settlement.governor_id outside succeed_governor itself and from_dict. The mechanism is circularly blocked on the person layer (H1-045): no NPC exists to hold the office, so there is no candidate to appoint. The non-production harness uses bare placeholder strings like "podesta-appointee" in place of a real actor. (Already documented at the general level in the personnel-muster baseline's governor/officer terminology work; this record is the specific reachability/circularity finding from this lane's proposals.)

name: The strategic-to-cell Unit adapter for mass battle has no canonical spec
statement: Tree A's _faction_to_unit builds Units from faction.Mil using minimum-viable defaults, and its own docstring says so: "[GAP: faction->unit construction has no canonical spec]". The measured incompatibility (reproduced, not merely read): feeding a Unit built by Tree A's adapter to Tree B's run_battle raises AttributeError: 'Subunit' object has no attribute 'cells_float' — Tree B is cell-based, Tree A's adapter is not. This is Ruling A's actual blocker (H1-001) and is independently named by suite-07 as the sole remaining open question on mass battle after main's engine port landed (Q2: "what is a strategic army, in cells?").

name: Mass Battle Tree A lacks the fractional pool, the sigma head, and PP-241 Reform
statement: Tree A (the live, campaign-run mass-battle engine prior to Ruling A's execution) lacks the sigma head, the fractional pool, and PP-241 Reform (reform_check is an empty pass). ED-MB-0032's ruling that the mass-battle pool must be fractional is implemented only in Tree B. 40 of 51 mass-battle tests already target Tree B, so the test suite has been ready for the migration longer than the code. This resolves by deletion once Ruling A (H1-001) executes, per the corpus's own framing.

name: Knot Pool formula ratified with a +3/min-5 term; code implements neither
statement: systems/fieldwork/knots_v30.md:37 (PP-632, ED-FI-0005) ratifies the Knot Pool as (Spirit x 2) + History(Relevant) + 3, minimum 5. systems/fieldwork/sim/knots.py:216 computes (spirit*2) + history_rel — no +3, no floor of 5. The design doc contradicts itself internally: :76 gives the un-augmented form the sim actually cites (knots.py:57). The test guarding this, test_knot_pool_formula.py, states "there is no sim/ oracle that computes the Knot Pool, so this is a doc-content guard" — a false premise, since the sim clearly does compute it — so the test pins three prose surfaces and stays green while the game plays the un-ratified variant. Under CLAUDE.md §0.05 the code is currently the formula, meaning the game plays the :76 variant by default, which nobody decided.
formula: ratified: (Spirit x 2) + History(Relevant) + 3, min 5   |  coded: (spirit*2) + history_rel, no floor

name: Close-Knot-break Scar applies to one actor; canon specifies both partners
statement: systems/fieldwork/knots_v30.md:189 says the Close-Knot-break Scar goes "+1 to both partners". apply_knot_loss (systems/fieldwork/sim/knots.py:317,361) scars only the single actor argument passed to it. The same gap covers the paired Composure penalty at knots_v30.md:186. Canon-vs-code per CLAUDE.md §0.05: decide, then change the code to apply to both knot.actor_a and knot.actor_b.

name: A fabricated conviction alias table was shipped as centralization, contradicting two authored surfaces
statement: A prior session shipped CONVICTION_ALIASES = {'Reason': 'Scholastic', 'Autonomy': 'Liberty'}, justified in a comment as "a rename rather than a design call." Two authored surfaces refuse that exact mapping: conviction_taxonomy_v30.md:282 marks Reason a "composite — see PP-685 per character" (not a 1:1 rename to Scholastic), and alias_registry.yaml:658-663 lists Reason as legacy with no canonical target and "Per-character migration in PP-685"; Autonomy appears in neither surface at all. The alias decided a ruling by accident. It was deleted on discovery. Recorded as a worked example of the lesson: when two authored surfaces decline to state a mapping, that silence IS the ruling (not-decided), and implementing the obvious-looking value ships an unreviewed design call as canon.

name: npe.py's conviction-opposites table minted six non-canonical names
statement: systems/world/sim/npe.py carried opposites = {"Faith": "Reason", "Order": "Survival", "Justice": "Power", "Loyalty": "Truth"} plus inverses — six of eight names non-canonical against the (now single-owned) 13-conviction roster. Once CONVICTIONS became canonical, this table could mint names resolve_conviction raises on. The pairs were not salvageable by renaming — Justice<->Power is an opposition no taxonomy in the corpus states. Replaced with a uniform draw over the other twelve convictions; the ratified remedy is to cook the 13x4 conviction-axis matrix into an artifact (registered as map.conviction_axis in descriptor_registry.yaml:258) as the grounded answer to "what is the opposite of Conviction X", which is currently cooked nowhere.

name: knots.py's 'Honor' Scar substitution is an uncited session design call, not a canon transcription
statement: Following the conviction-roster fix, knots.py now scars conviction='Honor' for the ED-912 §6.1 Close-Knot Scar. Defensible on Honor's gloss ("pledged oath... binding"; taxonomy §8 D1 ratifies Honor for pledged-bond material), but canon names no specific Conviction for ED-912 §6.1 — this is a session call, not a transcription of an existing ruling, and it was not marked as one at the time it shipped. Recommended remedy (not itself extracted as a ruling, since none exists yet): add a ledger row recording the choice, or route it to Jordan.

name: The needs_jordan queue is current, not stale — 96 of 110 flagged items are July or August
statement: Measured directly from registers/editorial_ledger*.jsonl on 2026-08-23: 254 genuinely open items, 110 flagged needs_jordan. By age: pre-July 78 open / 14 needs_jordan; July 135/70; August 35/26; undated 6/0. The instinct that a large queue is mostly stale and that dropping pre-July items would clear most of it is wrong: dropping pre-July removes only 14 of 110. The Infrastructure and Settlements lanes together are half the Jordan queue (IN 30, SE 23, of 110 total by lane). Superseded in exact figure by suite-07 (main's own later triage put the effective count at 154 rows, 31 genuine Jordan decisions), but the shape finding — current, not stale — is independently confirmed by both measurements.

name: Settlement adjacency graph missing T16 key
statement: systems/settlements/sim/adjacency.py defines 16 keys (T1..T15, T17) but T16 is referenced only as a value inside T1's neighbor set, never as its own key. T16 is Schoenland, the island republic named in valoria_geography_v30.yaml with an explicit coastal edge to T1, so any neighbor walk through T16 raises KeyError or dead-ends. Every other edge in the graph is symmetric, making this the sole asymmetric omission rather than a modelling choice; the correct edge already exists in the geography file.

name: Standing homonym — ratified range plus unexecuted scope-tag, across three mechanisms
statement: registers/editorial_ledger_sc.jsonl:15 (ED-SC-0014, 2026-07-08) ratifies BOTH that the BG faction track's Standing range is 0-10 per references/glossary.md:138 (correcting clock_registry_v30.md's stated 0-5), AND that the cross-scale "Standing" homonym must be scope-tagged apart from the contest kernel's separate 0-10 ethos float. Neither is executed: Faction.standing (engine/autoload/game_state.py:129) remains an unbounded, unclamped int; clock_registry_v30.md:53 still states the pre-ruling 0-5; name_collision_database.yaml:142 still carries the pre-ruling exempt marker instead of a fourth entry. A third, wholly separate mechanism — the officer rank ladder Standing 0-7 in faction_politics_v30.md — is prose only and is NOT addressed by this ruling; treating it as unified with the ratified range is the vocabulary-collision error this corpus's own first two passes committed against itself before opening the ledger row directly.

name: Faction.standing — unbounded int outside the descriptor system, feeding the pool that writes it
statement: Faction.standing is an int=0 with no floor or ceiling (engine/autoload/game_state.py:129), written by bare += / -= at ten sites across crown_initiative.py, absolution.py and parliamentary_transfer.py, and read directly into two dice-pool-size expressions whose own outcomes write standing back — two closed positive-feedback loops with no damper. It is not one of the six ratified faction descriptors (descriptors.FACTION_STATS) and has no row in MULTS, so it cannot route through Faction.adjust() (which would KeyError) and every write bypasses the registry-clamped path the other six stats use.
formula: pool = int(crown.I) + crown.standing

name: hidden_allegiance computed and dropped at the NPC constructor
statement: systems/world/sim/npe.py:327 computes hidden_allegiance = rng.choice(other) as one of five NPC deviation-roll outcomes, but the NPC(...) constructor at :336-347 omits it from its keyword arguments, so the field silently stays None despite existing on the dataclass and round-tripping through to_dict/from_dict. This is the only mechanism in the executable tree that would model an agent whose interest diverges from its own faction, and it is severed at the point of construction — a dropped write, not a missing caller — consuming an RNG draw on roughly 6.7% of all generated NPCs for no effect.

name: The empty world is a guarded disposition, and the guards observe the wrong variable
statement: Three guards hold world.npcs empty as a considered disposition rather than pending work: engine/tests/test_pipeline_reach.py:625 xfail(strict=True) under a header stating population is "PERMANENT deferral until canon specifies a trigger"; engine/tests/test_f7_smoke_oracle.py:335 asserting npcs==0; and engine/tests/test_world_population.py:152, whose docstring couples any wire-up to updating both others. All three actually pin generate_npc's call counter (world.npc_counter, incremented only inside generate_npc) rather than world.npcs itself, so none can observe a loader that constructs NPC objects directly. The stated blocker — "no canon head names a world-gen initial count" — is answerable from references/npc_registry.yaml's 35 status:canonical records, each carrying a source field.

name: Registry-loader golden-safety refuted by controlled experiment
statement: Loading two NPC objects directly into world.npcs at world-gen (bypassing generate_npc) left both population guards green at npcs_generated=0 but moved seed-42's campaign winner from Crown to Hafenmark; a control arm with npe.simulate_npc_actions neutered reproduced the unmodified baseline byte-exact, isolating the channel to simulate_npc_actions drawing world.rng (the shared campaign stream) at systems/overview/sim/accounting.py:139 every season regardless of store size. This refutes the prior claim — drawn by analogy from populate_from_geography's docstring — that any authored-data loader is "golden-safe by construction": that manoeuvre is safe only for state with no per-season RNG-drawing consumer, which settlements have and world.npcs does not.

name: references/npc_registry.yaml — unquoted characters break YAML parsing on two records
statement: references/npc_registry.yaml:835 and :850 write "faction: Hafenmark (Inner Council #4)" and "faction: Varfell (Jarl Council #5)" unquoted; YAML parses "#4)"/"#5)" as a comment, silently truncating both values into singleton namespaces sharing no other record, while four other records use the correctly quoted full strings. The same file was separately unparseable for its whole prior git history from an unrelated unquoted colon in NPC-034 Gustav's faction field — the corpus's one authored instance of intra-faction divergence. Must be fixed before any loader reads the file, or the affected officeholders join factions that do not exist.

name: Geography's provinces: block has no production reader
statement: The VSG generation seed step is specified to read per-province frames (anchor, polygon, fort_level, spiritual_weight, proximity_calamity, starting_pros, faction, region/sub) from valoria_geography_v30.yaml's provinces: block, but populate_from_geography (systems/settlements/sim/registry.py:216-241) reads only the settlements: map — grep for a provinces reader across engine/ and systems/ returns two hits, both comments. The data VSG's seed step conditions on is dead at runtime.

name: Settlement.pressure (Π) — declared, zero writers; the 298/300 runaway is a retired lesson, not a live bug
statement: Settlement.pressure: float = 4.0 (systems/settlements/sim/registry.py:79) has exactly two non-declaration references tree-wide, neither a write; the only other ".pressure" in the tree (social_contest/sim/contest/resolver.py:241) is an unrelated venue field — a separate vocabulary collision. No homeostat code exists anywhere on main (the implementation that once ran it was retired to FORK:1e4c6f4), so the frequently-cited "298/300 settlements pinned at the pressure ceiling" result is a validated lesson about a retired formula, not a present-tense defect — presenting it as live would itself be fabrication.
formula: restore_toward(3) := sign(3-Pi)*min(1,|3-Pi|); Pi_next = clamp(Pi + sum(unserved_needs) + 0.5*sum(active_grudges) + 0.5*sum(ambitions_in_motion) + external_shock - sum(player_releases) + restore_toward(3), 0, 10)
status_evidence: systems/settlements/sim/registry.py:79 (declared, unwritten); formula retired to FORK:1e4c6f4

name: The Π homeostat's boundary bifurcation, resolved as arithmetic
statement: Running the declared Π formula as pure arithmetic (no kernel needed), 50 seasons, Pi0=4.0, target 3, clamp [0,10], zero noise: any per-season accrual <= 1.00 reaches a stable equilibrium at 3+accrual; any accrual > 1.00 pins the ceiling in roughly (10-Pi0)/(accrual-1) seasons (1.50 pins in 12 seasons, 2.00 in 6). The bifurcation is structural — min(1,...) saturates the restoring term at +-1, so net drift is accrual-1 for any accrual>1 — and the design's own six ambition-clock NPCs contribute up to +3.0/season before any unserved need or grudge, meaning accrual>1 is the design's default regime, not an edge case.
formula: bifurcation at accrual = 1.0 exactly; pin_seasons ~= (10 - Pi0) / (accrual - 1) for accrual > 1
status_evidence: (arithmetic derivation on the formula recorded at H2-009; no kernel required)

name: E1 (Π homeostat) may not ship without E3 (capped accrual) and E7 (release path) landing in the same commit
statement: systems/_architecture/ners_vsg_reconciliation_v1.md:48-50 rules E1 cannot ship without E3 and E7 in the same commit. Proportional restoration alone (restore = -k(Pi-3)) does not rescue this: equilibrium is Pi* = 3 + accrual/k, stable only for k<2, and at the design's own accrual (~3.0/ season from six ambition clocks) holding Pi out of the crisis band needs k>=1 — a controller erasing the full displacement every season, trading the R failure for an E failure (the meter stops behaving like a meter). Accrual must be capped (E3) and a genuine release path (E7) must exist before proportional restoration can work at all.
status_evidence: (no homeostat code exists on main; see H2-009)

name: Exactly one of fifteen VSG weight-table paradigms is authored
statement: Of the fifteen conditioned-slice paradigms VSG specifies (P1 Location through P15 Verify), only P4's Type weight table is written out as an actual formula. The other fourteen, including P13 Actor roster and P12 Temperament, have no authored weight table anywhere in the corpus — the largest distance between VSG-as-written and VSG-as-code, larger than the missing sampler kernel itself.
formula: weight(Type|P1,P3) = base_prior(Type,size=P3) + 3*[fort_level>=3] + 3*[spiritual_weight>=2 and church_adjacent] + 2*[breadbasket_flag] + 2*[port_geometry] + 2*[capital_region and starting_pros>=5] + 2*[mineral_flag] + 1*[frontier and low_pros], sampled at temperature tau
status_evidence: (no sampler exists; zero random.choices/np.random.choice/weighted_sample hits in engine/ or systems/)

name: settlement_generator_v1.md's spiritual_weight range contradicts its own geography data
statement: settlement_generator_v1.md:45 declares P1's spiritual_weight as range 0-2, but the live valoria_geography_v30.yaml data has T9=4 and T15=5 (Himmelenger, the Cathedral City), agreeing with generation_sourcebook_v1.md:82,86. A sampler written from the doc's stated range would clamp Himmelenger to 2, destroying the exact conditioning meant to draw a Cathedral there.

name: The temperament slice (alpha/beta) executes when called, but has zero production callers
statement: systems/settlements/sim/temperaments.py:33-38 carries a live five-typology alpha/beta vector including Goldenfurt's authored draw (traditional: alpha=0.3, beta=0.7) and a runtime strain-driven drift function (:124-131), directly executed and producing alpha=0.48/beta=0.52 after strain_delta=3. Grep across every .py for temperament_of, apply_strain_shock, or an import of the module returns one hit, a comment — zero production callers and zero tests. Its drift is one-directional (if drift > 0 only), a restoration-free accumulator.
formula: drift = clamp(drift + 0.1 * strain_delta, -1, +1), applied only if drift > 0

name: generate_npc's two-tier archetype/deviation generator — built, zero production callers
statement: systems/world/sim/npe.py:226-330 is condition-then-noise: Tier 1 seeds an NPC's five axes from territory ecology weights (60% bias toward the controlling faction via FACTION_DEFAULT_WEIGHT_PCT), Tier 2 rolls a deviation. _ecology_weights (:186-208) returns binary flags rather than continuous weights, and every categorical axis (convictions, compromise, the deviation flip) falls back to a uniform draw — the module's own comment at the deviation flip states a grounded 13x4 conviction-axis matrix exists as prose but "is not cooked into any artifact code reads," so a uniform draw is the honest interim. No production call site.

name: Uncapped tag_modifiers in the VSG event-deck weighting — unbounded positive feedback on the sampler
statement: The runtime event-deck card weight formula is base + pressure_scaling(family, Pi) + tag_modifiers (sim_build_spec.md:124): a card's outcome writes ledger tags, and tags re-weight future card draws, with no cap on tag_modifiers named anywhere. Same accrual-without-restoration class as the Pi homeostat, one level up — on the sampler's weight vector rather than on settlement state directly.

name: Officer object minimum spec, and why the personal↔mass-battle seam has no worked precedent
statement: The corpus's own clearest statement distinguishes six skill roles from four position roles: attributes alone cannot distinguish them — they are distinguished by practice, instruments and OFFICE (General and an army, Politician and a seat, Governor and a settlement, Leader and a faction). The minimum officer record needs a typed seat (small enum, not free text), a nullable holder (vacancy is a state, not an absence), a rank on that seat's ladder, a patron edge, and an advance predicate reading live state; power_base and patron_id return zero .py hits anywhere on main. Separately: no surveyed precedent demonstrates a personal contribution provably leverage-in-band from N=1 to N=1000+ (every mechanism found is scale-blind or fully fused into the mass sim), so an officer bridging personal combat and mass battle is attempting something with no worked precedent, and any proposal for it should say so rather than presenting the seam as an imported, solved pattern.
status_evidence: (no officer object exists in executing code; nearest is Settlement.governor_id: str|None)

name: 74 authored ladder rungs, each with an entry gate and a demotion cell — zero executing in either direction
statement: faction_politics_v30.md's ten ladder tables total 74 rungs (independently recounted, reproducing exactly), every one carrying both a promotion gate and a demotion cell. At least 15 cross-cutting downward mechanisms sit above the rungs (Demotion Magnitude, a two-season appeal window with no appeal for Dismissal, the Riskbreaker Deniability-Debt cascade, Conviction Reformation failure, Baralta cascades, failed leadership challenges, a battle-fate table). None of the 74 rungs, in either direction, executes; the only near-miss is contest/faction.py::succession, exercised only by its own kernel tests, unreachable because Faction has no leader field.
status_evidence: (zero code hits for standing_change, officer_deaths, power_base, patron_id)

name: Parliamentary Censure — the one executing demotion pipeline, aimed one scale above where an officer ladder needs it
statement: Parliamentary Censure (faction_action.py:276-301 dispatching to parliamentary_action.py:97-160) is the only executing demotion in the game: an agent proposes it (self-gated on GD-3 plus proposer Mandate >= 2), a body adjudicates it via a real ballot, and its pass effect applies Sta -1 / L -1 to a target chosen by an explicitly non-fabricated heuristic grounded in Athenian ostracism. This is the full officer-demotion pipeline already built, aimed at a faction rather than a seat; re-pointing it at a seat is smaller work than authoring one.
formula: on pass: target.Sta -= 1; target.L -= 1

name: succeed_governor already preserves durable ledger tags across a handover, via ledger_sweep — zero callers
statement: succeed_governor (systems/settlements/sim/registry.py:199-208) does not merely swap a governor_id string — it calls ledger_sweep(s.ledger, season), whose contract is "remove expired (ttl) tags; durable tags (ttl=None) always survive" (ledger.py:69-75), over the five kinds {Precedent, Grudge, Debt, Reputation, Leverage} (ledger.py:30). The succession primitive already guarantees a demoted/replaced governor's durable record survives them — a property precedent research names as commonly missing elsewhere. It has zero callers, and separately zero code outside the two owner modules calls add_tag/ledger_add/LedgerTag at all, so the ledger it sweeps is never written to in the first place.

name: The ledger's future writer must validate tag kind and bind provenance to the causing Key
statement: ledger_add (systems/settlements/sim/ledger.py:47-58) validates nothing today — an unrecognised tag.kind not in TAG_KINDS appends silently rather than raising — and no LedgerTag carries a provenance field bound to the causing Key. Shadow of War's War Chests failure (buying the output of an earned relationship broke the causal chain for non-payers too) is the precedent: the commit giving the ledger its first production writer must validate kind membership and bind provenance, or a convenience path can manufacture a relational outcome the Key history does not justify. Every authored Grudge/Debt/Leverage key already named in the corpus is already intra-faction, so this is the cheap moment to add the guard — before the ledger has a writer to protect.

name: T-07, the counter-force that never fires — instances at the officer ladder and settlement Order
statement: A bidirectional mechanism whose damping/reversing arm exists in the primitive but is never invoked is the same defect as an unstoppable slide, viewed from the other end. The officer ladder is one instance (~88 up-gates and 74 demotion cells authored, 0 up and 0 down executing); settlement Order is a second (governance_type_registry_v1.md:104 states "no unforced decay term of its own"). The clean verified instance elsewhere is Coherence (systems/threadwork/sim/ coherence.py), whose docstring declares signed deltas with positive meaning recovery, yet every one of five call sites passes zero or negative — its ceiling clamp is unreachable dead code. The guard this pattern earns: for any function whose contract declares a signed delta, assert a seeded campaign reaches at least one call of each sign.

name: Precedent guard — test a down-direction against best-case counter-investment, not the average
statement: Imperator Rome's launch Loyalty shipped a down-direction governors could not out-invest — they lost 20+ points on appointment alone regardless of play — and the whole action-currency was scrapped four months later. Before any suspicion/demotion writer lands on G606 (cumulative suspicion, faction_politics_v30.md §1.0d, Settlement.suspicion registry.py:78), the maximum available per-season mitigation must be run against the maximum accrual and the net asserted recoverable by arithmetic alone; if the fastest possible remediation still nets negative, the mechanic is broken, not merely hard.
status_evidence: (no suspicion writer exists on main to check against)

name: Precedent guard — an internal-competition threshold needs a control arm proving it is reachable
statement: EU4's Estates are the canonical ignorable mechanic: legible and well-motivated, tuned so its failure state is almost never reached, to the point players "hardly even bother." A mechanism engineered not to fire is indistinguishable from one that does not exist. Valoria's live instance is §1.0d Performance Audit, proven mathematically redundant with G606 (H2-025). Every internal-competition threshold this project ships should carry a seeded control-arm run that never engages the mechanic, plus a stated reachability bar; a mechanic firing in 0% of the control's complement should be deleted, not tuned.

name: §1.0d Performance Audit is mathematically, not just empirically, redundant with G606
statement: G606 (cumulative suspicion, capped +1/season, fires at 4) and §1.0d Performance Audit (a streak counter reset by any single Comply, threshold 5 in the tested regime) read the same non-compliance signal. Since G606 fires on the fourth total miss regardless of streaks, and 5 consecutive misses necessarily contain 4 total misses, §1.0d cannot fire first on any trajectory whatsoever under that tuning — the previously-cited "100% of terminal recalls route through G606" result is a certainty derivable from the two mechanisms' shapes, not a statistic (the harness that measured it, pr119_integrated_campaign.py, no longer exists in the tree or archive). Generalized: for cumulative threshold c and streak threshold k, §1.0d's marginal contribution is exactly zero whenever k>=c. The design ruling to merge them (D5, ED-IN-0046/0047) is correct, but both remain live and unmerged in design prose (faction_politics_v30.md:129-143; governance_play_redesign_v1.md:115-125).
status_evidence: (harness no longer exists; conclusion re-derived from the two mechanisms' stated shapes)

name: _emergency_council_parties — Valoria's one live intra-faction two-sided contest, both sides derived from the same faction
statement: engine/cross_scale/scene_dispatch.py:121-139, fired by the Stability Crisis trigger (default-ON, Jordan's 2026-07-08 ratification quoted in mc_v18.py:63-77) and firing ~975 times per seeded 8-campaign golden batch, derives two contest sides from ONE faction's own aggregate stats: side_a is "the sitting leadership's case to stay the course," side_b "the crisis's own case for change." Both sides run the identical default policy (logos_spammer vs logos_spammer, which the module's own comment notes makes every verdict deterministically one genre), and the echo returns to the same faction it came from (actor_faction == target_faction at :267-268). This is the mandate's only executing intra-faction contest, and it has nobody on either side.
formula: side_a = max(1, round(f.L)); side_b = max(1, round(7.0 - f.Sta))

name: The socket to give council contest sides identities already exists, unused
statement: The adapter receiving _emergency_council_parties' output, wrapper.py::_as_contestant (:80-96), already accepts a dict shape carrying a per-side faculty AND a per-side standing_start and evidence dossier — but the party-derivation function passes bare ints, so both sides silently take the int branch and both get the default standing_start=5.0. One level deeper, Venue.split_standing (resolver.py:162,204-205) is a default-off prototype already splitting the fused contest Standing into rank ("ascribed station... not built by ethos") and credit ("earned credibility, built by ethos/support") — rank is a purpose-built, non-ethos-built channel for exactly what an officer's ladder rank would be. Both the input socket and the differentiated channel already exist; nothing currently supplies them with two distinct values.

name: Treaty lapse/consent — flat unconditioned hazard draws with a broken no-RNG fallback, zero callers
statement: systems/factions/sim/treaty.py sets TREATY_LAPSE_RATE_DEFAULT=0.90 per arc and TREATY_CONSENT_RATE_DEFAULT=0.28, both rolled flat against a pure ledger of active treaties with no conditioning on treaty age or relations — an S-fail (no legible logic) and E-fail (teaches the player nothing) together. Separately, the no-RNG fallback is roll = rng.random() if rng else 0.95, compared against roll < lapse_rate — with no RNG supplied a treaty can never lapse at any canonical rate in the stated 0.90-0.95 band. The module has zero production callers, which is the only reason this is dormant rather than a live defect.
formula: TREATY_LAPSE_RATE_DEFAULT = 0.90 (per arc); TREATY_CONSENT_RATE_DEFAULT = 0.28; no-RNG fallback roll = 0.95

name: crown_initiative's bidirectional standing bands are a healthy engine; do not convert to deterministic odds
statement: crown_initiative.py's graded +-1/+-2 standing outcome bands across eight sites are a healthy stochastic engine on a genuinely bidirectional ledger — the one place in the faction layer where both signs of a standing change execute. Its real defect is elsewhere: the standing value it writes/reads (H2-003) bypasses Faction.adjust()'s registry-clamped bounds at all ten write sites. Converting this engine to deterministic odds would be the named over-correction; the fix is a one-line clamp on the value, not a resolver change.

name: Initiation-duty and recognition-contest rung gates are healthy d10 engines; do not convert to deterministic odds
statement: The rung-gate contests of faction_politics_v30.md §1.1-1.4 (Burgher's Examination, Doctrinal Defense, Demotion Appeal, Recall scene, contested mastership) are legitimate rolling engines on the healthy d10 pool with legible obstacles and graded degrees — migrating them to deterministic-odds Mode B would flatten a multi-exchange track the player reads into one probability, destroying the surface the player weighs a real bet against. Leave them on the pool resolver when they are built.
status_evidence: (none of these rungs execute yet; see H2-018)

name: F9 Bloc — the proposed intra-faction divergent-interest generator primitive
statement: Proposed, not built: a faction-scale generator slice drawing k=2-4 "cascade roots" per faction (licensed by faction_behavior_v30.md:121's own statement that a faction may have multiple parallel cascade roots), each carrying a conviction-centroid offset, a cohesion alpha-profile, patronage-degree, caste-gate posture, and a benefit-when-faction-loses flag — a bloc whose payoff is negatively correlated with the faction's headline outcome. The cheapest version of the divergent-interest primitive is one boolean and one sign flip in a payoff read. Proposed collision constraint: every faction must carry at least one bloc pair such that any Directive it issues pleases one bloc and wrongs the other. Verified: effective_convictions and cascade_root return zero .py hits anywhere on main — the design grammar is entirely prose today.
formula: effective_convictions(npc) = alpha*personal + (1-alpha)*effective(supervisor); alpha = clamp(0.4 + alpha_seniority(-0.2..+0.4 by Standing) + alpha_institution(-0.2..+0.2))

name: Officer generation vector (F10) — power_base as the built-in downfall field
statement: Proposed officer generation vector: role, power_base drawn from {patronage, merit, kinship, bureaucratic, military, purchased, ideological}, Standing 0-7, an ethic <alpha,beta> drawn near the settlement's own temperament with a spread parameter, two convictions, an ambition {goal, escalation ladder, timeline 3-5 seasons, fires_card, advance-predicate}, Disposition, leverage {wants, fears, secret}, and >=2 Knots edges into the collision graph. power_base is named as the field that types the NPC's built-in downfall — every generated officer would already carry the specific mechanism by which they can be brought down. Generator invariants proposed: every officer reachable in a well-governed world, not only via failure states; every officer escalates on neglect; every advance-predicate has >=1 player-independent source and a per-season cap.

name: npc.ethic must gain a resolution-branch reader or be dropped
statement: The proposed officer ethic <alpha,beta> vector is specified as descriptive flavour with no resolution branch reading it anywhere in design or code. The stated design invariant is that a generated officer field must be load-bearing on at least one resolution branch or it should not be generated at all; ethic is named as the one deliberate gap to close before it ships.

name: Bailiff Konrad Ems (NPC-G06) — the trace case for the officer object's absence
statement: Konrad Ems (NPC-G06), Crown levy agent at Goldenfurt and the corpus's own "suspicion track made flesh," has a full authored prose dossier (npc_cast.md:100-111, including a Secret — taking Orsk's coin, discoverable via Investigate as a counter-lever against the suspicion track) but no runtime object, and is absent from npc_registry.yaml despite that file's own enforcement line that no named character may appear in design docs without an entry there. Tracing him through all four scales shows every crossing that would need him (settlement governor, faction rank, battle commander) is EMPTY or BROKEN, while crossings needing no person execute lossily on a bare scalar.

name: ED-FA-0018 — the Crown Administrative examination-ladder ruling survives all five closure tests
statement: registers/editorial_ledger_fa.jsonl:18 (2026-07-09, needs_jordan: true, still open): whether the deliberately-flat Crown Administrative branch (faction_politics_v30.md §1.1b) gets a differentiated, non-Skyrim-Eight credentialing sub-structure (capped pass rates, direct Std-3 appointment, a Waiting Laureate Pool). It survives CLAUDE.md's five-test closure ladder: no later ruling touches it, the subject is live, no design document decides it, no in-tree precedent settles it (the four branches with ladders were grounded from Skyrim, which this item exists to correct), and two defensible options lead to materially different political fictions (examination-joined vs. patronage-joined bureaucracy). A sibling precedent worth pairing with it: the Florentine scrutiny-and-lot pipeline (squittinio -> imborsazione -> tratta) together with its documented capture failure (the Medici accoppiatori turning an impartial lot into a weighted one) — pairing a mechanism with its attested subversion, since the subversion is itself the intra-faction game.

name: The score/2 obstacle derivation is genuinely SUSPENDED, at three inconsistent built sites, not "unexecuted"
statement: Jordan's 2026-08-14 ruling that an obstacle rolled against a target derives as their score/2 plus instance modifiers is implemented at crown_initiative.py's coronation_renewal_ob exactly, at tribunal.py conditionally (only under formal grounds), and contradicted at parliamentary_transfer.py (full score, not half) — three built, mutually inconsistent sites, not zero. tests/valoria/test_faction_obstacle_conventions.py pins all three because Jordan explicitly SUSPENDED reconciliation on 2026-08-21 rather than have a session reconcile three ratified numbers on its own authority; wiring score/2 uniformly today would overwrite parliamentary_transfer_v30.md:30's own stated number and collapse the Tribunal's deliberate two-tier formal-grounds halving. This corpus's own first draft mis-cited a stale docstring ("implemented nowhere") and recommended exactly the suspended action — its own worked example that a comment is not a measurement.

name: Every obstacle-derivation site quantises to integer against a ladder built to consume fractions
statement: All four target-derived obstacle sites (coronation_renewal_ob, tribunal's effective_ob, opposing.py's threadwork depth modifier, scene_dispatch's council-party derivation) round or floor their result, while degree_from_net's own docstring states both operands may be fractional and that only the Partial band's window logic survives contact with fractional obstacles at all. The producers were correct when written and stopped being correct once the ladder moved to accept fractions underneath them — a pattern defect, load-bearing on the game (it feeds margin = net - ob at every faction-scale roll) and separable from the suspended score/2 question: fixing the rounding is not blocked by the hold.

name: A settled geography ruling is still presented as an open precondition in four documents
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-07-13 (B2) that S-006 = Goldenfurt and S-007 = Lowenskyst Fortress, followed by a full 37-settlement geography reconciliation, verified landed in valoria_geography_v30.yaml. Four live documents nonetheless still present the seed's identity as an open, blocking precondition: settlement_generator_v1.md:162, generation_methodology.md:186, and generation_sourcebook_v1.md at two rows (:173,:186) that contradict its own :155, which records the question as RESOLVED. An editorial defect, not an execution defect — but a settled question left uncorrected in prose keeps blocking the generator's own calibration fixture.

name: Legitimacy ruled a base descriptor, roster six, floor 0 — executed at faction grain, settlement grain untouched
statement: Three Jordan rulings (2026-08-23) that Legitimacy is a base descriptor, the descriptor roster is six, and the floor is 0 are executed in engine/substrate/descriptors.py:22-26. But Settlement.legitimacy and Settlement.popular_support (systems/settlements/sim/registry.py:69-74) remain declared, serialized, and never read or written by any logic anywhere in sim/ — the settlement-grain half of the same ruling is untouched, and this field also gates whether VSG's P11/P12 allegiance-slice output can ever be checked for sensible politics, since the field it would write is inert.

name: Precedent constraint — tracking interior state and expressing it as legible drama are different unsolved problems
statement: Every precedent that appears to solve expressing interior state (mood, grudge, loyalty, ambition) does so by narrowing scope rather than generalising — Dwarf Fortress's templated flavour text, Nemesis's small closed trait vocabulary, Wildermyth's hand-written per-personality variants (explicitly not procedural, by its own developers' account). Any plan treating "we have the Key substrate" as equivalent to "we have emergent narrative" is skipping exactly the step every precedent struggled hardest with; the Key substrate supplies tracking, not expression, and the two must be budgeted as separate line items in the same milestone, with acceptance stated as a specific reachable state having a specific enumerated expression path.

name: Key.causes has exactly one honest production writer; the corpus's own first claim of four consumers was itself a vocabulary collision
statement: Key.causes is honestly written by exactly one emitter, _apply_accord_echo's scene.accord_echo construction (engine/cross_scale/echo_transport.py:328), whose comment states the discipline: cite an upstream Key id only when one genuinely fired for the same scene, empty list otherwise — never fabricated. This corpus's first pass claimed four production consumers (corroboration independence, case-board known-unknowns, evidence quality, Holding.independent_support); on adversarial re-check none exist in Python — they are design-prose terms, and the only non-test reader of .causes is KeyLog's own invariant validator, which consumes nothing. This is the mechanism by which a person's history would become queryable once a person object exists — Valoria has the chain and not the individual.

name: Cross-scale matrix — every crossing that executes needs no person; every crossing needing one is empty, broken, or flag-off
statement: SETTLEMENT->PERSONAL is EMPTY (all 37 settlements have governor_id None and empty npc_ids after a seeded create_world); FACTION->PERSONAL is BROKEN (combat_bridge.py passes one rounded integer, history=max(1,round(f.Mil)), as the entirety of a personal-combat actor's customisation, gated behind DISPATCH_COMBAT_BRIDGE default-OFF and unreachable even ON since no queue_scene("combat",...) call site exists); PERSONAL->SETTLEMENT is BROKEN (the accord_echo carrier is fully wired but has no live producer setting echo['scene_outcome'] anywhere in the campaign loop). The one EXECUTED personal<->faction crossing, _emergency_council_parties (H2-026), is degenerate precisely because it needs no person. Every crossing that executes carries a scalar; every crossing that would carry a person does not exist.

name: Precedent constraint — a cross-scale bridge's default must not be "off equals doesn't exist"
statement: No surveyed precedent defends a cross-scale bridge whose default state is silently equivalent to the seam not existing — every surveyed game either has no such seam to disable, or ships an explicit, imperfect crossing. combat_bridge.derive_parties correctly returns None on a derivation gap rather than fabricating an actor (preserve this through any repair), but the flag gating it, DISPATCH_COMBAT_BRIDGE, is default-OFF with no production queue_scene("combat",...) call site even when flipped ON — dead twice over, in the one configuration no precedent defends.

name: Precedent constraint — a personal-scale effect on mass-scale outcome must scale as a fraction of unit size, never flat
statement: engine/cross_scale/zoom_in_out.py commits both documented failure directions of the personal-to-mass leverage problem in sixteen lines: pc_incapacitated (:138-142) applies immediately regardless of battle size (flat leverage dominant at small N, the Dominions shape), while contested_figure_wounded (:149) is a flat +0.15 Ob shift whose own comment admits it is not a per-wound-cumulative model — against a distribution whose standard deviation grows as 0.8*sqrt(N), a fixed Ob shift's effect on outcome probability decays as 1/sqrt(N) (leverage evaporating at large N, the Mount & Blade shape). Both carriers are currently unreachable (no producer queues a personal scene from a battle), which is exactly why nobody has had to decide their semantics yet; the guard belongs before the producer that would make them live.

name: Mass-battle's survivor-ratio degree map is a second, self-disclosed degree semantics for one event class
statement: systems/mass_battle/sim/massbattle.py:37-50 maps three survivor-ratio thresholds (0.75/0.25/0.50) to a battle degree, and its own comment states these are "NOT the canonical degree ladder," calling reconciling the two open MB-lane work. This is Total War's autoresolve-divergence failure in miniature — a cheap classification maintained by a different process than the single-owned margin ladder for the same event class; the self-disclosure does the work of a guard, not a fix. The mass-battle resolver must call into combat_engine_v1 for any flagged personal-scale encounter rather than maintain its own approximation.

name: Five historical-precedent officer mechanisms grounded and authored into canon; all prose, none executes
