statement: ED-FA-0019 Recognition Fork (Kamakura honryoando/shin'on reward crisis, PROPOSED, granter's decision rule undefined); ED-FA-0020 Court Attendance (sankin-kotai plus hostage kin, RATIFIED, prose only); ED-FA-0021 Performance Audit / kaochengfa patron-death lapse (PROPOSED, ruled to MERGE into G606 per H2-025, unauthored); ED-FA-0022 capital-gated Free Mastership (Arte della Lana, RATIFIED, prose only); ED-FA-0023 guarantor-gated guild entry (Book of the Eparch, RATIFIED, prose only). All five are grounded in a 2026-07-09 comparative-governance pass; none executes in code.

name: roll_pool's TN parameter was accepted, recorded and discarded — since superseded by a hard TN=7 ruling
statement: As documented in this corpus, engine/autoload/dice_engine.py's discrete roll_pool accepted a tn parameter, recorded it on RollResult, and never used it in computing net — the discrete engine was silently pinned to TN-7 odds regardless of the tn passed, while its continuous sibling honoured tn. 19 production call sites (three of them faction-scale obstacle sites) passed non-trivial tn values into this silently-ignored parameter. This is SUPERSEDED: dice_engine.py now calls _require_tn7(tn) inside roll_pool, refusing any tn != 7 outright (verified at HEAD, 2026-08-27/28), consistent with the ruling recorded in the catalogue's kernel section (Jordan, 2026-08-25, ED-IN-0196). Retained only because it was this corpus's own headline defect and the ruling that mooted it postdates this analysis by at most a day.

name: Settlement.suspicion — zero writers, the field the ruled D5 merge would write to
statement: Settlement.suspicion (systems/settlements/sim/registry.py:78) has zero writers anywhere in engine/ or systems/ — the only other "suspicion" hit in any .py is an unrelated contest-mode comment (social_contest/sim/contest/modes.py:184). It is the field the ruled-but-unauthored D5 merge of §1.0d and G606 (H2-025) would write to once built; today it is a declared, inert schema stub.

name: Faction stats option F-2 — retire Intel scalar into an Intelligence Holdings ledger
statement: Proposal F-2: cut the Faction.Intel scalar (0-7, declared but unread/unwritten by live code) and re-home it as an Intelligence Holdings ledger — "knowing specific things about specific parties" — composing onto the settlement ledger's existing Leverage tag kind. Recommended over F-1 (ratify as-is, keeps a dead stat).

name: Faction stats option F-3 — split derived Mandate into Mandate and Support
statement: Proposal F-3: split faction-scale Mandate into Mandate (elite/settlement Legitimacy) and Support (popular), mirroring the settlement-scale L/PS split already ratified (LPS-2e). Without the split, "beloved locally, distrusted at court" is mechanically inexpressible.

name: New faction Administration stat — WITHDRAWN
statement: Draft-1's proposed F-4 (a new `Administration` stat plus derived `Chancery`) was withdrawn: `Settlement.ap` and the formula `floor(s.ap * compliance(s))` already model administrative reach ("the CK3-Administrative shape realized as a formula"). Draft 1 had lifted a per-settlement quantity into a flat faction scalar — the anti-emergence direction; the corrected move is to aggregate `ap × compliance` upward instead.
status_evidence: registry.py:92 and lps_wiring_v1.md:95, as cited in proposals/2026-08-15-character-and-faction-stats-and-progression.md:300-304

name: Faction Discipline → "Cohesion" rename WITHDRAWN
statement: Draft-1's proposal to rename faction Discipline to "Cohesion" was withdrawn: Cohesion is a name PP-232 already retired (`mass_battle_v30.md:7`, `glossary.md:153`), so re-issuing it fails the CLAUDE.md §4 idempotent-in-meaning rule the rename was invoked to satisfy.
status_evidence: mass_battle_v30.md:7 and glossary.md:153, as cited in proposals/2026-08-15-character-and-faction-stats-and-progression.md:308-309

name: ap × compliance(s) — the governance action-economy formula is PROPOSED, not implemented
statement: `compliance(s)` (the local-attenuation term feeding `Settlement.ap`'s effective governance reach) has zero occurrences in any `systems/**/*.py`; it is a formula from `lps_wiring_v1.md`, whose own status is PROPOSED, not measured code. A companion census (2026-08-16) had tabulated it as a measured BLEND role; the adversarial pass corrected that to "a proposed formula tabulated as measured."

name: Faction actions and settlement governance read no character attribute at all
statement: Of seven character-facing gameplay surfaces (physical/social/spiritual capability mappings), two read no character attribute at all: faction actions consume only bare faction stats (Mil, W, I) and settlement governance consumes only `ap × compliance` plus Ledger tags. The character sheet reaches five of seven surfaces; personnel and faction leadership are not among them.

name: Ten character-facing roles split into six skill roles and four position roles
statement: Jordan's ten enumerated character-facing capabilities (spy, detective, interrogator, combatant, general, debater, politician, orator, governor, leader) split into six "skill" roles carried by practice/instruments/school, and four "position" roles — General, Politician, Governor, Leader — that additionally require an office (an army, a seat, a settlement, a faction respectively), not just aptitude.

name: Position-role build status — General/Politician/Governor/Leader
statement: Of the four position roles: Politician (Standing ladder + Mandate/votes, needs a seat) and Leader (Standing 7 / faction emergence, needs a faction) are prose-only with no resolver. General is partly built (Command formula only; no army object exists). Governor is partly built — `registry.py`'s AP/ledger primitives exist, but the verb layer that spends them does not.

name: A cross-domain role architecture already exists in three places, unnamed
statement: The layered role architecture (Pool/practice, Instruments, School, Techniques, Faculties, Office) that combat already implements is independently duplicated by the social-contest kernel's Dossier/EvidenceItem + four-way style axis, and by settlements' `ledger.py` + AP. Naming this shared architecture once, rather than three unnamed instances, is most of the remaining design work for the Governor position role.

name: Attribute-roster count RULED at ten; tenth attribute unnamed
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-08-14 (ED-IN-0193): the character attribute roster is ten, not shrinking or dissolving. The registry ships nine named attributes; the tenth is deliberately unnamed — naming it is the only open part of the count, per `descriptor_registry.yaml:39-43`. An earlier draft's "the roster dissolves into a generated view" (§19.5 of the source document) is explicitly withdrawn as stale-on-arrival.

name: Command formula, corrected — round not ceiling, and clamped
statement: Mass-battle Command is `clamp(round((2·Charisma + Cognition)/3), 1, 7)` at `exchange.py:49` — `round()`, not the ceiling notation five separate documents (including this one, twice) had copied from prose. Cha/Cog default to `None` in the wired strategic path and the derivation is guarded on both being non-None.

name: Command derivation is provably inert on the wired strategic mass-battle path
statement: In the campaign-reachable path, `_faction_to_unit` hardcodes `command=4` for both sides and Charisma/Cognition default to `None`, so the Command formula (H3-011) never actually executes; `test_field_golden_pins.py:47-49` classifies the Command flags as provably inert. The formula only lives in the excluded/canon (J2) engine, flag-gated on `COMMAND_SIGMA_ENABLED`.

name: Own vs. borrowed scores, by system — factions and settlements borrow nothing
statement: Bottom-up per-system score census: factions declare W, Mil, I, Sta, L, standing, territories and settlements declare prosperity, defense, order, L, PS, fort_level, facility_tier, ap, ledger tags — and neither borrows a single roster (character) attribute into resolution. Of seven systems censused, only these two borrow nothing at all.

name: Faction entity — declared fields
statement: `Faction(name, parliamentary, L, Sta, W, I, Mil, intel, territories, standing, excommunicated, peaceful, …per-arc flags)` — the declared entity at `engine/autoload/game_state.py`. Six scalars carry the bulk of resolution; the rest is boolean turn-tracking.

name: Faction.intel — declared, never read or written by live code
statement: `Faction.intel` (declared 0-7) is "currently unread/unwritten by live code" per its own inline flag at `game_state.py:105-110`. Confirmed independently: `intel` has no `MULTS` entry (`game_state.py:45`), so `Faction.adjust('intel', …)` raises `KeyError`, and it is absent from `STARTING_STATS` and `serialize_world`.
baseline_ref: personnel_muster_integration_master_v1.md §9.2 item 5 (Fiscal Stance / faction-scalar gaps, adjacent finding)

name: Faction.L doubles as the scalar Mandate, the superseded pre-LPS-1 convention
statement: `Faction.L` is used as the scalar Mandate by explicit tree-wide convention (cited five times, e.g. `parliamentary_bridge.py:72` — "Mandate==Faction.L pre-LPS-1"), evaluating nonzero (Church 5.0, Crown 5.0, Hafenmark 4.0, Varfell 4.0). The ratified LPS-1 aggregate (`clamp(round(7T/(T+6)),0,7)`) that should replace it has no implementation because neither per-settlement Legitimacy nor Popular Support exists in code.

name: Faction.standing — the only durable cross-season pool-feeding standing in the tree
statement: `Faction.standing` (`game_state.py`, written at `crown_initiative.py:79,115`) is a durable, cross-season TRACK that also feeds a pool (Royal Progress = `Influence + standing`) — the only such faction-scale primitive in the tree.

name: Settlement entity — declared fields
statement: `Settlement(sid, name, stype, province_id, owner_faction, governor_id, prosperity, defense, order, fort_level, garrison, legitimacy, popular_support, facility_tier, suspicion, pressure, active_directive, religious_building, church_attention, governor_emergence, subnational, npc_ids, ledger, open_needs, deck_state)` — `systems/settlements/sim/registry.py`.

name: Settlement prosperity/defense/order — derived-value formulas, correctly re-sited
statement: Prosperity, defense and order are derived values (approx ×50 / ×20 + fort×30 / ×20 respectively). The 2026-08-16 census originally mis-cited these to `registry.py`; the adversarial pass corrected the site to `systems/settlements/sim/settlement.py:89-91`.

name: Settlement.ap formula, corrected — includes a Seat/Cathedral bonus
statement: `AP = 2 + facility_tier + bonus`, where `bonus = 1` at Seat/Cathedral/Cathedral-City (`registry.py:92-97`) — corrected from an earlier flat `2 + FacilityTier` statement. Three settlements (S-001, S-031, S-036) therefore start at AP 3, not 2.

name: Settlement.legitimacy / popular_support — declared, zero non-definition references
statement: `legitimacy` and `popular_support` are declared on `Settlement` (`registry.py:69-74`) with zero non-definition references anywhere in `systems/` — the adversarial pass narrowed the original "never read or written" claim, since `registry.py:120,145` do read/write them for serialization; nothing outside serialization touches them.

name: Settlement ledger — five tag kinds, zero consumers in systems/
statement: The settlement ledger (Precedent, Grudge, Debt, Reputation, Leverage — `ledger.py`) is a real, durable, TTL-bearing TRACK with zero consumers in `systems/`.

name: Territory and Settlement independently declare prosperity, fort_level and garrison
statement: `Territory` (`game_state.py`) separately declares `accord, pt, garrison, prosperity, fort_level, templar`. `prosperity`, `fort_level` and `garrison` therefore exist at BOTH settlement and territory scale, and whether this is the same quantity at two grains or two quantities sharing three names is explicitly unresolved.

name: Subscript writes hidden from AST census — NPC stance and conviction scars are live-mutated
statement: An AST scan matching only `ast.Attribute` targets is blind to `Subscript` writes, so an earlier "the only character-scale quantity any live code changes is Coherence" headline is false: `systems/characters/sim/conviction.py:213` writes `state.scars[conviction]`, `systems/world/sim/npe.py:355-365` mutates NPC `stance[issue]` up and down, and combat's `wrapper.py` mutates several per-beat scalars via subscript/attribute paths an AST-on-`Attribute` scan cannot see. The defensible claim narrows to "no durable roster attribute has an external writer."

name: ap tagged CEILING despite zero readers — inconsistent with the sibling inert-field tags
statement: `ap` was tagged CEILING (an active resource bound) in the original census despite having zero readers in `systems/` — the identical evidentiary position as `legitimacy`/`popular_support`, which the same document correctly flags as inert. The adversarial pass names this an inconsistent tagging, not a new fact about `ap` itself.

name: descriptor_registry.yaml imposes a roster four of seven systems do not conform to
statement: `references/descriptor_registry.yaml` imposes a character-attribute roster that factions and settlements (among four of seven censused systems) do not draw from at all — they declare their own local scores instead. The proposed fix (S10, not ratified) is to invert the registry into a generated view of what systems actually declare, with promotion to a shared name requiring evidence (≥2 systems, same semantics, same shape).

name: Faction personality is a bare name-string comparison; two of six factions have no branch
statement: Faction-specific behaviour is implemented as `if faction.name == 'Crown' … elif == 'Church'` string comparison; Hafenmark and Varfell have no branch at all, so swapping their names in the starting-stats table leaves the simulation unchanged. `parliamentary_action.py:68-69` states explicitly: "No grudge / hostility / inter-faction-relationship stat exists in game_state.Faction."

name: Faction.adjust() unconditionally clamps every stat to [0.5, 7.0]
statement: `Faction.adjust()` (`game_state.py:127-128`) clamps unconditionally to `[0.5, 7.0]`, and 0 of 31 non-test call sites override the bounds. Since score/2 of the minimum 0.5 is 0.25, and every built stat-derived obstacle floors again anyway (tribunal `max(1.0,…)`, crown/fieldwork `+1`, parliamentary transfer `+2`, mass seizure `OB_FLOOR=1`, knots `min 1`), no site has ever produced a zero obstacle. The live decision is whether to keep this single hardcoded clamp or install per-stat floors — and neither declared design source knows the clamp exists.

name: Fieldwork already wrote the score/2 ruling's exact shape against Faction.intel — pre-ratification
statement: `systems/fieldwork/fieldwork_v30.md:662-663` already specifies BG espionage as `Ob = floor(target Intel/2) + 1` — the exact ruled score/2 shape, authored before Jordan's ruling. Since `Faction.intel` is dead (H3-015), ratifying score/2 without wiring Intel makes the tree's first already-compliant faction obstacle evaluate to a permanent constant of 1.

name: Massbattle's opposed-roll degree label is mechanically dead on the live campaign path
statement: `systems/mass_battle/sim/massbattle.py:950` computes a degree and annotates it "# narrative degree label only"; damage at `:965-966` bypasses it entirely, and the variable is assigned three times in the file and read never. The structurally identical line in the canon (J2) tree (`tests/sim/mass_battle/orchestration.py:1304`) feeds `DAMAGE_BY_DEGREE` — so the campaign-reachable opposed roll is dead while the mechanically load-bearing twin lives in the tree the campaign cannot reach.

name: Obstacle sites by subsystem — factions carries 21 of 213 tree-wide, 6 unclassifiable
statement: An 18-agent census enumerated 213 obstacle sites tree-wide (122 non-oppositional, 31 oppositional, 33 ambiguous, 19 hybrid, 8 opposed-roll). Factions account for 21 sites (6 unclassifiable); fieldwork+npcs+characters carry the most (51), settlements+world 20.

name: The middle reading of the score/2 obstacle ruling has a working faction/threadwork precedent AND a trap for mass battle
statement: Threadwork's `opposing.py:80-85,115-123` already implements the "middle" reading of the score/2 ruling: both practitioners roll, AND each side's obstacle is `base_ob + floor(opponent_tps/2)`. Applying the same shape to mass battle is a named trap: `massbattle.py:1887-1890` hardcodes `command=4, discipline=5` for BOTH sides under a declared `[GAP: no canonical spec]`, so a defender-Command/2 obstacle would become the literal constant 2 for both sides, in every campaign battle, forever — deleting the only thing that currently distinguishes the two sides.

name: B2 — the faction stat roster is a four-way, unreconciled conflict across ratified surfaces
statement: Four surfaces disagree on the faction stat roster and its ranges: `descriptor_registry.yaml` (5 base stats, Mandate explicitly not a base attribute; Influence 1-7, Wealth/Military/ Intel/Stability 0-7); `faction_canon_v30.md` (6, incl. derived Mandate; Influence/Wealth/ Military/Intel all 1-7, Stability 0-7); `module_contracts.yaml` (Mandate + Treasury derived, plus an unenumerated "faction stats 1-7"); and code (`game_state.py:98-111`, 6 fields `L, Sta, W, I, Mil, intel`, with `L` a writable base Mandate proxy). The registry's 0-floors are a deliberate, documented 2026-07-08 override (ED-IN-0029) that never names `faction_canon_v30.md` — a genuine conflict between two ratified surfaces, not drift.

name: B2 does not reach mass battle — command/discipline are hardcoded, not read from faction stats
statement: `_faction_to_unit` reads only `faction.Mil`; command and discipline — the two stats every mass-battle obstacle would need to halve under the score/2 ruling — are hardcoded literals. B2 (the faction stat roster ruling) and B3 (the obstacle-derivation ruling) therefore do not compose at the mass-battle seam.

name: Treasury should be struck from the faction-roster open list, not ruled
statement: Treasury = Wealth × 100 is already agreed by three surfaces (`derived_stats_v30.md:298`, `descriptor_registry.yaml:192`, `module_contracts.yaml:109`); the only gap is a missing field, not a design disagreement — it should not be added to the B2 ruling docket.

name: Mandate-as-derived is a sequencing call — it blocks faction-side ruling on the settlement lane, not the faction lane
statement: Derived Mandate = `clamp(round(7T/(T+6)),0,7)` over per-settlement L/PS, and neither Legitimacy nor Popular Support exists in code. So "Mandate is derived" means every faction obstacle depending on it blocks on the settlement layer being built, not on faction-lane work.

name: A conditional (kit-dependent) obstacle has no slot in the R1 obstacle-derivation doctrine
statement: If a character's obstacle-facing score is a static attribute, score/2 reads off a 1-7 roster and is static. If it is instead the acquisition layer (kit/tradition), the obstacle becomes conditional — inert without the right kit — so two identically-statted defenders present different obstacles depending on what they carry. The R1 doctrine as scoped has no slot for a conditional obstacle object.

name: No per-object content-address (proposition identity) primitive exists anywhere in the runtime
statement: `hashlib` appears exactly once in all of `engine/`+`systems/` (`keys.py:460`, `KeyLog.content_hash()` — a digest of an entire append-only log). There is no per-object content-address primitive; a proposed byte-level preimage spec (sha256 over canonical UTF-8 JSON, explicit nulls, type-tagged entity refs, hash_version outside the preimage) is design only.

name: Preimage merge (delimiter collision) manufactures contradictions silently
statement: A proposition-identity preimage built by naive string concatenation risks a delimiter collision that merges two distinct claims into one id — worse than a divergent hash, because provenance unions and `independent_support` inflates with no provenance floor to surface it. Both existing joined preimages in the tree today (`harness.py:143`, `workbench.py:253`) are unescaped.

name: The degree ladder is single-owned and guarded; obstacle derivation has no owner and no guard
statement: `tests/valoria/test_degree_ladder_single_owner.py:134-141` registers six ladders plus two declared holds and fails if a hold silently resolves. No equivalent guard exists for obstacle derivation, and the obstacle reaches the single owner (`dice_engine.roll_pool`) as a parameter from only the factions and threadwork lanes — the largest outstanding ruling (R1) has nothing that would fail on recurrence.

name: is_live" and "is load-bearing" are independent axes for obstacle sites, and censuses conflate them
statement: Combat's scene path is orphaned (unreachable); mass battle's live opposed roll is mechanically dead while its inert twin is load-bearing in the canon tree; the contest's canonical audience resistance is derived and never consumed. A ruling scoped to "live" sites would touch almost nothing; scoped to "load-bearing" sites it lands hardest on the canon mass-battle tree no campaign reaches — the two scopes produce nearly disjoint work lists.

name: Eleven open items on Jordan's desk from the B1/B2/B3 census
statement: Enumerated docket: B3's reading (narrow/broad/middle); what IS a character's scalar score (blocks B3-broad and the PC migration); B2's faction roster (registry's 5 vs faction_canon's 6); the `[0.5,7.0]` clamp vs per-stat floors; whether score/2 stays fractional at five integerizing sites; Faction.intel disposition; Mandate derived-vs-base; acquisition-layer distinctness; the B1 proposition-identity preimage spec; whether TN is a live lever; and two named collisions (tribunal's double-halving, the two-doc Suppress Ob contradiction).

name: Two-doc Suppress obstacle contradiction, filed nowhere
statement: The same Suppress roll is specified as `Ob = Church Mandate` in `conviction_track_v30.md:204` and `floor(Church Mandate/2)+1` in `faction_layer_v30.md:699` — a doc-vs-doc obstacle conflict. The code implements the losing form (the flat form) behind an inert default the only live caller never sets, so the conflict has never mattered in practice but is undocumented as a collision.

name: Six re-verified obstacle/roll facts, hand-checked
statement: Hand-reverified after the census workflow: `roll_pool` ignores `tn`; `hashlib` appears exactly once in `engine/`+`systems/`; `Faction.adjust` clamps `[0.5,7.0]`; no `queue_scene("combat")` call site exists; `massbattle.py:1884-1893` hardcodes `command=4, discipline=5` for both sides; `a_deg`/`b_deg` are assigned three times and read zero times.

name: Mass battle's private roller honours TN; the single owner it delegates to does not
statement: `systems/mass_battle/sim/massbattle.py` forks its own `roll_pool(n, tn=7, rng=None)` (`:627`) which actually honours `tn` (`elif tn <= f <= 9: net += 1`, `:635`), while deferring to the single-owned ladder via `compute_degree` (`:640-643`). The unofficial fork is more correct than the owner: `dice_engine._die_result` hardcodes the TN-7 face rule and ignores its own `tn` parameter.

name: Production roll inventory — 55 call sites, 6 distinct adjudicators, exact AST count
statement: An AST-exact inventory over `engine/`, `systems/`, `tests/sim/` finds 36 production roll call sites (55 including `tests/sim/`), 7 carrying an obstacle, 20 passing a (mostly-inert) TN, 19 adjudication call sites, and 6 distinct adjudicator functions in use tree-wide. Factions is the densest subsystem: 9 rolls, 7 of them obstacle-bearing, 8 passing TN.

name: All 7 obstacle-bearing production rolls live in systems/factions/sim/ — corrects the census synthesis
statement: All 7 obstacle-bearing rolls in production are in `systems/factions/sim/` (`absolution.py:65`, `council_solmund.py:63`, `crown_initiative.py:83/153/239`, `parliamentary_transfer.py:259`, `tribunal.py:125`). This corrects the 2026-08-19 obstacle census's own synthesis, which claimed the obstacle also reaches the dice owner from threadwork — threadwork rolls bare and adjudicates the obstacle in a separate, private step.

name: Rolling and adjudicating are decoupled in 6 of 7 resolving subsystems
statement: The obstacle is not a parameter of *rolling* almost anywhere — it is an argument to a *local* degree function called after a bare roll. That is why the obstacle has no single owner: it was never on the dice owner's call path in the first place, except in the factions lane.

name: Nineteen production TN parameters are inert, listed by site
statement: Nineteen production call sites pass `tn=` into `dice_engine.roll_pool`, which ignores it: `sigma_leverage.py:274`; `combat/sim/combat.py:214,216`; six factions sites (`absolution:65, council_solmund:63, crown_initiative:83/153/239, mass_seizure:263, parliamentary_transfer:259, tribunal:125`); `fieldwork/sim/knots.py:223`; two social_contest sites; three threadwork sites. Only the continuous path (`sigma_leverage.py:285`) honours TN.

name: Settlements, overview and characters resolve entirely deterministically — zero dice-engine imports
statement: Settlements (0 of 8 files), overview (0 of 8) and characters (0 of 5) import neither `dice_engine` nor `sigma_leverage`, and have zero raw `rng`/`random` calls anywhere. They resolve entirely by threshold comparison and accounting arithmetic (Prosperity/Order/Defense deltas, CI/RS/MS/IP track movement, conviction scar accumulation) — a legitimate design that nothing declares, so a reader looking for e.g. an Order-0 revolt check finds only a comparison.

name: Factions imports engine.* at 88% of files — the one lane that uses the dice owner as intended
statement: 16 of 18 files in `systems/factions/sim/` import `engine.*` (autoload, dice_engine, game_state, substrate) — the highest engine-integration ratio of any subsystem, versus settlements at 0% and combat at 6%.

name: settlements is the only subsystem that loads external runtime data — its own geography YAML
statement: `settlements` imports nothing from `engine/` at all and is the only subsystem that loads external data at runtime — its own geography YAML (`registry.py:248`), not a shared registry.

name: references/ registries have zero runtime readers tree-wide
statement: Nothing in `engine/` or `systems/` loads any file under `references/` — `descriptor_registry.yaml` (the stat vocabulary owner), `names_index.yaml` (naming owner) and `module_contracts.yaml` (the IO owner) each have zero runtime readers, only 44 `tools/` (CI/tooling) readers. Every stat name and faction name in the runtime is therefore a hand-copied literal that can silently drift from its registry with no mechanism to catch it (warn-tier CI only).

name: Measured literal duplication of faction-roster and attribute-name strings
statement: Measured duplication: 11 distinct faction-roster literal lists, 10 attribute-name literal lists, and 15 distinct key-type strings written as literals in code — none of which even agree with their own registry (the registry's primary attribute names Acuity/Will/Attunement appear as code identifiers nowhere; code uses the aliases cog/spirit/att instead).

name: The Key substrate's typed export layer has essentially one runtime loader on the Python side
statement: Of `engine/engine_params/`'s typed exports, only `key_types.json` has a runtime loader (`echo_transport.py:68-69`); `combat_engine_v1.json` and `params_tables.yaml` have none. The typed layer exists for the Godot port and is, from the Python runtime's perspective, a write-only artifact with a round-trip check.

name: A cooked-export + runtime-loader pattern already exists once and could extend to the stat vocabulary
statement: Since `key_types.json` (cooked from markdown, loaded by `echo_transport`) already demonstrates a working pattern, the smallest concrete fix for the literal-duplication problem (H3-053, H3-054) is proposed: give `descriptor_registry.yaml` a cooked export and one runtime loader, so stat/faction names become imported rather than copied.

name: Six private roll/degree implementations exist in production, one is the mass-battle roller
statement: Six private roll/degree owners fork the single-owned dice/ladder machinery in production: `massbattle.roll_pool` (forks the roller, honours TN), `massbattle.compute_degree` (thin delegate), `contest/resolver.roll_net`, `combat/core.degree` (declared HOLD), `threadwork /operations._compute_degree`, `threadwork/opposing._degree_label`. `tests/sim/` (the J2 canon mass-battle engine) additionally carries a complete second dice stack.

name: If the obstacle gets an owner without the roller getting one, the same fork will recur
statement: "Single owner" was enforced on the degree ladder only; the roller forked four ways in production and again in `tests/sim/`. Ruling the obstacle (H3-040) without also owning the roller predicts the same fork recurring — a measured precedent for the CLAUDE.md §0.1 point-5 guard argument, not merely a prediction.

name: A decision is needed on whether probability gates (27 in combat) are in scope for any obstacle doctrine
statement: Personal combat resolves most of its outcomes (measure closing, disengage, riposte, bind dominance, grab escape) via 27 probability gates comparing `rng.random()` against a computed probability, not via dice rolls — 30 of the tree's outcome-producing branches tree-wide. No ruling has ever mentioned whether these are in scope for the obstacle/TN doctrine.

name: Order-of-operations note — GDScript cannot read Python literals, so every hand-copied name needs re-export
statement: Every hand-copied literal identified in H3-054 is a value that must be re-typed by hand for the Godot port unless exported first — the Key-substrate export pattern (H3-056) is named as the template.

name: In every seeded campaign, the population of Valoria is zero — a ruled permanent deferral, not an oversight
statement: `generate_npc` is correct and tested but has no world-gen or season-tick call site; `world.npcs` is empty every run. `engine/tests/test_pipeline_reach.py:137-145` reclassifies this from "oversight" to a PERMANENT deferral (OI-05, `xfail(strict=True)`) because canon (`investigation_systems_v30.md:102`) specifies scene-specification-driven generation and no live scene spec generates anyone — the trigger canon requires does not exist in the live loop.

name: Settlement.npc_ids has a slot for people; the person record has a slot for nothing
statement: `Settlement.npc_ids` (`registry.py:87`) is a declared field awaiting occupants; there is no reciprocal "which settlement am I in" or "what happened to me" field on any person record — the loss runs one direction.

name: Five built, correct, orphaned governance/personnel mechanisms with no caller
statement: `generate_npc`, `succeed_governor`, `mass_seizure`, treaty expiry, `add_belief`, `revise_belief`, and `Settlement.ap` are all built and correct with zero production callers — the settlement ledger's only production caller is `ledger_sweep`.

name: Social contest runs live but is fed degenerate input — every contest is logos_spammer vs logos_spammer
statement: The social-contest call site never passes `world=`, so audience resistance is derived and always `None`; no `Dossier` is ever populated; no armature is passed, so Style, the CLASH/REINFORCE algebra and the CR5 backfire are unreachable; `base_ob = 2.0` is fixed, never overridden by any of 8 proceedings. The consequence spine is a bare ±1/±2 Mandate delta on one faction. This is a caller-enrichment fix, not a new mechanism.

name: Entity comparison — Settlement is instantiated and named every campaign; NPC never is
statement: Settlement has 25 fields, is authored/named, instantiated every campaign via `populate_from_geography`, has 8 of 25 boot-populated (corrected upward from an initial ~6-7 estimate), and is read every season. Faction has 16 fields (stats + 7 booleans, 4 of them turn-tracking flags). NPC has 12 fields, is unnamed, and is never instantiated in a campaign — the loop over `world.npcs` runs on an empty dict.

name: owner_faction is populated for 37 of 37 settlements — corrects an earlier misread
statement: Corrected by directly parsing the geography YAML: every settlement entry carries `controller` (Crown 15, Hafenmark 10, Varfell 10, Church 1, Schoenland 1) — `owner_faction` is boot-populated for 37 of 37 settlements, not the single S-037/Schoenland entry an earlier misreading of `registry.py:233-236` had implied.

name: Boot-populated Settlement fields are 8 of 25, and the registry is not boot-only
statement: Boot-populated fields are `sid, name, stype, province_id, owner_faction, prosperity, defense, order` (8 of 25). But the registry is not boot-only: `overview/sim/accounting.py:143` calls `_probe_province_accord_drift` unconditionally every season, which sharpens rather than softens the module-contract finding — `module_contracts.yaml:693` points `sim_module:` at `settlement.py`, which has no importer, while `registry.py` (the file with a live per-season reader) has no `sim_module:` row at all, a disclosed split rather than an absence.

name: No PC record exists — form_knot duck-types four fields no class defines
statement: `form_knot` duck-types `.bonds`, `.spirit`, `.history_relationships`, `.ts` — no class in the tree defines them. A PC is a bare `actor_id` string used as a key across five registries, of which `world.npcs` is territory-keyed rather than actor-keyed (`game_state.py:188`), so even the shared-key framing is only true of four registries. (Corrected scope: "no actor class" holds only for PCs — `NPC` and `Combatant` are real actor classes with per-instance state.)

name: Hidden-allegiance deviation is a dead write voiding 1 of 5 branches of the Tier-2 NPC deviation mechanic
statement: `npe.py:296-299` assigns a hidden-allegiance deviation to a local variable the constructor at `:308-319` never receives — silently voiding 1 of 5 branches (`rng.randint(0,4)`, `:283`) of the Tier-2 deviation mechanic, ~20% of deviation rolls producing no state change, against canon's "one axis is rolled against the opposite extreme" (`investigation_systems_v30.md:104`). The field is canon-required at `investigation_systems_v30.md:86`.

name: NPC faction-weighted selection comment is false — the code is an unweighted rng.choice
statement: `npe.py:261`'s comment claims selection is "weighted by faction"; the code is an unweighted `rng.choice`.

name: apply_knot_loss drops two of four consequences into a dict no caller applies
statement: `composure_damage` and `disposition_set_to` are computed inside `apply_knot_loss`'s return dict but no caller applies them — 2 of 4 declared consequences are silently dropped.

name: NPC persistent_state is never written despite being canon-required for cross-scene memory
statement: `persistent_state` defaults at `npe.py:134`, is serialized at `:147`/`:163`, and has no assignment site anywhere — canon specified it for "remember interactions with the player (Disposition changes carry forward)" (`investigation_systems_v30.md:109`).

name: The conviction taxonomy split is a documented-supersession violation, not an arithmetic error
statement: `conviction.py:44-49` runs `conviction_track_v1.md:20-28`'s legacy 9-Conviction set verbatim, in table order (Faith, Order, Reason, Equity, Precedent, Autonomy, Continuity, Community, Warden) — even though that same doc's own line 2 says "do not use §1 of this file for Conviction definitions." An earlier claim that the set contained "4 members in no taxonomy" was arithmetically wrong; the real defect is that the code knowingly runs a table its own canon head disowns.

name: A third, canon-quoted conviction roster exists in NPE generation and disagrees with both others
statement: `npe.py:80`'s 8-member roster (Faith, Order, Reason, Justice, Survival, Loyalty, Truth, Power) is quoted verbatim from its own canon head, `investigation_systems_v30.md:84`, which asserts this IS "the existing conviction taxonomy" — so the defect lives in canon, not only in code. Of the canonical 13, six of npe.py's eight are absent. Two are cross-roster term collisions: Loyalty is also a 0-3 affiliation scalar in the same file (`npe.py:125`) and Truth is also the renamed 0-5 personal axis (`conviction.py:61-63`, ED-IN-0075).

name: The 'Loyalty' knot-scar no-op is masked by a test that asserts intent, not effect
statement: `knots.py:349-353` scars `'Loyalty'`, a member of no canonical roster; `conviction.py:191-193` returns magnitude-0 for any unknown name — a silent no-op. `engine/tests/test_knots_ed912.py: 103-116` asserts `c["conviction_scar"] == 1`, but `knots.py:346` sets that flag unconditionally, before and independently of the `apply_conviction_scar` call, so the test never observes the actual effect — a live CLAUDE.md §0.1 point-2 exemplar sitting in the blocking sim-regression job.

name: NPC temperament drift has a read/write asymmetry — writes are world-scoped, reads always hit the module global
statement: `temperaments.py:153-158` writes drift through `_drift_store(world)` into `world.npc_drift_state` (real, serialized); `temperaments.py:117` reads `_drift_store()` with no `world` argument, always hitting the module-level global. Latent today (neither has a caller); would silently diverge the moment either is wired — the exact read/write asymmetry shape CLAUDE.md §0.1 point 1 names.

name: CI_GAIN_TEMPLAR is a dead canonical constant contradicted by its own docstring
statement: `infrastructure.py:53` declares `CI_GAIN_TEMPLAR` (+1 CI/season); `ci_track.py:37` documents the dependency in prose but imports nothing from `infrastructure` and applies no Templar term in its 5-step PP-412 computation.

name: npc_relational_graph_v30 asserts BUILT sections with zero code behind any of them
statement: `npc_relational_graph_v30.md` marks §7/§8 "BUILT 2026-06-09, ED-1000" while its own §655-657 lists parts of the same sections as "full mechanics deferred (§7 hook only)" and "not stress-tested" — a within-document self-contradiction. No code exists behind any of the six authored edge types (sworn-bond, liege-vassal, kinship, patronage, rivalry, feud): no `canon/relational_edges_v30.yaml`, no cascade module, repo-wide.

name: A complete narrative-rendering pipeline exists and is orphaned from the only live campaign loop
statement: `combat_engine_v1/workbench/{narrate.py,commentary.py,server.py}` and `contest/agon_harness.py` together form a runnable game-state → prose → UI pipeline (including a live stdlib HTTP server), but its two callers (the combat workbench, whose engine has no `queue_scene` caller, and the contest chronicle, whose only callers are its own tests) have no campaign reach. `contest/narrative.py` also would not generalise — it binds to the bout's specific beat-log shape by construction.

name: Authored settlement prose (description, coords) is dropped at load; only the name is carried
statement: `valoria_geography_v30.yaml` carries a hand-written `description` and `coords` per settlement; `populate_from_geography` carries `name` through (`registry.py:261`) but drops both `description` and `coords`, because `Settlement` has no prose or position field — narrower than an earlier "authored strings are wholly discarded" claim.

name: The authored-person loader — the single build that turns four or five dormant person-mechanics live at once
statement: Recommended: a named-NPC registry loader populated from `references/npc_registry.yaml` at `create_world`, on the exact pattern of `populate_from_geography`. Because `world.convictions`, `world.beliefs`, `world.knots`, `world.npcs` and `Settlement.npc_ids` are already declared, routed and serialized, one loader would activate several already-ticking systems at once; `generate_npc`'s output is anonymous by construction and its trigger is a ruled permanent deferral (H3-061), so it cannot substitute as the path to real people.

name: references/npc_registry.yaml holds 46 fully-structured characters with zero Python loaders
statement: `references/npc_registry.yaml` holds 46 characters, each with id, first_name, faction, role, birthplace, territory, ts, coherence, a stats block (cognition/focus/endurance/social), a weighted-primaries convictions block, cultural_label, migration notes, authored goals, arc_trajectory, resonant_style and notes. Its own line 5 states "No character name may appear in design docs without an entry here." It has zero Python loaders — `tests/valoria/ test_references_yaml_parse.py:1-9` records the file was unparseable for its entire visible git history and nothing noticed, because it had zero readers (ED-IN-0121).

name: Two further authored-conviction data sources are machine-parseable and unloaded
statement: `conviction_migration_roster_v30.md:41-245` adds 13 authored, machine-parseable conviction profiles on the npc_registry model; `conviction_axis_matrix_v30.md:26-38` supplies a complete numeric 13×4 matrix with its composition rule at `:209-211`. Both are unloaded by any runtime code.

name: Loading a named-NPC registry needs the conviction taxonomy resolved first
statement: Every one of the 46 npc_registry entries carries weighted convictions in the canonical 13-member taxonomy, while the live validator (`conviction.py`) runs the legacy 9-member set — so the authored-person loader (H3-081) cannot be written without first resolving the conviction-taxonomy split (H3-073, H3-074).

name: Strategic mass battle is geometrically degenerate — both armies co-locate and never move
statement: `_faction_to_unit` hardcodes both sides identically (`command=4, discipline=5, 'Line', infantry`), so only `power` varies between armies and `terrain` is always `None`. Every strategic-scale battle is symmetric by construction; identical shape+tier+position+direction means both armies occupy the same cells and `advance_cells` computes `dr=dc=0`, so nothing ever moves.

name: The degree ladder is read on one mass-battle path and dead on the other
statement: The strategic-scale `degree` drives the Terms/Storm conquest fork; the per-engagement `degree` computed on the campaign-reachable tactical path is dead (see H3-030), while its twin is load-bearing in the canon (J2) tree the campaign cannot reach.

name: insurgency_pipeline promotion is structurally dead — the promoting field is written exactly once
statement: `insurgency_pipeline.py`'s promotion mechanic sets `rec.L` once to 1.0, the promotion gate requires ≥3, and nothing else in the tree ever writes it again — promotion is unreachable.

name: settlement_layer_v30 specifies a ratified but unloaded Dearth/granary accounting chain
statement: `settlement_layer_v30.md:740-778` specifies the Dearth/granary chain in full, including a `granary: int (0-3)` registry field, as ED-SE-0008 (PROPOSED). Reporting "zero food/harvest code tree-wide" without naming this reads as "canon is silent" when canon is explicit and merely awaiting ratification.

name: Method finding — presenting already-filed governance defects as new discoveries inflates apparent yield
statement: Several findings this document initially presented as discoveries were already filed: `proposals/2026-08-15-character-and-faction-stats-and-progression.md:342-343` already recorded the superseded-9 conviction roster and the 'Loyalty' no-op seven days earlier; a 2026-08-10 audit already recorded the 8-field boot population, inert legitimacy/popular_support, the religious_building collision, and `ap`/`add_tag`/`succeed_governor`'s zero callers. The corrective rule stated: read `proposals/` and `audit/` before claiming a defect is new.

name: Keys flow OUT and essentially never IN — the substrate is a pure emission-and-transport layer
statement: Across 15 per-subsystem flow skeletons (165 traced inputs, an enforced 7-value `kind` enum), Key-typed inputs are only 7 of 165 (4%), and 6 of those 7 are not real subsystem consumption (substrate self-construction or a subscriber callback receiving its own emission). No gameplay or worldly subsystem takes a Key as an input — what actually shapes a subsystem is caller arguments (30%) and direct world-state reads (25%). This is why nothing loops.

name: An earlier interim claim that gameplay subsystems consume almost nothing was misleading
statement: A prior reading of `module_contracts.yaml`'s declared Key edges alone (combat 2, fieldwork 1, social_contest 1, threadwork 0, mass_battle 0) was "true of declared Key edges and misleading as a general statement": the flow skeletons show social_contest with 17 traced inputs, mass_battle 12, combat 11, threadwork 11 — richly shaped, just not by Keys, which are only 4% of real input flow.

name: Per-subsystem input profile — factions carries the highest state-field count of any subsystem
statement: factions (lane FA): 11 traced inputs, 8 outputs, 23 state fields (the highest of all 15 subsystems), 10 seams, 15 traced gaps, dominant input kind arg/world-state. Settlements (lane SE): 8 in, 7 out, 11 state, 9 seams, 12 gaps, even kind distribution.

name: Characters emits final_state convictions/beliefs that nothing downstream reads
statement: Only two outputs tree-wide are traced as having zero consumers at all: threadwork's `scene.thread_operation`/`meta.thread_woven` (never constructed anywhere despite being declared) and characters' `CampaignResult.final_state['convictions'/'beliefs']` — "nothing reads these two keys downstream."

name: Entity expressiveness — Settlement is named and rich; NPC has no name and five bare axes
statement: Settlement (~20 fields, named, prosperity/defense/order/fort_level/garrison/legitimacy/ popular_support/facility_tier/suspicion/pressure/active_directive/religious_building/ church_attention/governor_emergence). Faction (~11 fields, 7 of 11 booleans, 4 of those per-arc-spent turn-tracking flags). NPC (5 axes, unnamed: stance per issue 1-5, worldview 1-2 of 8 convictions, affiliation+loyalty 0-3, compromise_category, volatility 1-5). "A generated NPC has no name, no relationships, no history, no memory and no goal."

name: names_index.yaml holds 528 entries with no runtime loader — the engine can generate a person and cannot name them
statement: `references/names_index.yaml` holds 528 entries and has no runtime loader anywhere in `engine/` or `systems/`.

name: Authored narrative richness and runtime expressiveness run in opposite directions
statement: `systems/npcs/` holds 20 documents (a 13-character roster with roles/motivations/arc trajectories, foils, character analyses, and a relational graph with 6 authored edge types — sworn-bond, liege-vassal, kinship, patronage, rivalry, feud — each with strain capacity, accrual and break/transition rules), and zero code references any of it. The most heavily designed entity (the NPC) is the least implemented (5 integers, no name); the least designed entity (the settlement) is the most implemented.
baseline_ref: proposals/2026-08-19-subsystem-delta-and-narrative-robustness.md §5, §6 (parallel finding on the authored NPC corpus)

name: The narrative gap and the input-asymmetry gap are the same gap from two sides
statement: A character cannot be shaped by what happens to them when the entity has no field to record it in AND the subsystems resolving their scenes take no Keys as input — events are emitted and never read back into the things they happened to.

name: 15 per-subsystem flow skeletons already exist and are guarded — the input taxonomy should not be re-derived
statement: `systems/*/[a-z]*_flow_skeleton_v1.md` (15 files) already carry §2 IN (input·kind·origin·anchor), §4 OUT, §5 state, §6 seams (with a direction column) and §7 traced gaps, format-contracted at `subsystem_flow_skeletons_v1.md:88-99` and guarded by `test_flow_skeletons.py` (95 passing). The enforced 7-value `kind` enum (key·world-state·arg·param·flag·registry·file) already exists; vocabulary unification over it is under an explicit Jordan hold (ED-IN-0103).

name: acquisition already names a live Varfell territorial mechanic — a word-choice collision
statement: `systems/factions/sim/varfell_territorial_acquisition.py` already uses "acquisition" for a named territorial mechanic — a term collision with any generic "acquisition layer" (kit/school) vocabulary proposed elsewhere in this corpus.

name: npcs subsystem has real code — an earlier "zero .py files" claim was a folder-vs-code error
statement: `npcs_flow_skeleton_v1.md:12-16` traces the `npcs` container's code to `engine/autoload/npc_ai.py` + `systems/world/sim/npe.py`. An earlier claim that "npcs has zero .py files" conflated the empty `systems/npcs/` folder (docs only) with the container's actual implementation, which the flow-skeleton spec forbids by standing rule.

name: The dotted-namespace nomenclature already exists — it was never adopted, not never built
statement: `references/names_index.yaml` has carried 113 dotted identifier keys since before the v40 generation. Measured: of 51 non-proper-noun dotted keys, 16 appear nowhere outside the generated registries, 32 appear only in tooling/tests, and only 3 (`substrate.key`, `fac.intel`, `clock.mending_stability`) appear in engine code or a live design doc — one is genuinely load-bearing, one a single mention, one prose-only. The engine otherwise runs on bare literals like `self.order`, `world.clocks['MS']`.

name: Measured grep-noise for canonical display names — governance/faction terms dominate the worst offenders
statement: Raw corpus hits for ordinary-English canonical names, excluding `deprecated/`: Order 1,630 hits/414 files, Authority 1,366/279, Standing 1,234/285, Discipline 1,151/274, Military 1,092/191, Precedent 635/198, Command 564/136, Legitimacy 513/124. The control group (56 Key types, dotted by construction) has a median of 24 occurrences and zero complaints — proving the namespace, not the corpus size, is what makes a term findable.

name: Three incompatible live namespace axes for identifiers — kind/category, event-domain, owner/scale
statement: Axis A (kind/category, `names_index.yaml`: `clock.ip`, `set.legitimacy`), Axis B (event domain, key type registry: `scene.combat_hit`, `da.public_governance`) and Axis C (owner/scale, Jordan's worked examples: `npc.almud_almqvist`, `settlement.piety_track`, `world.invasion_pressure`) are live and contradict each other where they overlap (e.g. `clock.ip` vs `world.invasion_pressure` name the same value under different prefixes).

name: Recommendation — Axis C for entities/owned-state, Axis B retained for Keys, Axis A retired
statement: Proposal: Axis C (owner/scale) governs entities and owned state (matching Jordan's three worked examples and the "each category/class requires its own nomenclature" instruction); Axis B (event domain) is retained unchanged for Key types, since a Key is an event, not an entity-owned value, and is already measured working (median 24 hits); Axis A is retired.

name: Proposed entity namespace roster
statement: Proposed entity namespaces: `npc.` (46/`npc_registry` or 25/`proper_noun_registry`), `faction.` (6 + 2 subfactions), `settlement.`, `territory.` (17), `realm.` (3), `region.` (2), `people.` (4), `org.` (1).

name: Proposed owned-state namespace roster
statement: Proposed owned-state namespaces: `character.` (9 personal attributes + 3 aggregates, from `attr.*`/`agg.*`); `settlement.` (legitimacy, popular_support, prosperity, defense, order, piety_track, from `set.*`); `faction.` (influence, wealth, military, intel, stability, from `fac.*`); `world.` (6 world clocks, from `clock.*`); `unit.` (power, discipline, command, from `mass.*`); `thread.` (thread_fatigue, unchanged). `settlement.`/`faction.` deliberately overlap entity and owned-state usage (e.g. `settlement.hafenmark` vs `settlement.legitimacy`) — recommended to accept the overlap rather than split into `settlements.`/`settlement.`.

name: piety_track's owner is unresolved across three disagreeing canonical documents
statement: Jordan's own worked naming example assigns `piety_track` to `settlement.`, but `module_contracts.yaml:368` files it under `systems/characters/` and `conviction_track_v30.md:31` calls it a per-territory stat — three canonical sources disagree on the owner independently of the naming proposal itself. This is a design ruling, not a naming one.

name: piety_track / Conviction Track (CV) / Piety Track (PT) are one stat under three names, deferred since 2026-04-17
statement: The stat known as `piety_track`, "Conviction Track (CV)" and "Piety Track (PT)" is one quantity under three names, with a rename deferred as "a P2 cost-benefit decision for a dedicated cleanup pass" since 2026-04-17 (`ED-644`, restated `faction_politics_v30.md:787`).

name: Freeing world. for owned state orphans 62 proper-noun entries that must be re-prefixed in the same pass
statement: `world.` is currently a 62-entry grab-bag holding NPCs, factions, territories, realms and peoples (with the real category demoted to an optional, 30-of-113-populated `token_class:` field). Freeing `world.` for world-scale state (so `world.invasion_pressure` can exist) orphans all 62 entries, which must be re-prefixed in the same pass or the namespace means two things during the interim.

name: Contract-name rename recommended as citation-form-only, not a full field/YAML rename
statement: The 27 module-contract names have a median of 131 bare occurrences and zero qualified uses. A full rename would touch ~10k references and every generated join; recommended instead: citation-form only (`contract.victory` in prose/comments), leaving file and YAML keys untouched.

name: The designated rename executor tool covers almost none of the live corpus
statement: `tools/valoria_rename.py`'s scope (`SCOPE_DIRS = ('designs','params','references','canon')`, extensions `.md/.yaml/.yml/.jsonl/.txt`) covers only 67 of the live tree's relevant files; 270 live-corpus files, 261 `.py` files and 41 `.json` files are silently missed because two of its four scope roots (`designs/`, `params/`) no longer exist and `iter_files()` skips a missing directory with no error. This is named as a pattern defect (CLAUDE.md §0.1 point 5): correct when written, broken when the tree moved.

name: One concept, one ID — the naming-grammar rule proposed for new coinage
statement: Proposed grammar rule 5: "one concept, one ID" — no leaf may accrue a second display name once namespaced (the `piety_track`/CV/PT case is the worked failure this rule targets).

name: Namespace registry proposed as the single owner of new namespace coinage
statement: Phase 1 proposes `references/namespace_registry.yaml` as the single-owned closed roster of namespaces, so a new namespace is an edit to one file rather than a convention that spreads by imitation — explicitly citing the retired index+infill pair (CLAUDE.md §4) as the failure mode to avoid.

name: Phased rollout — report-only landing, then a ratchet burn-down, then blocking at zero
statement: Five-phase lifecycle proposed: Phase 0 rulings (axis + 4 open cases); Phase 1 grammar/roster/ report-only checker; Phase 2 migrate the two registries with alias resolution; Phase 3 adopt in code one subsystem per PR, worst-noise-first (settlements and factions lead); Phase 4 flip the checker to blocking at zero backlog. Reuses the repo's existing A1-A17 report-only→backlog-burn→ block lifecycle rather than inventing a new one.

name: Phase 3 hazard — renaming a field while a writer still assigns the old name silently no-ops the writer
statement: Named explicitly per CLAUDE.md §0.1 point 1: a Phase-3 rename must grep the field's *assignments*, not its readers, and add each renamed field to `test_morale_write_sweep.py`'s `_CELL_OWNED` registry — settlements and factions are named as the worst-noise, first-migrated subsystems and therefore the first exposed to this hazard.

name: parliamentary_bridge runs live every season by default and generates a topic from world pressure
statement: `mc_v18.py:148-151` runs `parliamentary_bridge` every season by default (`ECHO_TRANSPORT` default ON, Jordan 2026-07-08 "the baseline campaign"). `_derive_vote` (`parliamentary_bridge.py:82-97`) generates a motion topic from world pressure (lowest-Stability faction proposes, highest-Mandate defends), and `parliamentary_vote.py:206-216` writes the result back to `world.factions`. This retracts a prior "the contest is sealed off from the world" headline claim — the parliamentary path is live and carries a topic and a write-back, though it is a Mandate-pool roll, not a full rhetorical agôn (no evidence, no claim record, no rhetoric crosses it).

name: ledger_add silently deletes prior Reputation tags — SINGLE_VALUED by kind, ignoring key
statement: `ledger_add` (`ledger.py:31-32,50-53`) treats `Reputation` as `SINGLE_VALUED` by tag *kind*, ignoring `key`, so inserting a new Reputation tag deletes every prior one on the same holder. Tags additionally live on exactly one `Settlement` (`:14-16`), so there is no holder dimension at all — a faction cannot hold a ledger tag. This is a genuinely new primitive gap, not (as an earlier pass claimed) something needing no new mechanism.

name: Ledger holder dimension and reach carrier — two named gaps in the record spine
statement: Two SE-lane gaps in the settlement ledger, beyond the SINGLE_VALUED bug (H3-117): (1) no holder dimension — `Reputation` cannot express "the bench thinks X of you" alongside "the room thinks Y" without a `D[holder][object]` schema change; (2) no reach carrier — `key`/`ttl` give identity and lifetime but not *which* ledgers hold a tag, so a king's precedent cannot be distinguished from a governor's on binding breadth.

name: Ledger mount points proposed — Faction and contest Body both gain a ledger list
statement: Proposal to add `ledger: list` to `Faction` and to the contest `Body`, since `ledger.py`'s functions are already free functions over a plain list and `Settlement` merely holds one — an additive change, not a refactor. Would give factions their first ledger-tag capability (currently zero — H3-117).

name: Proposed faction opposition-memory primitives — aims, redLines, threat, patience
statement: CIP-6 proposes adding to `Faction`: `aims` (2-3 visible goals), `redLines` (unbuyable, announced, structurally bypassable stances, sequenced after a side-payment verb exists), `threat` (an accumulator with concealed magnitude but visible structure, probed by truthful banded reads), and `patience` (a capability gate plus accumulator). Motivated by the current state: `faction_action.py:220` is a single weighted `rng.random()` per season with no cross-season memory, so factions cannot obstruct across seasons or concede.

name: What makes a faction feel like it believes something — four required parts, one already cheap
statement: Four properties are named as jointly necessary for faction "belief" to read as intentional rather than caprice: disposition reads public policy/record state (not a private gift ledger); the preference is immutable (no payment moves the agenda, only the offending state does); the AI pays a real cost for holding the belief; and the reason is voiced at the moment of obstruction. The fourth is named as the cheapest and most valuable to add.

name: FactionBoost's style-reward table is crowd-profile data, not a per-holder opinion table — a rescue error to avoid repeating
statement: `FactionBoost` (`dictionaries.py:386-442`) maps faction → the argument style a room dominated by that faction rewards; it contains no holder, no valence, no opinion about anyone. A prior document rescued it into the wrong track (a per-holder disposition primitive) — recorded here so the error is not repeated. The style-reward die itself has no resolution consumer at all in code (prose-level only).

name: CIP-7a — the mandate gate, a bind() primitive making repudiation risk computable
statement: Proposal: `bind(actor, body, terms)` returns BOUND if `terms.within(mandate.limits)`, else fails — so `repudiationRisk` becomes arithmetic over already-available data (the bodies/offices a deliverable touches, and the actor's standing in each). Addresses the current gap: a personal-scale win binds an entire faction with no check the character could bind anyone, and the only exit today is breach.

name: CIP-7b — the repudiation branch has no published precedent; do not spine it yet
statement: A PROVISIONAL binding the counterparty acts on, later disavowed by the actor's own principal with the counterparty keeping what was transferred (historical precedents: sub spe rati, Versailles), has no published game implementation. Recommended: paper-prototype first, do not build this branch into the spine yet.

name: CIP-7c — the institutional party differs from a person in four measurable, currently-unbuilt ways
statement: An institutional actor (e.g. an inquisition) differs from a person-actor in four measurable ways: (a) ascribed vs. earned standing (the office carries authority the officer did not earn); (b) a dossier assembled over time rather than owned at scene start; (c) a mandate bounding which rungs it may reach (jurisdiction as precondition, not rung); (d) institutional consequence on defeat (the institution's Reputation moves, not only the individual's). (a) has a coupled, unused primitive already: `split_standing` separates ascribed Rank from earned Credit (`resolver.py:200-214`, default off), but Rank's only in-bout consumer is the `hard` verb another proposal in this same document (CIP-13) recommends deleting as strictly dominated — so `split_standing` cannot be rescued and have its only consumer removed at once.

name: CIP-12 — reputation reconciled to one currency with two holders (bench vs. room), consumed strictly post-close
statement: Three previously-independent "second output" candidates (attribution — did the target believe the decision was their own; record kind — which LedgerTag a close emits; room impression — what the audience thinks of you afterwards) are reconciled: record kind is not a currency (it is the shape of an emission, not an independent magnitude), and attribution/room-impression are one quantity read by two holders (bench vs. room) under the ledger's proposed holder dimension (H3-118) — one currency, two holders, priced by margin, consumed strictly post-close so it cannot collapse into the scalar `adv`.

name: CIP-14 — the audience as a party; the crowd/room/bench channel to the world is unbuilt and conditional
statement: Two of three audience-pressure channels are already wired (Room feeds Readiness toward the character; Pressure feeds `_bias` and raises leak toward the adjudicator); the third — audience impressions carried into the world as reputation/respect afterwards — is absent. Proposed: a per-venue crowd taste profile distinct from the bench's, a post-close room-impression emission to the ledger bounded by presence (only factions with someone in the room learn anything), and bench cross-contest reach (a king's ruling binds widely and lasts; a governor's is local and expires) as a ledger reach carrier. Explicitly conditional on CIP-9b (an unratified auto/played fidelity refinement) and CIP-12's ruling (H3-126) — without CIP-9b the two-output close is either inert or an exploitable mode-shop.

name: Cross-lane observation — three CIPs on the ledger/authority spine explicitly touch the SE and FA lanes
statement: The document explicitly marks CIP-1(a)/(d) (ledger mount points and holder dimension) as SE-lane-touching, and CIP-7c(d)/CIP-12's downstream as FA-lane-touching — flagged as observations, not rulings, but load-bearing on any settlement-ledger or faction-record schema change made independently by those lanes.

name: CIP-8 — folding negotiation into the contest gate is only valid once a reservation-value/side-payment verb set exists
statement: `burden = NONE` is ratifiable as the negotiation implementation only once an offer/counter/ side-payment verb set and a reservation-value concealed quantity exist in the move vocabulary; `modes.py:13` already flags negotiation as a scaffold and `NegotiationMode` is stub-wired. Before that, folding negotiation into the gate is a rename, not a consolidation.

name: Reserve-cost exploit flagged as an open fork — support both regains more than it costs and builds ethos
statement: `support` costs 2 Reserve, regains 4, and builds ethos simultaneously (`primitives.py:51-52`, `resolver.py:331-332`) — flagged as fork item 8 needing Jordan: fix cost ≥ regain, or cut the resource.

name: The programme has never been reconciled against a separate ruling capping the irreducible primitive set at eleven
statement: A separate document ("04") ruled the irreducible social-contest primitive set at eleven; this 16-proposal consolidation/integration programme has never been counted against that ruling, flagged as an open fork (§4.9) at the time of writing.

name: The Grounded Event-Card Deck — 58 governance/faction event cards across four research dockets
statement: A 58-card event deck (from 59 generated, one merge) spanning all seven card families (Opportunity, Ambition, Thread, Crisis, Petition, Intrigue, plus family imbalance noted below) and four research dockets (historical-concerns action catalogue, comparative-governance, rise-to-power roster, proactive-governance-scale). Each card carries historical grounding, a trigger predicate, response branches with stat/tag deltas, a three-vector burden, FI/SC/FA ripple gradings, and a named follow-on arc actor. Produced by a 15-agent workflow with a per-cluster adversarial critic (0 CUT / 40 KEEP / 19 REVISE, flagged as a possible under-applied critic stance) plus a cross-cluster synthesis pass.

name: The deck's draw-and-resolve mechanism — one Π-weighted draw engine, three existing resolvers, zero new engines
statement: Every card is drawn by one Π-weighted event-table engine (the deck's single new engine, flagged for canon ratification, carrying one resolution-diagnostic finding — a discrete band-cliff at Π 7→8 flipping Intrigue↔Crisis). Every card's response branches resolve through one of three already-ratified resolvers: `d_sigma` (governor-verb/Directive choices), `deterministic_accounting` (pure state-write Opportunity/Ambition branches), or `dice_pool` (branches that are themselves a contest — Denounce→Tribunal, Verify→up-tier, Parliament motions). No card invents a fourth resolution shape.

name: New governance lever — Consent-Rule (council veto structure), the deck's most-exercised new lever
statement: Proposed lever: a per-council `Consent-Rule` (Unanimity vs. Majority) determining whether a single council member's veto binds. Exercised by three cards (EVT-COURT-06 "The Banked Claim," ECON-03 "Privileged Estates Veto," GOVFRIC-02 "Guildhall Rises" Concord branch) — the deck's most-reused new lever, so its ratification (R-1) gates all three branches.

name: New ledger family — Capital-Posture (Speculative/Debased), backing a monetary-crisis Thread card
statement: Proposed ledger-tag family `Capital-Posture` (states include `:Speculative`, `:Debased`), grounded in the John Law/Mississippi Bubble and French-assignat precedents, backing EVT-XSCALE-07's Bank-Run Thread card (a per-season ticking backing-ratio gap resolving to a peninsula-wide Crisis at threshold) and ECON-01/ECON-04. Awaits Ledger-family ratification (substrate §2.2/§9).

name: New settlement lever — route/corridor Precedent, the deck's most load-bearing R-1 dependency
statement: Proposed lever `route/corridor Precedent` (single-corridor vs. diversified) records that a settlement's Prosperity now hinges on one named chokepoint a rival can target — a quantity Prosperity's magnitude alone cannot express. It is the single most load-bearing R-1 lever dependency in the deck, invoked by 6 cards (CLIM-03, GEO-04, ECON-08, OPP-07, GOVFRIC-01, XSCALE-06).

name: New faction-scale counter — Nepotism-debt, a threshold-triggered systemic backlash mechanic
statement: Proposed: a faction-wide `Nepotism-debt` counter incremented when a term-limited patron installs a protégé by waiving a merit gate (EVT-COURT-08); at threshold it fires a systemic Reform-Backlash demotion wave across all protégé-tagged seats (modelled on the 1692 abolition precedent).

name: Compact ledger family (already-ratified, ED-SE-0019) is the deck's flagship case — irrevocable perpetual terms binding all future officeholders
statement: EVT-OPP-03 ("The Perpetual Endowment," grounded in Fugger's Fuggerei and Pliny's civic endowments) is the flagship illustration of the already-ratified Compact ledger family (ED-SE-0019): accepting the irrevocable terms binds every future holder of the seat via a Compact that can never be unilaterally undone — a cross-tenure externality that a short-tenure purchased-office holder can accept cheaply while leaving the cost on successors.

name: ~50 of 58 cards' faction/social-contest ripple is AT-RISK pending one unauthored hook
statement: Nearly the whole deck (≈50 cards) depends on an unauthored `social_contest` `stakes.source_key` hook to let a Parliament motion cite a card's outcome Key as a contest predicate; until it lands, those cards' SC ripple degrades from "mechanically wired" to "a motion may cite this narratively." Authoring this hook is named the single highest-leverage next step for the deck.

name: 17 cards are gated on the R-1 settlement-lever ratification, unevenly distributed
statement: 17 distinct cards will not fully express until R-1 (new settlement levers) is ratified: StockLevel (2 cards), Assessment tag (3), route/corridor Precedent (6, the most load-bearing — H3-136), Capital-Posture (3, H3-135), Consent-Rule (3, H3-134). Several can partially play on existing stats with the lever branch degraded.

name: A first-playable slice of the deck is fully wired on current canon with no new lever
statement: Seven cards (ECON-02, ECON-06, GEO-06, GOVFRIC-07, COURT-02, COURT-03, GEO-02, OPP-04) resolve all three ripple channels (FI, FA via a real Mandate driver, and SC either wired or gracefully degrading) on machinery that already exists, with no R-1 lever and no §13 hook dependency — recommended as the deck's first vertical-prototype slice.

name: Six FA-ripple claims were corrected inline from an overclaimed Mandate driver to the real one
statement: Eighteen of nineteen critic REVISE verdicts were dependency/overclaim defects, mostly a card claiming its stat delta moved faction Mandate when the moved stat (e.g. Prosperity, Weight) actually feeds Treasury (`Σ Prosperity×10`), not the L/PS aggregate that composes Mandate. All were corrected inline to route through a real L/PS/Standing driver rather than an asserted one (e.g. EVT-OPP-03 and EVT-OPP-08 gained an explicit PS/L delta to make their Mandate claim true).

name: Cross-cluster near-duplicate — two independently-generated Berlin-Blockade enclave cards
statement: GEO-04 and XSCALE-08 are near-duplicate cards — same grounding (Berlin Blockade), same hard-precondition mechanic (a pre-banked Fortify airbase/corridor tier), same three-branch shape — held apart only by which lever each owns (route/corridor Precedent vs. the Fortify-tier gate) and one added arbitration branch. Flagged as a merge candidate the per-cluster critic structurally could not see (it only compared cards within its own cluster).

name: A two-card Ω-d dependency — OPP-03's non-dominance depends on OPP-04 shipping in the same campaign deck
statement: EVT-OPP-03's "accept the irrevocable Compact" branch is only non-dominant because the obligation bites later via EVT-OPP-04; if OPP-04 is not drawn in the same campaign, OPP-03's accept branch reverts to a near-free win, reopening the exact concern the critic pass had closed. The two must ship as a bonded pair, not two independent draws.

name: Card-family imbalance — Crisis is 37% of the deck, Thread is 1 card, Ambition is 4 cards
statement: Crisis cards are 22/58 (37%, over-represented — every high-Π cluster defaulted to Crisis); Thread is 1/58 (only EVT-XSCALE-07 is a true per-season ticking-fuse card, though several other cards contain thread-like fuses filed under their triggering family instead); Ambition is 4/58, too thin to carry the low-Π draw band the Π-gate promises against 6 Opportunity cards competing for the same shelf.

name: Provenance breadth verdict — all four research dockets represented, no docket collapsed
statement: Surviving-card counts by grounding docket: Historical Concerns Action Catalogue 33 cards (climatic 8, geopolitical 9, economic 8, cross-scale 8); Comparative Governance Research 9; Court & Standing Research 8; Proactive Opportunity Research 8 — all four dockets represented, weighted toward the historical-concerns catalogue as the deepest single well.

name: Autocracy Bounded by a Parallel Legitimacy Order
statement: Proposed design hook: flag an AUTOCRATIC_FIAT faction with a non-territorial Legitimacy-adjudication faction (ideological/juridical power_base, e.g. an ulema-equivalent) that can force an L/PS recalculation from outside the scale hierarchy without itself being a chain-bypass veto-holder. Grounded on Ottoman kanun/şeriat, Roman Senate auctoritas, Carolingian synodal canons, Han tingyi.

name: Portfolio-Seat Council With Internal Peer-Blocking Veto
statement: Proposed OLIGARCHIC_COUNCIL variant where each seat carries a distinct portfolio-scoped veto (Ottoman Divan military/fiscal/chancery seats; Roman consular intercessio); a peer-blocking veto gates the Consensus resolver's "holdout" state instead of being majority-tallied.

name: Fixed Indivisible Council Charter
statement: Proposed OLIGARCHIC_COUNCIL configuration with a hard rank-7 seat cap and an indivisibility rule barring seat-splitting across an NPC's heirs, plus a codified rulebook as the settlement's governance charter — modeled on the HRE Golden Bull's 7-elector college and Japan's Hyōjōshū/Shikimoku.

name: Estate-Allocated Sequential-Veto Chamber (NEGOTIATED_ESTATES)
statement: Proposed governance_mode where seats are pre-assigned to named blocs that sign in sequence rather than simultaneously, deliberately modeling a documented representation-lag between an estate bearing obligations and that estate winning a formal vote (HRE Reichstag's three curiae; Japan's shogun-first-among-equals; Florence's guild Signoria).

name: Sortition-Plus-Scrutiny Anti-Capture Selection Pipeline
statement: Proposed multi-round Consensus-resolver pipeline alternating random Key-holder subsets with assent/stand-aside/holdout votes so that capturing an appointment requires controlling every round, not one — modeled on Venice's doge pipeline, Florentine imborsazione, and the papal conclave's Ubi periculum decaying-ration holdout cost.

name: Gated Sponsored Meritocratic-Bureaucratic Ladder
statement: Proposed MERITOCRATIC_BUREAUCRATIC Initiation-Gate with hard minimum-rank-duration and cooldown timers plus a persistent sponsor→Mentor link; a bureaucratic-power_base seat has lower disloyalty liability but accretes patronage into a kinship/military base over time. Grounded on Roman cursus honorum, Han cha ju, Carolingian palace office, and the HRE ministeriales.

name: Governance-Mode Mask vs. Substance Split
statement: Proposed split between a faction's displayed governance_mode (what public Legitimacy calculations show) and its substance mode (the actual decision procedure); the L/PS consent gate reads the displayed mode, leaving the gap between the two exploitable rather than folding "informal capture" into a new taxonomy value. Grounded on Cao Cao's "Han" edicts and Florence's informal Medici principate.

name: Governance-Mode Migration Event
statement: Proposed rule that a polity's governance_mode is legislated and can migrate (e.g. DELIBERATIVE_ASSEMBLY→OLIGARCHIC_COUNCIL) via one ratified charter act, with L/PS gating whether the migration holds — mode as an emergent readout of power_base rather than a fixed per-polity choice. Grounded on Venice's 1297 Serrata, the HRE Golden Bull, and the Roman Dominate.

name: Chain-Bypass Authority by Accretion, Purchase, Negation, or Leash
statement: Proposes that a Monarch-tier chain-bypass authority be reachable four ways — accreting nominally-separate grants (Augustus), lump purchase of a title (Milan), a nullify-not-compel negative veto (Roman tribune), or a "leashed monarch" configuration requiring a companion co-signature Key before a directive resolves (Venice's Doge).

name: Dual Co-Resident Authority Tracks With Dormant-but-Live Crown
statement: Proposes a Monarch/Parliament bypass pair modeled as two simultaneous L/PS tracks on the same settlement (e.g. bakufu administration vs. court legitimacy in Japan, or HRE election-plus-papal-ratification), where a cascade resolves only when both agree; the Crown consent-gate never fully zeroes even under total practical eclipse and can snap back given a large enough two-signal collision (non-MoH grounding: Roman Senate reassertion).

name: Consent-Gate Decoupled From the Seat, With Dual-Signal Audit
statement: Proposes modeling L/PS as procedure/oath-sourced consent separate from formal authority (Roman auctoritas, Carolingian 802 oath + paired lay/ecclesiastical missi, Venetian Avogadori), plus a Demotion-Trigger requiring two independent audit channels to concur, with an auditor able to retroactively null an improperly-obtained standing gain.

name: Recognition-Fission and Rank-as-Secession-Blast-Radius
statement: Proposes chartering a diverged population into a bounded sub-faction with one Crown-facing liaison (defensive fission, Ottoman millet), letting the Crown compel partition of a rival's holdings (offensive fission, Han Tui'en Ling / Liu Yan), and keying secession blast-radius off the scope of granted authority rather than nominal rank, so mass-demoting high-rank immediate actors yields an empire-wide fracture (HRE 1803 mediatization).

name: Standing Ladder as a Display Aggregate Over a Debasable Currency
statement: Proposes the faction-politics 0–7 Standing ladder be authored with dual Initiation-Gates (age AND election) plus a cooldown pair (biennium/decennium), per the Roman cursus honorum, Venice's Balla d'Oro→Doge cursus, and the HRE Golden Bull's seven-tier hierarchy — the number is a display aggregate over an underlying, debasable currency, not ground truth.

name: Resolution-Quality to Standing Bridge (Delivered vs. Demanded Gap)
statement: Proposes the primary non-Mandate-of-Heaven legitimacy source: a Directive/Need delivered-vs-demanded arithmetic gap automatically grants or strips Standing rank, in both directions. Grounded on Roman lex repetundae, Carolingian missi, HRE Reichsexekution, Han field-promotion/impeachment, Japanese honryō-andō/ shin-on, and Ottoman itimad.

name: Power_Base-Typed Vulnerability — Kin-Severed Trades Velocity for Ceiling
statement: Proposes that a kin-severed power_base (Ottoman kul/devshirme, Roman equestrians, Venice's Cancellier Grande, Han cha ju) buys uncapped advancement velocity at the cost of a total-clawback demotion ceiling, while kinship power_base buys survivability (containment, not confiscation) at a lower ceiling — the trade is explicit and symmetrical.

name: Demotion Magnitude Graded by How the Seat Was Won
statement: Proposes a Demotion Magnitude scale keyed to the seat's power_base — clawback (confiscation) for favor-derived seats, containment (exile, cage) for kinship-derived ones. Grounded on Florence's four demotion tiers, Han's relegation/forced-suicide/zu-extermination ladder, Japan's kaieki/kunigae/exile, and Ottoman müsadere/Kafes.

name: High-Rank Fall Reverberates — Reaggregation Can Add a Seat
