statement: `name_collision_database.yaml:421-425` renames "Authority (pressure point)" → "Sanction," directly colliding with the live 5-tier "Parliamentary Sanction" ladder specified at faction_layer_v30 §5.4. A vocabulary fix for one collision manufactured a second, distinct term collision on the same word.
status_evidence: proposals/2026-08-23-MASTER-vocabulary-and-rulings.md:270 ("the prescribed fix manufactures a new collision")

name: Retracted degree ladder (net >= 2*Ob) still present in prose
statement: factions_personal_v30.md:423 states the Seasonal-Accounting Stability check's "Overwhelming (net >= 2× Ob)" — the exact RETRACTED degree ladder the live resolver superseded. The current single owner (`engine/autoload/dice_engine.py::degree_from_net`) uses margin bands (Overwhelming margin>=3, Success>=1, Partial [0,1), Failure<0), ratified 2026-08-14. Every live degree table this lane's code actually consumes (mass_seizure.py, tribunal.py, all crown_initiative/absolution/council/excommunication calls) correctly routes through the live ladder via dice_engine/roll_pool; only this prose line still states the debunked formula.

name: READY" in faction_systems_overview_v30 means canon-ready, not code-built
statement: faction_systems_overview_v30 (2026-05-17, "Pass 2 follow-up") labels charter_of_liberties "READY (mechanic-canon; flavor frame in identity-territory)" and hafenmark_equipment/altonian_reinforcements similarly "READY"/"READY mechanism" — but as of the current code state, charter_liberties.py and hafenmark_equipment.py are pure zero-logic stubwire stubs, and altonian_reinforcements does not exist anywhere in systems/factions/sim/'s 17 modules. "READY" in this document's vocabulary meant "canon spec exists to build from," not "code exists" — a reader relying on this document's status column without checking the actual sim/ tree would believe these are implemented.

name: Casus Belli source-list mismatch across two "canonical" enumerations
statement: faction_systems_overview_v30 §4.6 enumerates "8 CB sources canonized in parliamentary_transfer_v30.md §3" as: Adjacent Instability, Treaty Violation, Excommunication-current, Religious Building Desecration, Crown Diktat, Combined-Standing Threshold, Conviction Scar Accumulation, RM Adjacent-Movement Pressure. The document it cites, parliamentary_transfer_v30.md §3, actually lists a DIFFERENT 8: Crown constitutional restoration, Adjacent instability, Einhir Revival Partial, Parliamentary Transfer Partial, Military Conquest, Treaty-violation, Excommunication-related, Conviction Scar accumulation. Only 3 of the 8 names overlap cleanly (Adjacent Instability, Treaty-violation, Conviction Scar); "Religious Building Desecration," "Crown Diktat," "Combined-Standing Threshold," and "RM Adjacent-Movement Pressure" appear nowhere in the cited source.

name: Dual/conflicting `## Status:` lines across faction docs
statement: Five files in this lane carry a header `## Status: CANONICAL` immediately followed (or preceded) by a second, contradicting status line — faction_canon_v30.md (CANONICAL then "PROVISIONAL — pending ratification"), faction_behavior_v30.md (header CANONICAL, footer "PROVISIONAL pending ratification"), faction_succession_split_v30.md (header CANONICAL, body "PROVISIONAL — approved mechanical design"), fractional_province_ ownership_v30.md (identical pattern), and baralta_crown_claim_v30_infill.md's parent (DESIGN, flagged for review). A reader/tool taking the FIRST status line — which the 2026-08-24 vocab-rulings doc independently confirms is the common failure mode — reads all five as settled canon when every one is still provisional.
status_evidence: proposals/2026-08-23-MASTER-vocabulary-and-rulings.md:216 ("the doc-status count is unreliable because several files carry two Status lines and every reader takes the first — faction_canon_v30.md reads as CANONICAL while its second line says PROVISIONAL")

name: GD-2 "mandatory threat-response" claim does not match code
statement: faction_action.py's module docstring, engine/mc_v18.py's caller docstring, and excommunication.py's module header (twice) all claim "GD-2: mandatory threat-response before stochastic selection." The code implements no unconditional mandatory pass — RNG-free signals only re-weight the probabilities of a SINGLE stochastic draw (`roll = rng.random()`); a faction with a live conquest opportunity or an available Excommunication target is not guaranteed to act on it. The false claim is propagated into generated tooling (tools/build_execution_map.py) that inherited the wording verbatim — a self-perpetuating misdescription across 5 sites.

name: __init__.py module roster is stale (missing tribunal, home_sanctuary)
statement: The package docstring names only 14 modules; the directory holds 16 real modules (17 counting __init__.py itself) — `tribunal.py` and `home_sanctuary.py` are both omitted, despite home_sanctuary being one of the six pure-stub modules the docstring would otherwise be expected to enumerate alongside its five listed siblings (charter_liberties, hafenmark_equipment, infrastructure_reclamation, varfell_mandate_action, varfell_territorial_acquisition).

name: Emitted Keys with zero live subscribers despite "consumer" comments
statement: `scene.battle_concluded` (faction_action.py, every Conquest) and `da.public_governance` (parliamentary_transfer.py, every successful Transfer) are emitted every time their trigger fires, with in-code comments claiming "FOUR consumers" / "consumed by faction_layer" respectively — but `engine/cross_scale/articulation.py`'s `_TRIGGER_TYPE_IDS` (the only Key-subscription registry found) lists 13 other types and neither of these two. Both emissions cite `references/key_graph.json` DECLARATIONS, not runtime wiring. Both are log-only (no `apply=`) so this is inert telemetry, not a silent behavior bug — but it is a declared-vs-wired divergence in a doc that otherwise reads as confirming real cross-subsystem traffic.

name: cascade_resolution / mission_shift substrate Key types have no resolver
statement: `references/module_contracts.yaml` claims a `faction_state` resolver for `mechanical.cascade_resolution` / `mechanical.mission_shift` accounting logic (the entire PP-686 v2 Mission/Cascade machinery — H5-027, H5-028). Neither type has any Python implementation anywhere in the tree: `cascade_resolution` appears ONLY in its own key-types export declaration, never consumed; `mission_shift` is declared and consumed only as a subscription-constant list entry in `articulation.py` (a consumer registration, not resolver logic).

name: coronation_renewal_prereq docstring asserts an unimplemented check
statement: The docstring for coronation_renewal_prereq asserts Coronation is blocked "when Crown is BOTH excommunicated AND the Church just attempted to excommunicate this same season" — but the function body implements no such joint check, only testing whether `church` is present and parliamentary. The same-season block described never fires.

name: Mass Battle terrain always None at the faction seam
statement: _try_conquest hardcodes `terrain=None` on every call to resolve_mass_battle; per faction_systems_overview_v30 §4.5 this is one of four open forward-flags on the conquest resolution path, deferred to "Phase 7 follow-on Steps 2-9."
baseline_ref: catalogue §356 ("Terrain modifiers at the faction→battle seam")

name: Compound cascade dispatch — sentinel can surface as a fake outcome
statement: The four faction_take_action dispatch buckets are independent `if roll < cum_X:` statements, not `elif`. Because thresholds are non-decreasing, a roll landing in an early bucket whose branch returns the `_NOOP` sentinel falls through EVERY remaining bucket to the terminal, unconditional `_try_govern` call at S2.7 — whose own return is never checked by the caller (faction_take_action's return string is itself discarded at the mc_v18.py call site). `_try_govern` returns the same sentinel when the faction holds no territories or its rolled target's owner mismatches, so the top-level dispatch can in principle surface the bare string 'invalid' as if it were a real action outcome. Currently unreachable in practice (the caller gates out factions with no territories, and the one territory-transfer site that could desync Faction.territories from Territory.owner has zero production callers) — a latent defect protected only by an unrelated caller-side gate, not by any guard in the resolver chain itself.

name: Only 2 of 8 faction sheets authored in faction_canon_v30 PART B
statement: faction_canon_v30's Part B ("FACTION SHEETS") only contains fully-authored sheets for Crown and Church of Solmund — Hafenmark, Varfell, Guilds, Restoration Movement, Löwenritter, and the Ministry of the Peninsula have no consolidated PART-B sheet in this document at all, despite §11 "Partial Sheet Handling" and the Decision Log discussing all of them as if the consolidation were comprehensive.

name: Franchise proposal would replace faction.I, a heavily-used built field, with zero code migration
statement: franchise_v30.md §7.3 explicitly proposes that "the old Influence scalar... becomes `base_influence` — a legacy fallback" and that every Domain Action roll pool currently reading `faction.influence` should read a computed `national_influence()` instead. `faction.I` is read directly and unweighted by essentially every faction-unique action in the live sim (H5-014 Great Work, H5-017 Absolution via I, H5-019 Mass Seizure via I, H5-020 Parliamentary Transfer via I, H5-013 Royal Progress via I). This is a DRAFT-status proposal to structurally replace one of the six most pervasively-used fields in the entire codebase, with no migration path, no code changes, and an explicitly BLOCKING open item (§8: three-way stat mismatch between stats_1_7_scale.md, VDL, and this doc's own Church TI worked example) unresolved.

name: Card-economy action model structurally incompatible with the live stochastic model
statement: ci_political_v30 §5's card-hand+cooldown action economy (each faction has a fixed typed-card hand gating which Domain Action categories it may play, with per-card 1-2-season cooldowns) is a categorically different action-selection architecture from faction_action.py's live weighted-stochastic single-draw model (H5-012): the code has no concept of a card hand, no per-action-type inventory, and no cooldown track at all. Neither document acknowledges the other's existence or supersedes it.

name: Excommunication PC-succession clause references a mechanism absent from v18 schema
statement: factions_personal_v30.md §8.3's PC-excommunication clause (PP-244) specifies the faction "reverts to institutional tendency (GM-run)" — a Leader-vs-Institution two-layer behavioral model (institutional tendency vs. leadership deviation) that has no representation anywhere in game_state.py's Faction dataclass or any sim module; there is no player/NPC leader concept, no "institutional tendency" AI mode, and no handoff logic in the live engine at all.

name: Settlement (primitive)
statement: The Settlement dataclass is the base civic/political unit: sid, name, stype, province_id, owner_faction, governor_id, prosperity/defense/order (0-5), legitimacy/popular_support (0-7), facility_tier, suspicion, pressure, active_directive, religious_building, church_attention, governor_emergence, subnational dict, npc_ids, ledger (list of LedgerTag), open_needs, deck_state.

name: Settlement.ap (Administration Points, computed)
statement: Administration Points per season = 2 + facility_tier, +1 if the settlement type is Seat, Cathedral, or Cathedral-City. Governs how many AP a governor can spend on governance verbs that season.

name: AP formula (verbatim)
formula: ap = 2 + facility_tier + (1 if stype in ('Seat','Cathedral','Cathedral-City') else 0)
statement: The literal expression backing Settlement.ap, diffable against the design prose's AP = 2 + FacilityTier_s(0-3), Standing-5 +1 clause.

name: Province Accord derivation (floor-mean settlement Order)
formula: province_accord = floor(mean(settlement.order for settlement in province_members))
statement: Province Accord is the floor of the mean Order across a province's real settlement members; with zero members it returns 0. Live and read by a report-only drift probe at season end.

name: Ledger tag family collision — Leverage (code) vs Compact (design)
statement: ledger.py's TAG_KINDS = {Precedent, Grudge, Debt, Reputation, Leverage} while governance_play_redesign_v1.md §1.6 names the fifth family Compact (a fixed-term extraction agreement, ED-SE-0019), not Leverage. Code and canon disagree on what the fifth tag family is; settlement_generator_v1.md §4 later reconciles this by treating Compact as a recurring Debt subtype rather than a sixth family, but the code still literally carries Leverage, not Compact.

name: Institutional Facility Tiers (PP-661)
statement: Seat-type and certain City-type settlements offer bounded Institutional Facility slots (Wing/Suite/Chamber/Billet, by Hall Tier) that the controlling faction allocates to rank-holders; slots are finite and new rank-holders receive "pending" status when full.

name: Facility slot capacity by settlement type
formula: Seat: 3 Wing/5 Suite/8 Chamber; City: 1/3/5; Town: 0/1/3; Fortress: 0/1/4; Cathedral: 1/3/5; Port: 0/1/3; Mine/Outpost: 0/0/1; Billet unlimited everywhere
statement: Per-settlement-type ceiling on Wing/Suite/Chamber facility slots (Billet is unlimited/shared everywhere).

name: Capacity Pressure as Political Mechanic (Prince-in-Waiting fork)
statement: When facility capacity is full and a new claimant reaches the rank threshold, one of three forced resolutions fires: an existing Wing-holder departs; the settlement expands capacity via the Expand Institutional Capacity Domain Action; or the claimant accepts Prince-in-Waiting provisional rank, requiring a season Disposition-pool social contest vs Ob 2 to maintain inner-circle standing, reverting to the prior rank on failure.
formula: Prince-in-Waiting maintenance check: Disposition pool vs Ob 2, each season without a Wing

name: Cross-Faction Wing Allocation
statement: At composite-control Seat settlements, Wing slots belong to the settlement's direct controller rather than the province's controller; cross-faction Wings may be ceded as treaty concessions, counting against the ceding faction's capacity while the allied faction occupies them.

name: Church Settlement Infrastructure — Four Independent Axes
statement: Church presence in a settlement is four independent binary/tiered axes rather than a linear tier: Religious Building (None/Chapel/Church/Cathedral, PT bonus scaling with tier), Templar Station (binary, +1 CI/season, can interrupt rival Domain Actions), Inquisitor Base (binary, surveillance + RM Ob penalty + Church Attention generation), and Church Governor (binary, uses Church faction stats for settlement governance). Axes combine in any valid configuration.

name: Seizure Ob Modifiers (stacking, capped)
formula: Seizure Ob modifier = Chapel -0, Church -1, Cathedral -2, Templar -1, Inquisitor -1, Church Governor -2; cap -4 per settlement
statement: Stacking Ob discount for a Mass Seizure declaration against a settlement, one term per Church infrastructure axis present, capped at -4 total.

name: Parish Social Services (Order/Stability bonus)
formula: Chapel +0.5 Order/season; Church +1 Order one-time at installation; Cathedral +1 Order one-time + Order-decay -1
statement: Church buildings provide a stability bonus to their settlement regardless of who controls the Church presence — instrumentally useful to secular governors (the 'Geneva trap').

name: Pastoral Assumption (Church Governor vacuum-fill)
statement: When a settlement has no governor and holds at least a Chapel, the Church may install a Church Governor as a Domain Action at Ob 1 (vs the normal governor-assignment Ob); revocation by the province faction costs Ob = Church Influence ÷ 2, Order -1, Disposition -2 with Church.

name: Settlement Legitimacy/Popular Support → Faction Mandate (LPS-2e ruling)
statement: Jordan ruling (2026-05-30): Legitimacy (L) and Popular Support (PS), 0-7, are per-SETTLEMENT political-acceptance values, not faction-level stats; faction Mandate is the size-weighted aggregate of them with a stabilizing feedback from Mandate back to settlement L/PS. This supersedes the faction-level L/PS canonized in PP-686 v2 (faction_behavior_v30 etc.) at the faction grain — those had the right stats and blend, wrong level.
status_evidence: systems/settlements/sim/registry.py:69-73 (legitimacy/popular_support declared, "NEVER READ OR WRITTEN anywhere in sim/")

name: Settlement Weight (W_s)
formula: W_s = base(Type) + Prosperity_s + FacilityTier_s
statement: Settlement Weight operationalizes population/importance for Mandate weighting: base(Type) — Seat/City/Cathedral 3, Town/Fortress/Port 2, Village/Mine/Outpost 1 — plus current Prosperity (0-5) plus highest FacilityTier present (0-3). Range 1 (undeveloped Outpost) to 11 (fully- developed Seat).

name: Faction Mandate (size-weighted saturating aggregate)
formula: q_s = 0.5*L_s + 0.5*PS_s; T = Σ_s W_s*(q_s/7); Mandate = clamp(round(7*T/(T+K)), 0, 7), K=6
statement: Faction Mandate is a saturating, size-weighted aggregate of held settlements' acceptance — diminishing returns per additional settlement, bounded 0-7 for any holding, with K=6 as the calibrated saturation constant (Stage-4 sim).

name: Mandate → settlement L/PS mean-reverting feedback
statement: Each Accounting, held settlements drift toward the faction's Mandate: a settlement whose q_s sits ≥1 below Mandate gets L +1 (capped 7); ≥1 above gets PS -1 (capped 0); at most ±1 per settlement per season within the ±2 faction-stat seasonal cap. Negative (stabilizing) feedback, confirmed bounded/convergent over 30 seasons in a Stage-4 sim.

name: L/PS wiring buildable spec (E5) — consent-gate + write-side
statement: A worked, buildable pipeline to wire the inert per-settlement L/PS into sim/: pure aggregation functions mirroring registry.province_*, a designed consent-gate (compliance(s) throttling realized Treasury/AP by acceptance, plus a HELD/CONTESTED/SLIPPING state machine driving independence after 2 consecutive SLIPPING Accountings), five write-side sources accrued into pending_dLPS and applied once at the Accounting boundary, and a fixed five-step D.6-disjoint data-flow sequence (snapshot → accrue → apply → aggregate → gate → consume).

name: Consent-gate compliance formula
formula: compliance(s) = clamp((q(s) - Q_FLOOR)/(Q_FULL - Q_FLOOR), 0, 1), Q_FLOOR=1.0, Q_FULL=6.0
statement: Designed local-attenuation factor throttling a settlement's realized Treasury/AP contribution to its controlling faction by its own acceptance level q(s) — the mechanical answer to scale_hierarchy_v1 §4's unwritten consent mechanic.

name: Slip state machine (control_state)
formula: HELD if q>=3; CONTESTED if 1<=q<3; SLIPPING if q<1; 2 consecutive SLIPPING Accountings -> Independence roll
statement: A per-settlement ordinal control_state derived from q(s) each Accounting; sustained SLIPPING for two consecutive Accountings triggers an Independence check (scale_hierarchy §5.2), reusing the built insurgency-pipeline's 2-season formation cadence rather than inventing a parallel one.

name: Settlement registry (37 settlements, 14 provinces, 3 duchies)
statement: Canonical registry: 35 Kingdom settlements across 14 provinces in 3 duchies, plus two special cases (Himmelenger Church city-state, Schoenland foreign tributary island) bringing the adjacency-graph total to 37; Askeheim has 0 settlements. Types span Seat/City/Town/Fortress/ Port/Cathedral/Mine/Outpost/Village/Fortress-City/Cathedral-City.

name: Sub-features registry (30+ properties of parent settlements)
statement: Sub-features (districts, garrison towns, watchtowers, mines, lodges, shrines, harbors, gates, ruins) are not separate settlements or siege-targets; they confer mechanical effects (Defense, Population, Wealth, vision range) to their parent settlement. Two Askeheim features (Ruins, Gate) attach to no settlement.

name: Two-Tier Authority Model (Provincial Authority vs Settlement Governor)
statement: Every settlement has two authority slots — Provincial Authority (the province-controlling national faction: military, taxation, legal framework) and Settlement Governor (local governance, economic development, local NPC relationships) — whose disagreement is the dual-authority engine's source of tension.

name: Governor eligibility ladder points at retired rank names
statement: settlement_layer_v30 §3.2 gates governor eligibility by Standing on the retired 0-5 titles (Operative/Agent, Counselor, Lieutenant, Successor); faction_politics_v30 PP-660 replaced the Standing ladder with 0-7 and different names, so the governor eligibility table now points at ranks that no longer exist.

name: Old four-verb governance menu (Develop/Fortify/Pacify/Administer)
statement: The pre-redesign governance menu: one free governance action per season choosing among Develop, Fortify, Pacify, Administer, each a single stat-pump roll. Explicitly superseded by governance_play_redesign_v1's AP-budgeted verb menu; retained only as the fallback baseline until the redesign lands.

name: Bishop-Governor (Church Ecclesiastical Appointment)
statement: A special governor type installed via Church Ecclesiastical Appointment; Bishop-governors follow the Church NPC Priority Tree rather than the controlling faction's tree, and settlement governance transfers to the Church on appointment, which can fractionalize the province if the resulting controller differs from the Seat holder.

name: Subnational Faction Governance table
statement: Seven subnational-faction archetypes each naturally align with certain settlement types and apply a distinct management effect when granted control (Church +1 Piety, Guilds +1 Trade, Ministry Order-decay -1, Löwenritter Defense +1, RM CV -1 potential in low-PT territories only, Wardens 1-band-earlier RS detection, Niflhel covert +1D intel-gathering — Niflhel is later struck/dissolved).

name: RM Cell Resilience
formula: if RM Presence in >=3 settlements/province: Church/Crown suppression +1 Ob; stacks with Inquisitor surveillance +1 Ob
statement: A distributed RM cell network gains suppression resistance (+1 Ob to suppress) once present in 3+ settlements of a province, modeling that no single arrest destroys a distributed network; composes with the separate Inquisitor surveillance Ob penalty for organizing.

name: Charters, prescription, and Quo Warranto
formula: Revocation Ob = (subnational Influence / 2, round up) + floor(charter_age_seasons / 8)
statement: Granting subnational management writes a durable Charter tag that ages, hardening privilege into right; revoking a Charter older than ~16 seasons is a public Quo Warranto social contest rather than a flat Domain Action, and on success additionally applies Order -1 peninsula-wide in every settlement that faction-type manages (the "London 1683" contagion effect).

name: Za model — patron-backed privilege lapse
statement: A Guild-managed settlement's Charter may carry a patron field (an NPC/institution whose standing backs the guild's privileges); if the patron's standing drops below threshold, the Charter's privileges lapse automatically at the next Accounting with no Quo Warranto contest — a "Patron's Rivals Move" Intrigue card fires one season prior, offering a Treat-verb Bargain window to shore up the patron.

name: The Seggio Council (hereditary corporate subnational faction)
statement: A new subnational-faction archetype at Seat/City settlements: the province faction may recognize 1-5 hereditary Seggio bodies, each holding one bespoke non-transferable privilege (gating a specific verb's funding option, or sole-adjudicating a dispute class); all resident Seggi share a single joint Eletti-bloc council seat the governor must Treat with collectively. Seggio privilege cannot be granted/revoked via the standard Domain Action or Quo Warranto — only inherited, married into, or seized by force.

name: Settlement Events table (§4.3)
statement: Each settlement generates 0-1 local events per season keyed on its stats/type — Dearth, Raid/Siege, Local Revolt (Order 0), Flourishing (Order 5+Prosperity 4+), RM Governance Transition, Consensus Delay, Religious event, Resource surplus, Garrison mobilization — feeding the Priority-4 Scene Slate; generalized into the event deck by governance_play_redesign Part 2.

name: Dearth chain and governor response verbs
statement: Dearth fires on entitlement failure (Prosperity 0, a cut grain route, or a Levy/Extraction stance taken at Prosperity <=1), grounded in the moral-economy literature (Thompson, Scott, Sen). Five governor response verbs — Open Granary, Fix Prices, Requisition, Ignore, Provision — each with a distinct PS/Order tradeoff; a new per-settlement granary field is required in the Settlement dataclass but is not yet added.

name: Grain routes and food dependency
statement: A rule layered on top of the existing settlement-adjacency graph: breadbasket provinces and Port settlements are grain sources; every other settlement needs a traced route (per-province granularity by default) to a source; cutting the route via occupation/blockade/siege of a waypoint puts every dependent settlement one season from Dearth — closing the "Hafenmark food dependency has no mechanical teeth" open item by making unreachability bite.

name: Thread Operations at Settlement Level
formula: Weaving Order+1 / Pulling fail Order-1 / Past-Pulling fail Prosperity-1 / Dissolution fail Defense-1&Order-1 / Mending Prosperity+1 / Community Organizing (PT<=2) Order+1&Prosperity+1 / Lock Defense+1; cap ±1/settlement stat/season
statement: Relational+ scale Thread operations performed in a settlement produce settlement-level stat consequences alongside province-level MS effects, capped at ±1 per settlement stat per season.

name: Local Actors (Throughline T7)
statement: Each settlement generates 1-2 lightweight non-faction Local Actor NPCs (Elder/Magistrate/ Merchant/Priest/Artisan/Farmer/Fisher/Miner/Scholar/Healer) with one Conviction and a Disposition track (starting +1 toward the governor, 0 to others), providing free Depth-1 information and serving as a recruitment pool for faction emergence at Disposition +3; ~45-50 total across 36 settlements by settlement-type count table.

name: Black Markets / Intelligence Brokers / Thread Exploitation Sites (settlement-scale Niflhel successors)
statement: Three location-based emergent phenomena replacing the struck Niflhel faction: Black Markets (Order<=1 or no governor → Wealth +0.5, Accord -0.5), Intelligence Brokers (discoverable named NPCs at Prosperity>=3 with weak governance), and Thread Exploitation Sites (Thread Proximity<=2, harvestable for Wealth at RS cost).

name: Settlement Assault/Siege/Bypass
statement: Invading a province requires capturing or bypassing its settlements one at a time along the internal road network; Assault resolves a battle immediately, Siege ticks defender Order -1 per season until surrender at Order 0, and Bypass (Military > Defense by 2+) leaves the settlement hostile with a garrison sortie risk against the invader's supply line.

name: Fortress chokepoint bypass rule
formula: Fortress cannot be bypassed unless attacker Military exceeds Fortress Defense by 3+
statement: A Fortress settlement forces engagement unless the attacker's Military exceeds its Defense by 3 or more (e.g. Defense-4 Lowenskyst needs Military 7+ to bypass).

name: Surrender on Terms vs Storm (FA-6)
statement: On attacker victory, two conquest branches per Grotius's law-of-war distinction — (a) Accept surrender on terms, available only when the defender is not routed (battle degree Success, not Overwhelming), with a lighter Accord penalty, an L-seed via Entry Terms, and partial garrison preservation; or (b) Storm, always available, with the harsher existing Accord penalty and battle damage. Which branch the attacker's AI picks is owned by faction_action.py, not specified here; exact magnitudes are ED-FA-0013's to set.

name: Garrison effective Defense
formula: effective_Defense = settlement.Defense + garrison.Discipline
statement: A settlement's garrison Discipline adds directly to its Defense for Assault-check purposes; Defense-0 ungarrisoned settlements auto-capture on any hostile entry.

name: Entry Terms at control transfer
formula: Confirm Privileges: Charter kept, L seeds 3, fiscal Standard-capped 4 seasons; Impose Administration: Charter stripped, L seeds 1, no cap, Order -1
statement: On every settlement control transfer, the new controller chooses one of two forks that seed the settlement's L value — Confirm Privileges (legitimacy-buying, Joyeuse-Entrée style) or Impose Administration (roving-bandit pricing, Olson 1993); L is seeded, never incremented, and composes with (does not stack with) the separate succession-drift rule at §1.8b.

name: The Stature Ladder (Renown/Standing → governance scope)
statement: Renown 0-10 and Standing 0-5 map to a five-rung governance-scope progression from Operative (personal actions only) through Settlement Governor, Multi-Settlement, Provincial Authority, to National Actor — the spine for both officer-governance and player faction-emergence.

name: Faction Emergence — Local to National
statement: A five-stage bottom-up faction-founding process (Cell → Organization → Movement → Faction → Hegemon), each stage gated by settlement-holding and Renown thresholds, culminating in a full faction stat sheet at Stage 4 with specified starting values (ED-790: L2/PS3/I=floor(Renown/2)/ W=2+(settlements-1) capped 5/Mil1/Int2/Sta3).

name: Faction Collapse — National to Local
statement: A national faction that loses all provinces contracts to a city-state (partial stat sheet, no Mandate/Military unless garrisoned) if its leader survives in a personally-controlled settlement, and fully dissolves — settlements becoming unmanaged, officers becoming free agents — only if the leader dies/is captured with no Standing-4+ successor.

name: Clock Recalibration for 10-30 year games
statement: Extended-game clock rates: MS decay unchanged, CI unchanged-conditional, Invasion Pressure halved to +1/2 seasons, plus a new Generational Shift clock (0-10, +1 per 5 years) aging founding faction leaders at three thresholds (attribute penalties, succession-arc activation, ultimate elderhood) with an Ibn Khaldun asabiyyah-cycle rationale.

name: Settlement/province succession (extended)
statement: On governor death/removal, the province faction must assign a replacement or the settlement becomes unmanaged (Order -1/season); a leader succession's effect on held-settlement L is specified at §1.8b; a cross-generational protégé handoff lets the player transfer governance and start a new character at Standing 0 inheriting Renown/2 (round down).

name: Province Accord edge cases (ED-SETT-03)
statement: Resolved editorial ruling: single-settlement province Accord equals that settlement's Order; multi-settlement is floor-average with ties broken by the Seat getting +1 weight.

name: Settlement Flow Skeleton — code-traced ground truth
statement: A code trace (not design) of every settlement entry point: `populate_from_geography` runs at world-gen; `province_accord` has exactly one production caller (a report-only drift probe); `succeed_governor`, `governor_id`, `npc_ids`, `active_directive`, `.ap`, the Ledger, and `build_infrastructure`'s write side all have ZERO production callers anywhere in engine/, systems/, or tests/ — the schema is complete and nothing reads it. Confirms the personnel_muster baseline's "chassis built, entirely inert" finding at path:line granularity.

name: Two independent, uncoordinated settlement-scale entities per province
statement: World.territories (built from STARTING_OWNER/STARTING_ACCORD constants) and World.settlements (built from valoria_geography_v30.yaml via populate_from_geography) are populated from two different sources in the same create_world() call, with no code cross-validating them beyond a report-only drift-probe counter (accord_drift_probe_hits) that never writes either value.

name: Accord Echo settlement-write leg is wired but organically dormant
statement: echo_transport's Accord-Echo path can write Settlement.order via a deferred Key, but it only fires if a caller explicitly declares echo['scene_outcome']; no live producer in the campaign loop sets that key, so the write leg never fires in a seeded campaign — exercised only by direct unit tests.

name: religious_building — two same-named, differently-keyed fields
statement: Settlement.religious_building (registry.py) round-trips through serialization but is never set by populate_from_geography nor read by any logic — logically dead. The live field of the same name is a different store entirely: InfrastructureState.religious_building, written by build_infrastructure and read by count_infrastructure/seizure_ob_modifier. Same name, two unrelated stores.

name: settlement_layer module_contracts entry names the wrong (dead) file
statement: references/module_contracts.yaml's settlement_layer contract's declared sim_module is settlement.py — an orphan with zero importers anywhere — while the live registry code (registry.py, which actually runs at world-gen and every season) has no contract entry of its own.

name: Ledger has no production writer
statement: LedgerTag/ledger_add/ledger_sweep and Settlement.add_tag/has_tag/tags are fully implemented, but the only call sites anywhere outside ledger.py/registry.py themselves are the tools/sim_harness prototype adapters (retired 2026-08-21, never CI-wired); succeed_governor — the one entry point that would trigger a sweep — itself has no production caller.

name: Governor's Turn verb menu (Develop/Fortify/Keep Order/Hold Court/Sponsor/Treat/Levy/Investigate/Retain Clerks/Survey/Negotiate Quota/Bind the Cells/Ordenanza/Petition-Defy)
statement: See baseline for the full per-verb AP/roll/Ob/effect/tradeoff table; no code exists for any of these verbs.

name: Ledger of Consequence — five tag families (design side)
statement: Precedent (biases related events ±1 Ob), Grudge (raises hostile-action weight), Debt (fires once when called in), Reputation (single-valued, modifies starting Disposition), and Compact (NEW, ED-SE-0019 — fires every season of its term until renewal/breach). Tags persist across governor tenure and survive succession.

name: Pressure homeostat (Π)
formula: Π_next = clamp(Π + Σ(unserved Needs) + Σ(active Grudges) + Σ(NPC ambitions in motion) + external_shock − Σ(player releases), 0, 10)
statement: A 0-10 per-settlement pressure scalar driving the event deck's draw count and family bias; low Π draws Opportunity/Ambition, mid is the dramatic band, high escalates to Crisis. This original formula was found MIS-SIGNED in the Goldenfurt build (pinned a quiet town toward Π=0 rather than restoring toward 3, per verification_findings.md CG-1) — see H6-093 for the corrected version.

name: Event card schema
statement: Each card carries an id, one of seven families, ALL-must-hold trigger predicates, a weight (base + Π-scaling + tag-modifiers), a cooldown, mutual exclusions, "the_ask" (summary + pressure_if_ignored), a set of player-verb responses each with consequences, and follow_on seeds for chained cards.

name: Event card families (seven)
statement: Petition, Friction, Opportunity, Crisis, Intrigue, Ambition, Thread — each seeded by a distinct pressure source (Local-Actor Convictions, Directive-Need conflict, high stats/low Π, high Π/stat floors, Grudges/covert factions, the NPC ambition engine, Thread Proximity/RS thresholds).

name: Card drawing rule
formula: draw n = 1 + floor(Π/3) cards, 1 at peace up to 4 in crisis
statement: Each season the deck draws 1+floor(Π/3) cards filtered by trigger predicates, weighted, deduplicated against cooldowns/exclusions; cards chain via follow_on, escalate when ignored, and resolve via player-verb responses.

name: NPC dossier schema (ambition/trajectory)
statement: Every significant settlement NPC is specified for identity, convictions, an ambition (goal, method, timeline, autonomously-advancing progress 0-5), the α/β ethic axis, loyalty, leverage (wants/fears/secret), Knot relationships, and a trajectory (how the NPC re-plans autonomously when its ambition is blocked or its Conviction is violated).

name: The ambition engine
statement: Each Accounting, every significant NPC advances its ambition by 1 (or more under favorable conditions) unless intervened upon; when progress hits its threshold the NPC acts, emitting an Ambition card — the settlement-scale instance of the sim_npc_as_player principle: NPCs play their own game on the same clock as the player.

name: The churn engine (world↔player two-stroke loop)
statement: A guaranteed-to-turn two-stroke loop: the world always acts on the player (mandatory Directive + Π-guaranteed ≥1 card draw), and the player always acts on the world (every governance verb emits a world-delta that becomes next season's trigger predicates and weights).

name: Clerk Capacity — opaque second AP source
statement: Retain Clerks (1 AP + Wealth -1/season, auto-succeeds) grants +1 effective AP per Clerk Capacity point (0-3), uncapped by FacilityTier, while silently incrementing a hidden Clerk Corruption counter that raises Intrigue-card weight — the only opaque-liability AP source in a doc where every other source is transparent up front.

name: Scale Hierarchy ruling — Territory as real intermediate tier
statement: Direct Jordan ruling (2026-07-13): Country > Duchy > Province (conditional) > Territory (NEW tier, multiple settlements) > Settlement. This supersedes PP-726 §1.1's "Territory = Settlement" equivalence.

name: Provinces are conditional, not fixed
statement: Direct Jordan ruling: territories are the fixed geographic unit; a province is an emergent aggregation existing only while its constituent territories share a common faction holder — replacing PP-726 §2.3's stateful fracture/reunify machine with an existence-conditional one.

name: The governance-type cascade (bidirectional, noisy)
statement: Direct Jordan ruling: each tier's governing authority sets/influences the governance type of the tier immediately below (Duke->Province->Territory->Settlement), and the cascade is explicitly bidirectional and noisy-weighted, not deterministic top-down.

name: L/PS as the top-down cascade's consent gate
statement: Direct Jordan ruling: L/PS is the resistance/consent gate on the governance-type cascade — a tier can impose a governance type, but whether it sticks depends on whether the settlements underneath accept it. This gives L/PS a precise, load-bearing role it did not previously have, and makes wiring it (E5, H6-014/018) the single highest-priority open item in the whole thread.

name: Factions hold people, not territory
statement: Direct Jordan ruling (verbatim): "Factions do not necessarily need to hold territory — they need to hold PEOPLE, and it is the number of people and the weight of their positions that carry the value of that faction." Faction tiers (local/provincial/national) are independent, not a strict containment hierarchy; territory-holding is a consequence of holding enough people in enough places, not the base unit of power.

name: Independence and cross-scale claiming
statement: Direct Jordan ruling: any settlement/territory/province can break from its current faction holder (Independence), and separately a settlement can be claimed directly by a faction from a different scale than its current chain of control, skipping intervening tiers (Cross-scale claiming) — e.g. RM claiming a single settlement without first holding its territory/province.

name: The two authorities that bypass the chain (Crown, Parliament)
statement: Direct Jordan ruling: the national ruler and Parliament are both exempt from the normal nested chain of command — the ruler can act directly on any duchy/province/territory/settlement regardless of ownership nesting, and Parliament can forcibly impact any province/territory/ settlement despite having no fixed hierarchy position.

name: VSG P12 ruling — settlement-grain temperament aggregation
statement: Jordan ruled (2026-07-13, verbatim): "Explore multiple temperaments whereby larger scales are partially informed by the aggregate of their constituent pieces." Rejects both a flat settlement-only temperament promotion and a pure top-down province->settlement inheritance — each scale in the new hierarchy carries its own temperament, partially derived from aggregating its children's realized temperaments. Exact aggregation function is unspecified authoring detail.

name: VSG P11 ruling — political allegiance as generation axis
statement: Jordan ruled, conditionally (verbatim): "If the generator can justify it within game world by backtracing, then sure." Deliberately seeding an off-owner/contested settlement is in scope only if the generator can produce an in-world causal justification (conquest, patronage collapse, migration) — not an arbitrary/unmotivated assignment.

name: VSG general calibration principle — every negative offset by a positive
statement: Jordan ruled, as a general principle beyond VSG (verbatim): "Every negative must be able to be offset by some kind of positive... Good, bad and middling governance must all be possible, but must all be unpredictable and dynamic." No paradigm's weight table should encode a purely negative or positive track; every pressure needs a counter-pressure and outcomes must stay genuinely unpredictable, not merely balanced-on-average.

name: VSG twelve-paradigm settlement generation stack (P1-P15)
statement: A DAG of fifteen weighted, seeded, conditioned generation paradigms (Location, Starting faction, Size, Type, Piety/Restoration, Altonian influence, Infrastructure, Economy, Caste, Governance type, Political allegiance, Sociopolitical sympathies, then downstream Actor roster, Event deck, and a mandatory Verify pass) producing a settlement as one noisy line drawn top-to-bottom; calibrated to reproduce the Goldenfurt slice exactly from its seed.

name: Noisy-throughlines formalism (conditioning/collision/coupling)
statement: Three distinct throughline kinds a settlement generator must satisfy: conditioning (vertical DAG-edge plausibility flow), collision (hard constraints like "every settlement carries >=1 Hold-Court collision"), and coupling (paradigms that are mechanically linked must be jointly sampled, never independently — the direct fix for the sim-F1..F9 missing-field class the Goldenfurt build produced).

name: Faction/territory paradigm stacks (F1-F8, R1-R9)
statement: A grounded but unratified parallel set of weighted-paradigm generation stacks for faction (substrate-posture, role template, stat block, holdings, sub-org ladder, emergence path, political axes, AI posture) and territory/province (location, duchy template, controlling faction/fracture, temperament, Piety, Calamity exposure, caste, settlement composition, political value/Franchise) generation, mirroring VSG's settlement stack.

name: 17-province canonical scalar table (fort_level/spiritual_weight/proximity_calamity/temperament)
statement: The full per-province scalar table (T1-T17: faction, region, fort_level 0-4, spiritual_weight 0-5, proximity_calamity 0-5, starting_pros, temperament α/β) that the generation stacks and territory_temperaments_v30 both draw on.

name: Consolidated blocker register (B1-B10) for the three generator stacks
statement: A ten-item cross-cutting blocker register: several items (B1 faction count, B2 S-006 tri-booking, B9 geography-YAML migration) were RULED/RESOLVED 2026-07-13, but B3 (Village/ Fortress-City/Cathedral-City type-taxonomy drift), B4 (inert L/PS), B5 (no settlement-scale Key vocabulary), B6 (no spatial substrate), B7 (no typed engine-params schema), B8 (event-deck engine S3-S6 entirely unbuilt) remain open as of the doc's date.

name: Settlement/temperament/contest/fieldwork/NPC-AI unreachable from mc_v18's import graph
statement: The live campaign loop (mc_v18) executes mass-battle / CI-MS-insurgency / victory, but the settlement layer, temperaments, contests, fieldwork, and NPC-AI are unreachable from its import graph as of this doc's writing — settlement/faction generation currently feeds nothing that runs (per "unaddressed-areas U-2").

name: Territory temperament typology (α/β pairs)
formula: pragmatic 0.7/0.3, traditional 0.3/0.7, balanced 0.5/0.5, principled 0.2/0.8, outcomes-only 0.9/0.1
statement: A five-typology outcomes(α)/conduct(β) weight-pair authored per province for the 17 canonical Valoria provinces; a faction's effective temperament is the population-weighted average across its territories.
status_evidence: systems/settlements/sim/temperaments.py:97-172 (temperament_of/temperament_modifiers/apply_strain_shock/get_faction_aggregate — all zero importers, confirmed by settlements_flow_skeleton_v1.md §7)

name: Temperament drift under strain
formula: on strain_shock(strain_delta>0): territory.temperament_drift = clamp(drift + 0.1*strain_delta, -1, +1)
statement: A territory's temperament drifts toward outcomes-only under sustained peninsular-strain shock events; calamity-adjacent territories start near outcomes-only with less headroom to drift further.

name: March Budget formula
formula: march_budget_pixels = Military*100 * cavalry_modifier(1.5 if Cav>=50%) * skirmish_modifier(1.3 if low-tier-only); cavalry+skirmish stack capped at 1.7x
statement: An army's per-season strategic movement budget in pixels, with a 1.5x cavalry-majority bonus and a 1.3x skirmish-only (no siege, no Elite/Heavy) bonus that stack but cap at 1.7x total.

name: Supply line attrition
formula: attrition strain +1/season per 4 settlements over an 8-settlement supply radius; converts to Size loss 1:1 at Accounting
statement: Armies operating beyond a supply radius from a friendly Mine/Cathedral/Port accumulate attrition, converting to unit Size loss at season Accounting; friendly territory does not contribute.

name: Effective vision (multiplicative stack)
formula: effective_vision = base_vision(240px) * terrain_factor * weather_factor * season_factor
statement: Fog-of-war/vision range computed as a multiplicative factor stack from a 240px base, per PP-709 §2.6.

name: Casus Belli on unauthorized inter-faction edge crossing
statement: Crossing an edge into another faction's territory without treaty/alliance/vassalage triggers Casus Belli +1 to the territorial faction and IP -2 to the trespasser, and the territorial faction may treat the army as hostile from the next tick if it does not retreat.

name: Settlement-scale battle terrain modifiers
formula: River/Mountain Pass: attacker -1D; Fortress: +Fort Level to Defender Ob; Seat: +1 Defender Discipline; Port: Defender +1D if naval reinforcement; Cathedral: attacker takes Church Casus Belli; Mine: attacker gains captured Prosperity
statement: Edge-type and settlement-type modifiers applied to the Manoeuvre Phase when mass battle resolves at a specific settlement node.

name: Army movement rate (settlement-granular)
formula: edges per season = max(1, floor(Military / 2))
statement: An army may traverse up to floor(Military/2) settlement-adjacency edges per season (minimum 1), replacing the old one-province-per-season abstraction.

name: Goldenfurt vertical slice (worked example content)
statement: A single interlocking worked example of the governance redesign built around S-006 Goldenfurt (a Crown breadbasket river-town): six collision-wired NPCs, a 28-card event deck across all seven families, an implementable sim-build plan, and a documented generation methodology. Status PROPOSAL; a 4-lens adversarial pass found 32 findings (15 high) against it.

name: Vectorized-slice-stack with noisy throughlines (authoring technique)
statement: The retrospectively-documented technique that produced Goldenfurt: seed a real map point -> condition ~6 weighted slices (type, economy, governance, religion, temperament) on it -> stochastically sample each (weights bias, do not determine) -> thread the draws into one coherent collision-wired settlement -> run an adversarial verification pass. Reified into settlement_generator_v1's VSG.

name: Goldenfurt seed identity is triple-booked across three canonical files
statement: valoria_geography_v30.yaml assigns S-006/S-007 to T3 Lowenskyst (Border Fortress); settlement_layer_v30.md:330 lists S-006 as Goldenfurt Town spoke; settlement_layer_v30.md:912 lists S-006 as Lowenskyst Fortress. The very settlement id/province the Goldenfurt slice seeds from is inconsistent across three canonical files. (Later resolved 2026-07-13 per settlements_currency_v1.md: S-006=Goldenfurt, S-007=Lowenskyst Fortress.)

name: Goldenfurt NPC collision cast (6 dossiers + 3 minor actors)
statement: Hedda Vorn (magistrate, law), Orsk Tallow (Guild grainmaster), Curate Wessel (Church), Tomas Vorn (Niflhel-linked smuggler, Hedda's brother), Greta Saatfeld (RM cell elder), and Bailiff Konrad Ems (Crown levy agent, corrupt) — six NPCs each with ambition/method+escalation/timeline/ autonomous-advance/leverage/trajectory, deliberately wired so any Hold Court ruling pleases one and wrongs another.

name: Corrected Π homeostat (bidirectional restoring term)
formula: restore_toward(3) = sign(3-Π) * min(1, |3-Π|); Π_next = clamp(Π + unserved_needs + active_grudges + ambitions_in_motion + external_shock - player_releases + restore_toward(3), 0, 10)
statement: The corrected Pressure homeostat term (v1.1 fix CG-1): the original design's decay_toward(3) only pulled DOWN, pinning a quiet settlement toward Π=0 and contradicting the doc's own anti-stall claim; the fix is bidirectional (pulls up when Π<3, down when Π>3).

name: Event-deck engine has zero code (governance.py, directives.py, events/ do not exist)
statement: The sim_build_spec's full build sequence (S0 registry through S6 content pack) specifies new modules governance.py, directives.py, events/{deck,predicates,pressure}.py, and an Accounting-step tick_ambitions — none of which exist in systems/settlements/sim/, confirmed by directory listing; only S0/S1 (registry.py, ledger.py) actually landed.
status_evidence: ls systems/settlements/sim/ shows only __init__, adjacency, infrastructure, ledger, registry, settlement, temperaments — no governance/directives/events

name: Adversarial verification of the Goldenfurt slice — 32 findings
statement: A 4-lens adversarial workflow (deck-balance, NPC-collision, churn-integrity, sim-completeness) found 32 defects (15 high) in the hand-authored Goldenfurt slice: a mis-signed Π term, an all-cost mandatory vise on the War-Levy card (zero Π-delta on any branch), a recall death-spiral, and 7 deck-referenced fields the sim spec never modeled. The architecture (the Hedda/Orsk rivalry, the two-stroke loop, the registry design) held; the content had real balance/completeness gaps, patched in v1.1.

name: NPC ETHICAL STANCE AND RESONANCE — the Stance Triangle
statement: Every named NPC holds three interconnected attributes — Conviction (operative worldview, determines what they want to do), Ethical Framework (faction-inherited, determines what they are rewarded for), and Resonant Style (the argument form that bypasses their defenses, determines how they can be moved) — which jointly produce NPC decisions, BG priority-tree behavior, and arc transitions.

name: Resonant Style Taxonomy (four styles)
statement: Evidence (vulnerable to verifiable facts, Memory+Revealing), Consequence (vulnerable to demonstrated/projected outcomes, Projection+Revealing), Authority (vulnerable to a framework-recognized authority, Memory+Obscuring), Solidarity (vulnerable to relational obligation, requires an active Knot) — each NPC has a primary and secondary.

name: Advisor-Principal Confidentiality Boundary
statement: A four-part mechanism (private counsel zone: no consequence for frank internal disagreement; public consequence zone: graduated Disposition/Renown/Standing/removal penalties by breach severity; Knot-mediated extraction: a player with Disposition >=+3 may attempt one Connect+Argue roll at Ob 3 to extract a private-counsel revelation with no consequence; public citation rupture: using the leaked counsel publicly as Evidence or in a formal proceeding fires an immediate Knot rupture and procedurally invalidates the leaked information as Evidence) that closes a loophole letting players extract advisor counsel as cost-free Consequence-RS Evidence.

name: Decision Fork resolution by Scar count
formula: Scar 0: Conviction over Framework; Scar 1: whichever Conviction the last Scar didn't address; Scar>=2: Conviction crisis table (GM d6); Stability<=1: Autonomy regardless of Conviction (no Leadership Deviation)
statement: The forced-choice resolution table a named NPC uses when institution and personal Conviction genuinely conflict.

name: NPC Practitioner Coherence decision thresholds
formula: 10-6 Stable: free operation; 5 Dissonant: defensive Thread ops only; 4-3 Degraded: cease Thread ops; 2 Fractured: seek withdrawal; 1 Severed: crisis mode, +2 Ob all Thread ops; 0 Conversion
statement: A six-tier Coherence table gating what Thread operations an NPC practitioner may attempt, applying to TTRPG GM guidance and BG/Hybrid NPC AI alike; a Warden MS<=20 override permits Mending-only regardless of tier.

name: Transformation Knot Strain Propagation
formula: TS 30-49: Close+1/season, Distant none; TS 50-69: Close+2, Distant+1; TS 70+ or in epistemic seduction: Close+3, Distant+2
statement: A transforming NPC's Thread-shift exerts strain on everyone Knotted to them, scaled by the NPC's current TS band and Knot proximity.

name: Constrained sub-arc state (Mandate<3)
statement: When a named NPC's faction Mandate drops below 3, Priority-2/3 arc behaviors requiring Mandate expenditure are replaced by Priority-6 institutional-rebuilding actions until Mandate recovers to >=3; Conviction/Resonant Style are unchanged, only the behavioral priority sequence shifts.

name: Resonant Style Targeting Effects
formula: confirmed targeting: +1D Argue roll for all four styles; Evidence win: +1 additional Track; Consequence win: NPC +2 strain; Authority: Doubt Marker regardless of outcome; Solidarity win: next Belief-revision Ob -1
statement: The mechanical payoff for confirming a Resonant Style targeting declaration in Contest, one effect per style.

name: Wrong-Style Penalty (Church Martyrdom Extension) with Compromise/Partial mapping
statement: Using the orator's declared-but-wrong Resonant Style against a Church NPC produces Stability +1 on Failure/near-Failure, graduated across Total-Victory (no penalty) through Failure (+1 full plus a compounded additional +1); RS declaration is locked at Contest setup (no mid-Contest pivot); multiple Wrong-Style penalties in one season stack nominally but are capped by the existing ±2/season Domain Action stat cap.

name: Stacking Limits on Argue-roll positional bonuses
formula: max +5D: genre+1, audience+1, Resonant Style+1, Recall+2; RS max +1D, does not stack with Recall
statement: The ceiling on combined positional dice bonuses (genre, audience, Resonant Style, Recall) any single Argue roll may claim.

name: Faction-level Framework Drift table
statement: Per-faction passive stat drift tied to each faction's Ethical Framework (Church CI+1/season + conditional Influence+1; Crown Truth+1/year unchallenged; Hafenmark Influence+1 conditional; Varfell TK+0.5/season capped at 3; Restoration Presence spread conditional; Guilds Favour+1/ year; Löwenritter military-consolidation redirect below Military 5); drift is passive, exempt from the ±2 Domain Action seasonal cap but still bounded 1-7.

name: BG NPC Faction Priority Tree template (7-level)
statement: A standardized 7-priority evaluation order (Survival, Conviction-critical, Framework-aligned opportunity, Institutional Tendency, Conviction-secondary, Reactive, Pass) that every NPC faction's board-game AI follows; per-faction trees (Church/Crown/Hafenmark/Varfell/Guilds/ Löwenritter/Restoration/Wardens) instantiate it with faction-specific conditions and actions.

name: NPC Personal Outreach Generation (World→Player bridge)
statement: Each season, after its priority tree fires, a named NPC with Disposition>=+2 and a relevant active Conviction may generate a Scene Slate Outreach entry (a request) or, at Disposition<=-2 with institutional authority, a Demand entry; max 3 Outreach and 2 Demand entries per season per player, with a cross-faction floor reserving at least 1 of 3 Outreach slots for non-player- faction NPCs; subnational faction leaders (Guild/Ministry/RM/Warden) generate settlement- anchored Outreach competing for the same cap.

name: Domain Echo from Resonant Style Engagement
statement: A decisive-or-better Contest win via Resonant Style targeting shifts the NPC's faction Institutional Tendency for one season (Total Victory: for the campaign, +1 Standing); any Belief Scar immediately updates the NPC's BG Priority-2 trigger for all future seasons.

name: NPC Recruitment Procedure (PP-642)
statement: A four-step recruitment procedure — Identify (source-gated; Disposition+4/5 toward current faction is a hard non-recruitable gate), Approach (a dedicated fieldwork scene rolling (Charisma*2)+History vs Ob), Offer (one incentive modifying Ob, stacking treated as coercion), and Resolution by Degree (Failure/Partial/Success/Overwhelming, with differing consequences) — plus a separate Hooks (leverage) system and a Priority-Tree-driven Defection check.

name: Recruitment Approach Ob formula
formula: Ob = floor(NPC's highest current Disposition toward any faction / 2) + 1, minimum 1; +4/+5 disposition is not recruitable
statement: The Approach step's Ob, keyed on the target NPC's own loyalty to their current faction — the same "score/2 plus modifiers" family of Ob ruling used elsewhere in the corpus (Jordan 2026-08-14).

name: Recruitment incentive Ob modifiers
formula: Advisory role -1; Territory governance -2; Wealth commitment -1; Belief alignment -2; Weak Hook -2; Strong Hook -> Ob 1 (floor, still rolled)
statement: One incentive per recruitment attempt modifies the Approach Ob; territory governance is explicitly named as a -2 Ob incentive — the "officer as settlement governor" recruitment lever. Stacking multiple incentives is treated as coercion (Ob halved but capped starting Disposition +1, resentment built in).

name: Disposition (canonical relation) vs affiliation_loyalty (code, 0-3)
statement: npc_behavior_v30's recruitment procedure and every other NPC-loyalty mechanic in this lane reads a -5..+5 Disposition scale. systems/world/sim/npe.py's NPC dataclass instead carries affiliation_loyalty: int = 0-3 — a different scale, a different field name, and the only loyalty-shaped state that actually exists in campaign-reachable code.

name: Roster Tracking Capacity (Active/Passive/Background tiers)
statement: Three named-NPC tracking tiers with differing state depth (Active: full per-season evolution; Passive: stable Disposition + Availability only; Background: identity only), a soft cap of ~35 Active + ~30 Passive NPCs, demotion triggers (4+ seasons off-screen, low-Disposition inertia, faction removal, player-declared) and reversible promotion.

name: npc_behavior_system_v1.md — retained superseded predecessor
statement: The pre-rename NPC ethical-stance doc, explicitly SUPERSEDED by npc_behavior_v30.md (2026-04-17) but retained as historical reference. Content genuinely diverges in places from the live doc, not just cosmetically — e.g. Maret Uln's Thread Sensitivity is 0 here vs 35 in the live doc, and Torben's Conviction-emergence window/mechanism differ materially — so treating this file as current would re-seed retracted per-NPC values.

name: Companion definition and eligibility
statement: A Companion is a named NPC with sustained personal-scale presence (Disposition>=+3), persistent cross-session state (Disposition/Wounds/Coherence), and narrative investment (a dedicated departure scene). Maximum 2 active Companions simultaneously; a single NPC may be both a Companion (personal-scale) and a Recruited NPC (faction-scale) at once — the officer-governor path is the canonical instance of this.

name: Companion vs Recruited NPC — the officer/governor/companion vocabulary distinction
statement: "Officer," "governor," and "companion" name three distinct roles that legitimately compose on one NPC but are governed by different systems: Companion (personal-scale, travels with PC, departure scene on loss), Recruited NPC (faction-scale, operates within faction structure, Mandate-1 talent-drain on loss), and Governor (settlement-scale post, per settlement_layer §3.2). This document is the one place that explicitly names the collision rather than letting it be pattern-matched away; each retains its own eligibility, tracking, and loss-consequence rules.

name: Companion officer-path stat generation
formula: Agility=floor(faction Military/2); STR=same; Endurance=same+1; Cognition/Charisma/Spirit=2 flat; Combat Pool=max(5, History+6); Wound Interval=Endurance+6
statement: A procedural stat-generation formula for officer-path Companions, derived from the recruiting faction's Military stat.

name: Companion Combat AI priority tree
formula: 1 Wounds>=Max-1: Full Guard; 2 PC ganged & unsupported: Rescue; 3 PC Wounded & Conviction-aligned: strike highest threat; 4 PC winning: standard split; 5 default: nearest target
statement: The autonomous combat behavior a Companion follows when the player does not direct it, overridden by explicit PC Phase-1 declaration.

name: Companion Mass Combat role tiers (Disposition +3/+4/+5)
statement: A Disposition-gated capability ladder for a Companion in mass combat: +3 commands an assigned unit inheriting the PC's Morale Effect even in personal combat; +4 becomes an independent sub-commander gaining an extra Co-Movement draw and access to Tier-2 tactics at Ob 2; +5 adds auto-stabilizing the PC once per battle with no Medicine action.

name: Companion Proxy Command
formula: Command re-establish: Cognition+History vs Ob 3; success -> units fight at floor(Military/2)
statement: When the PC-General is incapacitated, a Companion may attempt an intentionally-hard (Ob 3 vs the PC's usual Ob 2) Command check, succeeding at reduced effectiveness — not a general replacement.

name: Companion Departure conditions and scene
statement: Five non-voluntary departure triggers (combat death, 3-Scar Conviction departure with a final appeal roll, defection with a counter-offer window, faction dissolution, plus three ED-666 Thread-violation departures gated by companion Conviction) each fire a mandatory Priority-0 departure scene with its own resolution structure.

name: NPC Relational Graph — Edge Type Taxonomy (six types)
statement: Six canonical NPC-NPC relational edge types, each with a distinct directionality and 1-3 strength tiers — Sworn-bond (symmetric), Liege-vassal (asymmetric), Kinship (symmetric, special-cased parent->child), Patronage (asymmetric), Rivalry (symmetric/asymmetric, negative valence), Feud (symmetric, negative valence, hereditary). This is the state substrate for NPC-NPC ties, distinct from and co-existing alongside PC-NPC Disposition+Knots.

name: Relational-edge strain capacity by type/strength
formula: Sworn-bond/Liege-vassal capacity 3/5/7 by strength 1/2/3; Patronage 2/4/6; Kinship/Rivalry/Feud do not break by strain — they transition instead
statement: The strain-capacity table mirroring the Knot lifecycle template, at which a positive-valence edge breaks; negative/persistent-valence edges (Kinship, Rivalry, Feud) transition or escalate instead of breaking.

name: NPC-NPC Disposition derived from edge graph
formula: disposition(A→B) = base(0) + Σ edge.strength_signed(A,B) - (1 if any edge.strain > capacity*0.5 else 0), bounded [-5,+5]
statement: NPC-NPC Disposition is a pure reading of the relational-edge graph, never separately authored — authoring an edge implicitly sets Disposition.

name: Settlement Coupling — distance-scaled relational strain
formula: same/1-hop x1.0; 2-hop x1.25; 3-hop x1.5; 4+/unreachable x2.0 remote-tie; Thread-Witnessed edges bypass when both NPCs TS>=30
statement: Cross-territory relational edges accrue background strain scaled by settlement-adjacency hop distance (Renaissance long-distance-tie friction); a BFS residence-derivation rule resolves each NPC's canonical settlement (explicit override > Governor assignment > faction-headquarters default).

name: Defection Cascade — status claim vs code reality
statement: §7/§8's own section headers assert "BUILT 2026-06-09, ED-1000" for the Defection Cascade (hop-attenuated tier-1/2/3 propagation, a Fragility loop-gain term capped +3 and decaying -1/ season, a player Suppress damper) and its Faction-Cascade Integration. A tree-wide grep for relational_edges, defection_cascade, Fragility, sworn_bond/liege_vassal, and hop_distance across systems/ and engine/ returns zero .py hits, and systems/npcs/ itself holds zero Python files. "BUILT" here means a design decision was finalized, not that code exists — the doc-status-as-mechanism error §0.05 exists to catch.
status_evidence: grep -rn 'relational_edges|defection_cascade|Fragility|sworn.bond|liege.vassal|hop_distance' --include=*.py systems/ engine/ tools/ returns no output

name: Multi-edge composition rules
statement: A dyad may hold multiple edge types simultaneously with valence-dependent compatibility rules (Sworn-bond+Rivalry mutually exclusive and rupture into feud; Kinship+Rivalry allowed and canonical for brother-rivalries); strain on one edge spills over at half rate to same-valence co-held edges only.

name: Character Canon — Self-Other Orientation drift
formula: Δorient/season = κ*Σ(self-benefit outcomes) - κ*Σ(collective-sacrifice outcomes), κ=0.03 default, bounded [-1,+1]
statement: A [-1,+1] scalar orthogonal to the Conviction vector, tracking whom an NPC's actions primarily benefit; drifts under accumulated Mission outcomes to produce emergent fall-from-grace or moral-development arcs without authored beats.

name: Three orthogonal personal-scale axes (TS/Coherence/Spirit/Truth)
statement: Thread Sensitivity (0-100, canonical and reliable), Coherence (0-10, structural self-rendering integrity, partially authored), Spirit (1-7, whether will grips at low Coherence — Beckett vs Lispector texture, nearly absent from NPC sheets, defaults to 4), and Truth (0-5, cosmological framework alignment) are tracked as four independent axes the prose-writer skill consumes.

name: NPC Tier System with texture-floor expectations
statement: Tier 1 (Tracked Named) requires full schema population including Arc Map A/B/C minimum; Tier 2 (Operational Supporting) requires Identity+Convictions+Behavioral AI flaw+Goal; Tier 3 (Inner Circle/Council, ~14 NPCs) carries only Conviction+MS+Truth+a one-line note — below the prose-writer's stated minimum anchored-dimension requirement.

name: Character Canon Decision Log — surfaced source conflicts
statement: Eight explicit, surfaced (not silently resolved) conflicts across the NPC texture corpus: D1 Maret Uln/Yrsa Vossen Conviction values conflict between npc_behavior_v30 and the migration roster (migration roster taken as primary); D6 Baralta is misfiled in the migration roster under "Ecclesiastical Faction" with an ecclesiastical cultural template while npc_behavior §2.3 places her in Hafenmark with a Categorical Imperative framework; D7 Cesare/Lorenzo (Crown succession alternates) have full Conviction profiles in the migration roster but do not appear in npc_behavior's named-NPC roster at all.

name: NPCs Flow Skeleton — code-traced ground truth for systems/npcs/
statement: systems/npcs/ holds zero .py files; every design mechanic's actual code home is elsewhere. `generate_npc` (systems/world/sim/npe.py) has NO production call site — mc_v18 fires a stub_resolve in its place every season, and a dedicated test pins npcs_generated==0 on a seeded campaign. `select_action`/`evaluate_priority_stack` (engine/autoload/npc_ai.py) are unconditional stub no-ops with zero production callers. The npc_memory contract is doc:null, sim_module:none, with its own note that grepping npc_memory* tree-wide returns nothing.

name: simulate_npc_actions (stance-drift) — the one built NPC mechanic
formula: for each same-territory NPC pair sharing a conviction with an adjacent (|diff|==1) Stance on some issue: roll d6 vs average Volatility; on pass, shift both Stance values one step toward each other
statement: The one NPC mechanic that actually runs every accounting: pairwise Stance convergence between same-territory NPCs sharing a worldview conviction, called from run_accounting step 5. Its return value (a list of NPCAction descriptors) is discarded by the caller.

name: hidden_allegiance dead branch in NPC generation
statement: NPC generation's Tier-2 deviation roll computes a local hidden_allegiance value on one of its four flip branches, but the NPC(...) constructor call has no hidden_allegiance= keyword, so every generated NPC keeps the dataclass default (None) regardless of the roll — a wholly dead branch.

name: npc_behavior contract's doc/code ownership split
statement: The npc_behavior module contract's doc field was repointed (C-KEY-2, 2026-07-29) to a doc homed under systems/factions/, demoting npc_behavior_v30.md to a mere sources: citation; meanwhile CURRENT.md's "NPC behaviour" row still heads at the demoted doc. systems/npcs/ owns neither the code (sim_module: none) nor, per the contract layer, the doc of its own primary contract.

name: Baralta's Theological Position (direct communion / deed-monarchy)
statement: Baralta accepts the Church's theological content but rejects its exclusive mediation monopoly — a Henry-VIII/Luther/prosperity-gospel/deed-monarchy synthesis making her the Restoration Movement's structural adversary (both frameworks need Solmund as ultimate origin; pre-Solmund Einhir tradition implicitly denies that). Explicitly flagged as narrative/thematic positioning with no mechanical variable during a ~5-year game span.

name: Edeyja — the gold-standard NPC (stats, warden lineage, PC access gate)
statement: Thread Sensitivity 75-80 (highest of any living practitioner), Coherence 9, Conviction Warden, Resonant Style Evidence. Sole leader of a dying warden lineage holding the Southernmost; high-TS coordinated Weaving is described as a "military non-answer" that has deterred conquest since before the Calamity. Explicitly the canonical reference point for what TS 75+ looks like.

name: Edeyja PC Access gate (TS-thresholded expedition progress table)
formula: Season 2 contact: TS<=20 dismissed, TS 21-39 acknowledged, TS 40+ potentially useful; deeper access gated by Season 3+ site-reaching and Season 4+ Extraordinary Weaving success
statement: A five-stage expedition-progress ladder gating how much of Edeyja's cooperation and knowledge a party can access, TS-thresholded at first contact.

name: Conflict-as-disturbance — battles register on Edeyja's substrate sense
formula: MS -1/battle, MS -2 at Campaign/War scale (mass_battle §E.1); calamity_radiation Thread-tagged Domain Actions in radiation zones (PP-531)
statement: Every inter-faction battle and large-scale conflict on Valorian soil registers as a trace Thread disturbance Edeyja senses regardless of which faction caused it — she manages cumulative substrate cost, not source-faction blame.

name: The Ruler Diamond — four-way foil analysis (content)
statement: Six literary foil pairings among Almud, Lenneth, Baralta, and Vaynard analyzed across four axes (Post-War Settlement, Einhir/Caste, Church, Basis of Authority); a Part Two adds subjective first-person perspectives and an extended foil network including Ehrenwall. Largely narrative/characterization content with light numeric flavor (Mandate 5/7, Ob-1-deviation).

name: NPC Character Analyses — literary/historical-parallel corpus
statement: Twenty-four named NPCs each given a one-line historical-parallel characterization (e.g. Edeyja "The Last Maintenance Technician," Maret Uln "The Agent Who Became the Asset"). This raw material is exactly what character_canon_v30 §10.3 later structures into the per-NPC `Inspiration` field (historical_parallel + in_character_aspiration facets).

name: NPC Roster — 13 secondary officers, Mode Interface Matrix
statement: Thirteen secondary named NPCs (Maret Uln, Yrsa Vossen, Sæmund Haelgrund, Sigrid Torsvald, Halvar Brandt, Annika Feldhaus, Peder Almstedt, Gerik Strand, Dalla Virke, Doux Alexios Laskaris, Rikard Solberg, Aldric Tormann, plus Edeyja) each carry a Compromise, a named Behavioral-AI flaw, and a per-mode (TTRPG/Hybrid/BG) Presence classification — Full / Event Card / Modifier / Abstracted / Absent — with mechanical consequences attached to the flaw.

name: Gerik Strand flattery vulnerability
formula: social actions genuinely acknowledging Strand's competence: -1 Ob
statement: A representative Behavioral-AI-flaw mechanic — the Crown Lord Steward's insecurity is exploitable as a flat Ob discount on flattery-framed social approaches.

name: Sigrid Torsvald Thread-collateral abort rate
formula: ~30% Riskbreaker mission-abort rate in Thread-active territories when Torsvald leads
statement: A named-NPC Behavioral-AI consequence figure — Torsvald's TS-driven risk-aversion aborts roughly 3 in 10 Riskbreaker operations in Thread-active zones.

name: PP-726 §1/§2.3 hierarchy + fracturing rule
statement: PP-726's original hierarchy ("Territory = Settlement is the smallest political unit") and its §2.3 province-fracturing state-machine are explicitly superseded (2026-07-13, direct Jordan ruling) by scale_hierarchy_v1.md, which inserts a real Territory tier and replaces fracturing with a conditional-aggregation model. §2.1's settlement-count mechanics, §2.4's political-value formula, and §2.5's governor assignment are NOT yet rewritten to match — tracked, unexecuted propagation work.

name: Settlement count and march-route connection rules per province
formula: each province: 1-3 settlements, minimum 2; each settlement connected by road to >=2 other settlements
statement: Every Kingdom province must hold at least 2 settlements (no province reducible to one brittle siege-target), and every settlement must have at least two march-route connections (no settlement cut off by losing one connection) — the resilience rules underlying the canonical 35/37-settlement adjacency graph. Not itself superseded by scale_hierarchy_v1 (§6 item 1 flags §2.1 as needing a territory-tier analogue, not as wrong).

name: Political value computation (province/territory holdings)
formula: political_value(faction) = Σ(territory_value over owned territories) + Σ(province_unification_bonus over fully-owned provinces)
statement: A faction's political value for parliamentary influence and Mandate-track inputs sums a per-territory scalar (by settlement type + Prosperity/Defense/Order) plus a bonus awarded only when the faction owns every territory in a province — incentivizing full provincial consolidation over partial splits. Structure is canonical; specific scalar values are TBD pending balance calibration.

name: Sub-features are not separately siegeable (PP-726 §3)
statement: Districts, garrison towns, mines, watchtowers, lodges, shrines, watches, storehouses, harbors, gates, and ruins are properties of their parent settlement — not separately siegeable, not separately governed, and not separate march-targets — conferring mechanical effects (Wealth, vision range, Defense, cultural affordances) to the parent instead.

name: Three-Mode Architecture (TTRPG/Hybrid/BG)
statement: Valoria design canon (CANONICAL, PP-089/090 etc.) defines three resolution modes — TTRPG (scene-by-scene), Hybrid (BG strategic layer + TTRPG personal scenes via Zoom In/Out), and BG (turn-based seasonal Domain Actions) — differing in time scale and character presence (full sheet vs faction mat).

name: No-GM invariant violation in mode table and Personal→Faction handoff
statement: The TTRPG mode row states resolution occurs via "player narration, GM adjudication" (line 19) and §3.2 Personal→Faction states "GM recognises faction scope" (line 49). CLAUDE.md declares the engine resolves everything with no GM; this literal GM language is unretracted in the live scale_transitions_v30.md text as of this read.

name: §3.3 Personal → Scene (Contest) handoff is empty
statement: The document's handoff numbering reserves §3.3 "Personal → Scene (Contest)" as a named handoff heading, but the section body is empty — no handoff rule is specified for how a personal action becomes a Contest scene.

name: §3.1 Personal→Thread handoff
statement: A Personal-scale character may transition to Thread scale by succeeding a Leap; contact duration begins the round the Leap succeeds, the Thread pool and Thread operations become available, and the character returns to Personal scale on Contact end or voluntary withdrawal.

name: §3.2 Personal→Faction handoff
statement: When an action's scope is recognised as faction-level, the acting character's Personal-scale Ob resolves first, then the Domain Action Ob; a single roll is reused to produce the faction-level consequence through Domain Echo (§5) rather than requiring a second roll.

name: §3.4 Scene→Faction (Domain Echo trigger + tie-break)
statement: A scene meeting Sufficient Scope (§7) produces a Domain Echo (§5); if multiple Sufficient Scope conditions fire simultaneously in one scene, the highest-priority condition wins by a fixed order (Thread operation > Combat victory > Settlement governance > Disposition reach > Investigation completion > Faction-leader-direct > Other), and at most one Domain Echo may be produced per faction per scene.

name: §3.5 Thread→Faction handoff
statement: A Thread operation that targets faction-level configuration resolves directly as a Domain Action using the Thread pool and the applicable Domain Action Ob — the Thread operation itself IS the faction action, with no additional roll.

name: §3.6 Thread→Mass handoff
statement: Thread operations performed during a mass battle resolve per mass_battle §A.10, with Coherence cost scaled by battle scale (Skirmish/Company: TS≥30, cost 0/op; Battle/Campaign: TS≥50, cost −1/op; War: TS≥70, cost −2/op); rear/Reserve practitioners get a safe Phase 4 Leap while front-line practitioners get a conditional Phase 5 Leap, and Thread ops are recorded in Phase 4 (offensive) or Phase 6 steps 4-5 (support) and applied at Phase 6 Step 1.

name: §3.7 Mass→Personal (General Duel)
statement: During mass battle, a Personal Action (general duel) becomes available at Phase 5 Priority 8, limited to one exchange per battle turn and a maximum of 5 exchanges before forced disengage or incapacitation; the general's Command Rating is suspended while engaged in personal combat, and one mass-combat turn equals one personal-combat exchange.

name: §3.8 Scene→Mass handoff
statement: Winning a personal/social/investigation scene grants a one-turn modifier to the next mass battle turn: a social win grants +1D to a relevant unit's Command, an investigation win grants +1D to the first Volley, and a combat win grants one free Reform action; the modifier applies to the most relevant unit for one turn only.
formula: Social win: +1D Command; Investigation win: +1D first Volley; Combat win: free Reform action (1 turn duration)

name: §3.9 Fieldwork ↔ All Systems bridge family
