statement: Fieldwork maintains nine named bidirectional transition rules with Combat, Contest, Thread, Mass Battle and the BG/Hybrid layer (Exposure→ambush Initiative, Evidence cited as Contest Appeal, Thread-Read as perceptive Leap, Mass Battle suspending fieldwork, post-combat site investigation, post-Contest Disposition shift, BG Survey setting a TTRPG Fieldwork Ob offset, Fieldwork meeting Sufficient Scope producing Domain Echo per §3.4, and Fieldwork scenes being scoped to the Hybrid Personal Phase).

name: TTRPG Fieldwork → BG Domain Echo (governance-relevant row)
statement: A Fieldwork scene reaching Sufficient Scope (§7) produces a Domain Echo via the same §3.4 protocol; an Investigation Finding that names a faction leader, or a Disposition shift reaching Bonded with a faction-office NPC, each independently qualify as Sufficient Scope.

name: §4.1 Zoom In protocol
statement: Zoom In from BG to a personal scene has three legal entry points during mass battle (after Phase 1 declarations, after Phase 3 movement, after Phase 6 Step 1 damage application; a mid-Phase-5 Zoom In defers to after Phase 6 Step 1); a non-battle Zoom In fires at the end of the current Domain Action, applies RS changes immediately, and queues Domain Echoes to Accounting.

name: §4.1 Scene Opportunity Ob modifier
statement: The degree of the triggering BG Domain Action sets the difficulty of the resulting Zoom-In personal scene — Failure raises the scene Ob by 1, Success lowers it by 1, and Overwhelming lowers it by 2.
formula: Board FAILURE: scene Ob +1; SUCCESS: scene Ob −1; OVERWHELMING: scene Ob −2

name: §4.2 Zoom Out protocol
statement: Zoom Out transitions a TTRPG scene back to the BG layer; scene outcomes translate to BG consequences via Domain Echo (capped at ±1 Accord per territory per Zoom In), PC-incapacitation Stage-1 consequences apply immediately, a Contested Figure wound applies +1 Ob to the commander's remaining BG tactic rolls for the battle, and Phase 6 Steps 2-6 resolve after Zoom Out using the scene's updated state without pausing the BG clock.

name: Mandatory Zoom-In Triggers (§4.3.2)
statement: Eight named Priority-0 mandatory Scene Slate triggers are specified: Settlement Revolt, Heresy Investigation Target, Faction Leader Removal, Mass Battle at Settlement, Companion Arc Trigger, Knot Partner in Crisis, Stability Crisis, Rank Advancement Recognition. Already covered by the baseline execution-status audit.
baseline_ref: catalogue §8.3 (scene_dispatch.evaluate_triggers fires only Stability Crisis; other seven deferred)

name: The "debt scene" mechanic is referenced but never defined
statement: The Rank Advancement Recognition Event trigger states that withheld recognition "creates a debt scene per §1," but no such "debt scene" mechanic is defined anywhere in faction_politics_v30.md; the document's own inline editorial marks this unresolved.

name: §4.3.3 World-State Zoom-In triggers (Priority 1)
statement: Five Priority-1 (optional) Scene Slate triggers are specified: Clock Band Transition (any of MS/CI/IP crossing a threshold), NPC Conviction Crisis (Disposition ≥+1 and Scar count ≥2), Treaty Proposed or Broken involving the player's faction, Territory Control Change adjacent to the player, and Warden Emergency (RS ≤40 with WR≥1 or having met Edeyja).

name: §4.4 'Where Were You?' retrospective scene generation
statement: When a major world event (faction leader removal, territory conquest, mass battle resolution, Church Graduated Seizure, Löwenritter Coup, Altonian Invasion launch) occurs without the player present, the following season generates a free retrospective Scene Slate entry (no scene-action cost) whose content depends on the player's relationship to the involved parties (companion report, Knot resonance, letter/messenger at Disposition ≥+2, or unreliable ambient rumor with no connection) and cannot change the event's outcome, only the player's emotional response.

name: §5.1/§5.2 Domain Echo trigger + magnitude formula
statement: A personal scene produces a Domain Echo when it meets Sufficient Scope (§7), capped at one Domain Echo per scene per faction; the magnitude by degree is Overwhelming ±2, Success ±1, Partial no stat change (narrative only), Failure −1 to the acting faction's own stat, with a hard cap of ±2 per stat per Echo.
formula: Overwhelming: ±2; Success: ±1; Partial: 0; Failure: −1 (self); cap ±2/stat/Echo

name: Domain Echo timing (per-mode)
statement: In full TTRPG (Register Shift) mode a Domain Echo fires immediately at scene end with no extra roll; this timing differs deliberately from Hybrid mode, where faction consequences instead propagate through seasonal Accounting specifically to prevent real-time manipulation of BG stats from personal scenes.

name: Debate → Domain Echo (Piety Track band) + COMPOSED reconciliation with social_contest
statement: A Debate scene's Piety Track outcome maps to Domain Echo by band — Track ≥7 (winner's side) grants +1 Mandate and penalizes the loser −1 Mandate if it held institutional authority, Track 4-6 is a compromise producing no Domain Echo, and Track ≤3 reverses the effect. Jordan ruled 2026-07-08 (ED-SC-0002) that this band scheme and social_contest_v30 §6's genre scheme are COMPOSED, not rival: the band gates Echo magnitude while the won genre selects which stat/channel it hits (Memory→Mandate; Projection→outward-initiative).
formula: Track≥7: ±1 Mandate; Track 4-6: none; Track≤3: reversed

name: Accord Domain Echo
statement: Personal scenes in Hybrid mode may shift Accord via Domain Echo, capped at ±1 Accord per territory per Zoom In and targeting the settlement where the scene occurred (not the province directly) — province Accord then recalculates at Accounting as floor(mean(settlement Order)). Public governance success grants +1 Accord, destabilising action gives −1, a successful territorial-transfer negotiation sets transferred-territory Accord to 2, and PC-triggered territorial violence gives RS −1 immediate plus Accord −1; Accord Domain Echoes do not stack with a faction Govern action on the same territory the same season (higher value wins).
formula: province Accord = floor(mean(settlement Order)); cap ±1 Accord/territory/Zoom-In

name: Thread Domain Echo
statement: A Thread event produces a Domain Echo to faction stats when it meets "Thread Significance": an RS change ≥1, a witnessing NPC's Conviction Scar firing, or creation/destruction of a Gap/Lock/Knot at Territorial+ scale. Effects are fixed per event type (Dissolution Success: Stability −1; Mending Success Territorial+: Mandate +1; Gap creation: Stability −1; unauthorized Lock: Mandate −1; public op in Church territory: Church Mandate −1; public op in Varfell territory VTM≥3: Varfell Mandate +1), queued to Accounting, capped at 1/scene/faction, and may co-fire with an Accord Domain Echo on a different stat.
formula: Dissolution: Stability−1; Mending(Territorial+): Mandate+1; Gap creation: Stability−1; unauthorized Lock: Mandate−1; public op Church territory: Church Mandate−1; public op Varfell territory(VTM≥3): Varfell Mandate+1

name: No season-level Domain Echo aggregate ceiling
statement: §5 caps each Domain Echo channel per-scene-per-faction (PP-329) but sets no season-level aggregate ceiling, so a faction generating many qualifying scenes in one season (e.g. Debate-spam) can stack Domain Echoes without limit; whether a season cap is warranted is explicitly left unadjudicated for Stratum B/E balance review.

name: Coherence handling across Zoom cycles
statement: On first activation of a character in Hybrid mode, Coherence initializes to 10 (full); subsequent activations carry Coherence forward from the character's last personal scene rather than resetting. Additionally, only the PC who declares leadership at Phase 1 pays Coherence costs from Thread operations affecting the BG layer — co-leadership is disallowed specifically so exactly one PC bears the Thread-bridge Coherence cost.
formula: First activation: Coherence=10; subsequent: carried forward

name: §7 Sufficient Scope conditions
statement: A personal scene qualifies for Domain Echo if it meets any of seven conditions: involves a named faction leader or designated representative; directly challenges a faction's institutional authority; completes a Complex/Structural investigation (Evidence Track ≥5) concerning a faction's institutional acts; is a Thread operation targeting Relational+ faction configuration; wins combat against a named NPC holding faction office; reaches Disposition +4/+5 with an NPC holding faction office; or is a settlement-governance action changing Order by ±1 or more.

name: §7 Companion modifier on Sufficient Scope
statement: If the player has a companion present, the companion adds +1 to the player's net successes when evaluating whether Sufficient Scope was met — companion presence makes personal actions more politically visible.
formula: +1 net successes to Sufficient Scope check if companion present

name: §8 Scope Shift Rules is an empty section
statement: The document reserves a "§8 Scope Shift Rules" heading with no body content — like §3.3, a named section with zero specified rule.

name: §9 PC Faction Embedding
statement: A PC physically present in a territory grants their faction +1D to that faction's Domain Action resolved in that territory, once per season — the mechanical expression that PC presence in the BG layer matters.
formula: +1D to faction Domain Action in PC's territory, once/season

name: §10 Thread Timing in Hybrid (CI effects)
statement: In the Hybrid Strategic Phase, Thread operations auto-trigger CI effects: Dissolution gives CI +1, Past-Oriented Pulling gives CI −1 with a 1-season paradox window, Lock/Weave/Mend produce no CI effect. Full TTRPG RS values propagate directly to the BG RS track, and the BG Co-Movement ceiling applies only to BG-initiated Thread abstraction, never TTRPG scene Thread operations.
formula: Dissolution: CI+1; POP: CI−1 (1-season paradox window); Lock/Weave/Mend: none

name: §11 Contested Figure System
statement: A Contested Figure (CF) wound sustained during personal combat applies +1 Ob to the commander's BG tactic rolls for the remainder of the current mass battle.
formula: +1 Ob to commander's BG tactic rolls for remainder of battle on CF wound

name: All-Directions Key Delivery ruling (J-1)
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-06-19 (J-1) that Key delivery is direction-neutral: a single substrate mechanism (resolving an observer set from source_actor, targets[].actor_id, and actors_in_scale for public Keys, then applying stat_deltas) carries all six canonical directions (bottom-up, lateral/horizontal, vertical/up, diagonal via causes[], top-down, down-diagonal) with no per-direction special case; a bespoke top-down delivery channel must NOT be authored, since it would duplicate the substrate and violate the single-channel invariant — this is explicitly exempted from an earlier assessor finding (A6) that had identified only a missing rule/populated-targets gap, not a missing mechanism.

name: §12.3 Authoring discipline for sub-scale targets
statement: When a strategic or environmental Key carries a consequence reaching a sub-scale actor, the emitting system must (1) add each affected sub-scale actor to targets[] with the correct role (subject/object/witness/bystander), (2) include the sub-scale in scale_signature so actors_in_scale resolves those observers for public Keys, and (3) set stat_deltas and impact_vector for each such target — sparse down-targeting is the failure mode, exactly mirroring sparse causes[] as the diagonal-chain failure mode.

name: Known unpopulated down-seams touching governance
statement: Four emitter families have consumer intent already registry-canonical in key_type_registry but do not yet populate sub-scale targets[]: domain_actions → {npc_behavior, piety_track, settlement_economy}; faction_politics → npc_behavior; peninsular_strain → {npc_behavior, settlement_economy, settlement_layer}; scenario_authoring → settlement_layer. Closing these is emitter-side targets[] population, not a mechanism change.

name: NERS self-note on the all-directions ruling
statement: The document's own NERS self-assessment for the all-directions Key delivery guarantee: Non-dominance is met by closing the Robust-direction gap without new apparatus; Robustness is met because the eight handoffs plus the substrate guarantee leave no unreachable direction; Symmetry is met by identical observer-resolution methodology across every direction with no per-direction special case; Emergence is met because direction is a property of the Key rather than a catalogue of channels.

name: §2 Scale Table (5-scale ladder)
statement: Thread/cross-scale operations are classified into five scales, each with a fixed base Ob, minimum Thread Sensitivity, and Coherence auto-cost: Object (Ob 1, TS 30+, cost 0), Personal (Ob 2, TS 30+, cost 0), Relational (Ob 3, TS 50+, cost −1), Territorial (Ob 4, TS 50+, cost −1), Structural (Ob 5+, TS 70+, cost −2).
formula: Object:1/30/0; Personal:2/30/0; Relational:3/50/-1; Territorial:4/50/-1; Structural:5+/70/-2

name: Scale roster count collision (this doc's 5 vs code's 4 vs threadwork's 6)
statement: This document's Scale Table enumerates 5 scales (Object/Personal/Relational/Territorial/ Structural). A separate corpus-wide audit (2026-08-23 MASTER vocabulary reconciliation) found the engine's keys.py hard-enforces 4 scales (raises on a 5th), while a threadwork-scope table elsewhere in the corpus uses 6 — only "Personal" appears in all three, and the audit flags this as possibly "two different concepts forced into one class" rather than a simple miscount.

name: Conviction system (definition + structure)
statement: A Conviction is a player-authored one-sentence declared stance (subject + action/stance + implicit obstacle) that the game tracks; players hold exactly 3 at a time, one relating to personal goal, one to faction concern, one to a relationship/NPC. Player and NPC Convictions share vocabulary deliberately — both are targetable by Resonant Styles, and three Contest- inflicted strains on one Conviction force it to transform or be abandoned, making the world affect the player symmetrically to how the player affects the world.

name: Conviction resolution states + Momentum formula
statement: A resolved Conviction enters one of four states with fixed Momentum rewards: Fulfilled (+2 Momentum, Truth shift toward the value), Failed (+1 Momentum, Truth may shift away), Transformed (+2 Momentum, rewritten as a new Conviction not counted against the 3-cap for one season), or Unresolved (no Momentum, fades unrecorded; three simultaneous Unresolved Convictions trigger a "drift" warning). A resolution counts toward Portrait/retirement only if ≥2 scene actions were spent pursuing it.
formula: Fulfilled:+2 Mom; Failed:+1 Mom; Transformed:+2 Mom; Unresolved:0

name: Duty system — definition, generation, types
statement: A Duty is a faction-assigned seasonal objective generated from the faction leader's AI priority stack, gated to territories the player can reach and matched to the player's skills; eight named Duty types exist (Investigate, Diplomacy, Governance, Protection, Reconnaissance, Subversion, Thread Operation, Escort), each with a distinct success condition and failure consequence. Standing 0 (Petitioner) characters instead receive only a fixed narrative Initiation Duty before standard Duty generation activates.

name: Duty completion — Standing deltas and rank-threshold unlocks
statement: Duty resolution moves the faction-specific Standing track (0-7): Success +1 Standing, Exceeding +2; Failure gives −1, floor-protected so a player who has reached Standing 1+ can never fall below 1. Standing thresholds unlock fixed capabilities: 2=faction intel, 3=council observation + specialty branch (requires Formal Recognition Event), 4=NPC officer sub-commands +1 scene action, 5=treaty-level standing + inner-circle adjacency, 6=inner-circle voting +2 scene actions + Hall Tier residency, 7=succession-eligible Regent-Designate authority.
formula: Success:+1 Standing; Exceeding:+2; Failure:−1 (floor 1 once initiated)

name: Stature/Standing ladder (0-7) with titles
statement: The Standing ladder runs 0-7 with fixed generic titles (Petitioner, Operative, Agent, Counselor, Lieutenant, Senior, Prince/Chancellor/Senior-Jarl/Cardinal, Regent-Designate) and per-rank gates; full per-faction titles live in faction_politics_v30 §1 (PP-660). This is the corroborating half of the "two Standing ladders" collision already flagged against settlement_layer_v30 §3.2's retired 0-5 Counselor/Lieutenant/Successor titles.
baseline_ref: master doc §7 'P4 — Settlement governance', item 2 (two Standing ladders)

name: Leadership acquisition on faction-leader removal, and an internal unverified cross-reference
statement: On a faction leader's removal, succession is evaluated by the player's Standing: Standing 7 is offered leadership outright; Standing 5-6 triggers a succession contest whose SUC-01..03 cross-reference into faction_politics_v30 is flagged in-document as unverified (the cited Part 2 is Sub-Office Rank Ladders, not succession); below Standing 5, succession follows canonical NPC rules. Separately, a Standing-4+ character may force a leadership challenge via social contest at any time (council as Cognition-based adjudicator); success makes the player leader, failure drops Standing to 2 and Disposition with the deposed leader to −4.

name: Renown track — cross-faction personal authority, independent of Standing
statement: Renown (0-10) is a second, cross-faction axis measuring the player's peninsula-wide personal significance, persisting across faction changes and collapse, distinct from per-faction Standing — a player can be Standing-5/Renown-3 or Standing-0/Renown-8. Eight named sources each grant +1 Renown (Conviction resolved Fulfilled/Transformed, Duty Exceeded, Domain Echo produced, NPC arc influenced, Complex+ investigation resolved, mass battle participation, territory Accord improved while governing, Knot formed), capped at +2/season with no natural decay.
formula: cap +2 Renown/season; thresholds 3+:+1 neutral NPC start; 5+:+1D Impress; 7+: independent pool=floor(Renown/2); 9+: may call Grand Contest

name: Governance Responsibility — Renown risk from governance failure
statement: Players at Standing ≥3 who hold a governance post risk losing Renown from governance failure: Accord drops in the governed territory, faction Treasury reaching 0, or a battle loss in the governed territory each cost Renown −1, capped at −2 per season.
formula: Renown −1 per failure type, cap −2/season

name: Scene Slate generation — mandatory-crisis priority ordering
statement: When multiple Priority-0 mandatory scene triggers fire in one season, the game assigns a fixed default attendance-priority order (Faction Leader Removal > Heresy Investigation Target > Stability Crisis > Mass Battle in player's territory > Knot Partner in Crisis > Companion Arc Trigger > Settlement Revolt/Accord-0 > Rank Advancement Recognition), though the player may override the order — it is a UX triage hint, not a hard sequence.

name: Witness Mode — the mandatory-overflow fidelity, and its no-GM fix
statement: When mandatory scene count exceeds the scene-action budget, the player attends one mandatory scene per available action; the rest resolve in Witness Mode — present but non-directing, receiving one free (0 scene-action-cost but not auto-success) Read/Appraise roll at Ob 1, no Domain Echo, no Momentum/Coherence cost, resolution via NPC AI as if the player declined. The document's own ED-WR-0007 pass caught and removed a tabletop "GM may incorporate or reject" narrative-input sub-mechanic never re-derived for the engine's no-GM invariant, folding its flavor value into a Read/Appraise success unlocking one flavor-tagged dialogue line instead.

name: Scene Slate deterministic cross-step pruning algorithm
statement: Scene Slate generation is fully deterministic: all Step 1-7/2b entries are tagged (step_number, internal_index), mandatory entries are un-prunable, the remaining slot count is target_size−mandatory_count (by difficulty band), and non-mandatory entries are sorted by (step ascending, internal_index ascending), keeping the first remaining_slots — each step defines its own internal_index ordering rule (e.g. NPC Outreach sorts by Disposition then Renown descending).

name: Conviction-text keyword scanner and disambiguation validator
statement: Scene Slate Step 4 scans each active Conviction's text for matches against five categories (named NPCs, faction names, territory names, a ~25-term system-keyword list, 11 role-reference resolutions like "the king"→Almud), classifying strong/weak/no-match; a weak match now triggers an explicit yes/no disambiguation prompt at Conviction-write time rather than the earlier discarded capitalization-as-signal convention, generating up to 3 Conviction-aligned scenes.

name: Resources track (personal economic capacity) + consolidation ruling
statement: Resources is a personal 0-5 economic-capacity track (Destitute to Magnate) with faction- specific starting values, fed by faction salary/settlement governance/guild contracts/loot/ gifts, spent on equipment/bribes/hire/upgrades/Leverage. A 2026-07-08 ratified consolidation (ED-SE-0005) pruned the standalone Trade income roll into Guild contracts, merged the flat Fund-Development dice-bonus into the Develop governance verb's Treasury method, and retired the free Sponsor-event action into the single canonical Sponsor verb (now carrying a Debt tag), closing a dominant-strategy duplication.
formula: Resources 0-5; sources: salary +1(Std2+)/+2(Std4+)/season, settlement +1/season at Prosperity≥3, guild contracts +1..+3, loot +1, gifts +1

name: Legacy Conviction + Lineage Acts (character succession/inheritance)
statement: On character retirement/death, the player designates one Conviction as a Legacy Conviction (inherited transformed) and, independently, one of three Lineage Acts: Mentorship (60% skills + Founded-Org membership + 1 Close Knot to a Disposition≥+3 NPC designated as mentee-successor), Succession (titles/faction affiliation/estates carry to a declared heir, else canonical NPC succession), or Thread Legacy (half Warden Recognition + Thread knowledge, discoverable via fieldwork). No Lineage Act means a clean mechanical break.

name: Independent (non-faction) player path
statement: A player may refuse or abandon faction alignment: an independent character receives no Duties, generates scenes only from Convictions, has no faction stat pool for Domain Actions (until Renown 7+), cannot use Parliament or faction military, but can freely pursue Thread/fieldwork/ personal-combat and build cross-faction relationships without factional Disposition penalties.

name: D1 ruling — event architecture (card-deck vs predicate-sweep)
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-07-13 (D1) that the stateful card-deck event engine is canonical for player-facing settlement-season play, while the predicate-sweep engine remains only the balance-regression batch oracle; the two are kept in sync by an overlap map asserting shared events (Famine/Revolt/Raid/Flourishing) write identical state deltas in both.

name: D2 ruling — AP economy is the canonical action model
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-07-13 (D2) that the AP economy (AP = 2 + facility_tier, +1 at Seat/Cathedral) is canonical for play — the scarcity lever the "3 AP cannot serve all three needs" tension depends on — while the 500-seed framework's un-metered discrete handlers remain only a batch approximation for measuring the world.
formula: AP = 2 + facility_tier (+1 Seat/Cathedral)

name: D3 ruling — Compact modeled as a Debt subtype, not a 6th ledger family
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-07-13 (D3) that PR#119's proposed "Compact" ledger family is NOT a 6th ledger.TAG_KINDS entry and is not the same as the built Leverage family (Leverage = player-held hook; Compact = negotiated fixed-term extraction firing every season of its term) — Compact is instead modeled as Debt(key="compact:<quota>", ttl=term, recurs=True), reusing built machinery rather than minting a new primitive.
formula: Debt(key='compact:<quota>', ttl=term, recurs=True)

name: D3's Compact ruling appears unexecuted as of the later baseline audit
statement: Jordan ruled D3 on 2026-07-13 that Compact should be modeled as a recurring Debt subtype, not a 6th ledger family — yet the 2026-08-27 personnel/muster master doc (§7) still describes ledger.py's TAG_KINDS vs governance_play_redesign_v1 §1.6's "Compact" as an unresolved "code and canon disagree" discrepancy, with no mention of the D3 ruling. Either the ruling was never authored into governance_play_redesign_v1.md's text, or it was authored and the later audit missed it.
baseline_ref: master doc §7 'Two code-vs-canon discrepancies found here' item 1

name: D4 ruling — retire the §1.8 Mandate formula as collapse carrier; rename to resolve two-Mandates collision
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-07-13 (D4) to retire Mandate = round(7T/(T+6)) (settlement_layer §1.8) as the cross-scale collapse carrier — its L/PS inputs are declared-but-inert in sim/ — designating instead floor-average settlement Order + province fracturing + Standing/resolution_quality Keys as the real collapse signal, and directing that "Mandate" be reserved for the faction/ parliamentary meter to end a two-Mandates naming collision. The §1.8 L/PS→Mandate feedback loop is ruled design-only until L/PS is wired.
formula: retired: Mandate = round(7T/(T+6))

name: D5 ruling — merge §1.0d Performance Audit into the suspicion/recall spine
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-07-13 (D5) that the proposed §1.0d Performance Audit cascade is not a second accountability engine; it merges as a modifier onto the existing single suspicion/recall signal — cumulative per-Defy suspicion accrual (cap +1/season) triggering a G606 Recall scene with an always-available Submit-to-audit escape (−2 suspicion) and a Reputation:Just-lowered Ob. A Standing-6+ patron toggles a stricter suspicion→review cadence and faster-promotion upside.

name: D6 ruling — cumulative suspicion accrual, conditioned on a symmetric decay counter-mechanic
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-07-13 (D6, ED-IN-0047) that cumulative per-Defy-season suspicion accrual is canonical, but only on the explicit condition that E11 — a symmetric, ongoing suspicion- reduction mechanic driven by sustained compliance/consistency — lands in the same authoring pass as D5's merge, not as a deferred follow-on. Jordan: "every negative must be able to be offset by some kind of positive... good, bad and middling governance must all be possible, but must all be unpredictable and dynamic."

name: The twelve PR#119 item dispositions
statement: Twelve comparative-governance proposals received a consolidated disposition: five RATIFY as-is (§1.0c Court Attendance+Hostage-Kin, §2.5a Guild entry/mastership forks, §1.3c Ordenanza Ratification, §3.3b Za Patron-Lapse, the governance-ripple substrate, the 58-card grounded-deck architecture), four REFINE-THEN-RATIFY (§1.0b Recognition Fork, §1.1a Clerk Capacity, §3.3c Seggio Council, §1.3b Bind the Cells), one RECONCILE-FIRST (§1.3a Locked Extraction/Compact, gated on D3), one MERGE (§1.0d, folded into D5) — none required outright reversal.

name: §1.3a Locked Extraction/Compact — BREAK verdict + fixes required
statement: §1.3a (Locked Extraction / Compact) received a BREAK stress-test verdict: no subsistence floor on extraction and a protective Compact variant that gets Π-gated out at exactly the crisis Π where it's needed. Blocked on D3 (Compact-as-Debt) and additionally requires a subsistence-floor clamp (E3) authored before it can ratify.

name: §1.3b Bind the Cells — population-granularity gap, not an actor cap
statement: §1.3b (Bind the Cells, five-household collective-liability cells) received a MERGE-adjacent verdict; the underlying collision is a missing population-granularity layer, not an actor cap, since settlements already hold unbounded named NPCs and a separate §4.5 "1-2" figure is a different count-per-type metric entirely (a cross-reference error). Requires either an explicit household/population layer or scoping Collective-Liability to named-actor factions, plus fixing the §4.5 cross-reference.

name: The death-spiral bias and its designed-but-unported fix, with a later-superseding measurement
statement: Both stress harnesses independently confirm the settlement-governance resolution substrate is biased toward negative death-spirals (Flourishing events crowded out ~3.7:659 per-seed vs negative events). Goldenfurt already designs two unported fixes: a bidirectional Π-restoring term `sign(3−Π)·min(1,|3−Π|)` (CG-1) and a survivable recall (G606 escape + suspicion cap + lowered Ob). A later measurement (ners_vsg_reconciliation_v1 §3) found the unaugmented Π term alone insufficient across four methodologies — E1 must land bundled with E3 (subsistence floor) and E7 (positive-feedback recovery loop).
formula: Π-restoring term: sign(3−Π)·min(1,|3−Π|)

name: B1 ruling — starting faction count is 4, with named emergent-faction paths
statement: Jordan ruled (second-pass, direct input, B1) that the starting faction count is exactly 4 — Valorsmark/Crown, Hafenmark, Varfell, Church of Solmund/Himmelenger — matching valoria_ political_hierarchy_v30's existing 3-duchy-plus-Church structure, with an explicit intentional emergent-faction mechanic permitted: Restoration Movement (insurgency_pipeline_v30), Löwenritter-style post-coup splits (faction_succession_split_v30), and a named Altonia-usurper archetype.

name: B12, Territory/Province hierarchy conflict, open as of this doc
statement: As of 2026-07-13 this document records B12 as genuinely open: a conflict between a new Settlement→Territory→Province hierarchy Jordan described verbally and this document's companion valoria_political_hierarchy_v30.md's existing "Territory = Settlement" equivalence, gating even Part 41's Territory-scale content pending resolution. A same-day corpus-wide ruling (scale_hierarchy_v1.md) appears to be the resolution, but this document does not itself cite it.

name: E2 — Mandate-Challenge (political, non-violent privilege removal) is unauthored
statement: E2 names an authoring gap: a political (non-violent) mechanism to remove an entrenched/ irrevocable privilege (§3.3c Seggio Council, a lapsed §3.3b charter, entrenched Church infrastructure) does not exist — violent removal already exists via Siege + seizure_ob_modifier, but the non-violent path is the one genuine §3.3c residual, to be scoped as a bounded Parliament/Mandate-track contest rather than a full "unbuilt emergence pipeline."

name: Ripple substrate's own ratification status is ambiguous
statement: This document's own header states Status PROPOSED, "not yet Jordan-ratified." A later companion document (governance_consolidation_v1.md §2/§6) lists its disposition as "RATIFY (+ verify the one scoring edge)" among a set ratified via a "ratify commit all" instruction, but explicitly notes no ED citation was available to update the ripple substrate's item in that final pass — so its formal ratification is unconfirmed despite appearing in the ratified set's table.

name: The five governance primitives
statement: The governance-ripple substrate is built on exactly five primitives, each a genuine read/write dependency: Key emission (the loop's bus), Ledger tag (Precedent/Grudge/Debt/Reputation + the audited Compact/Concession/Capital-Posture families), Disposition (universal per-actor relationship scalar), Π (settlement pressure homeostat governing event draw), and Standing/ consolidation_progress (rank/advancement axis, player AND NPC). A proposed connection is real only if a specific field one writes is a field the other reads; a merely-thematic link must be cut — the pessimist NERS audit found this reskin failure in ~15 of 44 proposals.

name: The core causal-spine loop
statement: The governance loop is one closed spine: an event fires (Π-gated deck draw) and hits a settlement operation via typed levers; this creates a response burden across three pressure vectors on the responsible character; the response (shaped by governance mode/power_base) resolves and emits a Key updating the responder's Standing; that Key ripples into Field Investigation leads, Social Contest/Parliament content, and Faction-Action windows; these aggregate across scale (settlement→territory→faction→peninsula); the aggregate seeds or advances an emergent arc that re-weights the deck, closing the loop.

name: Five new settlement mechanical levers + open ruling R-1
statement: Five candidate new settlement levers survived a dedup pass against ~200 raw research proposals, each qualifying because it changes what KIND of decision a settlement presents: StockLevel (a standing granary buffer), Assessment tag (a locked assessed_base Prosperity figure), Capital- Posture (Mobile/Fixed, retyping what a Directive can extract), Consent-Rule (Unanimity/Majority, gating whether a ruling binds at all), and route/corridor Precedent (a targetable geographic vulnerability). Jordan has not ruled whether these five are in scope for the settlement layer versus letting the existing subnational-faction roster alone carry identity differentiation.

name: The three response-pressure vectors, kept mechanically distinct
statement: When an event lands on a settlement's responsible character, three distinct pressures must not be collapsed into one "stress" scalar: Upward (the governed pushing up — Disposition, Needs, Π, Petitions — resolved via Hold Court/Sponsor/Treat, failing as revolt/Π-Crisis), Downward (superiors demanding results via the Directive/patron ledger, resolved via Comply/Bargain/ Petition, failing as recall/audit/Demotion), and Positional (the seat's own AP-scarcity and power_base-typed vulnerability, resolved by choosing which of the other two vectors to pay, failing as "the collapse mode of how you hold power"). Positional is the document's genuinely new contribution: how a character came to hold their seat determines which levers they can pull and what it costs them politically.

name: resolution_quality — the event→standing bridge formula
statement: An event resolution (Comply/Bargain/Defy, or a Crisis-card branch) emits a Key carrying a computed resolution_quality signal: the arithmetic gap between what a Directive/Need demanded and what the season's actual stat deltas delivered on each contested axis, weighted by who the character answers to. This is not a new stat — it is a computed field projected onto the Key's existing impact_vector, read by faction_politics §1.0a's Demotion Magnitude rule as a Duty-failure or advancement input, with CHN-9 (Kaochengfa) treated as one patron-scoped configuration of this general rule rather than a standalone mechanic.
formula: resolution_quality(Key) = w_d·(delivered_to_Directive − demanded_by_Directive) + w_n·(delivered_to_Need − demanded_by_Need)

name: The event→standing bridge is HOOK-NEEDED, not wired
statement: The document's own §13 self-audit against its §9 primitive-dependency test finds the event→standing edge is not currently wired: faction_politics §1.0a's Demotion Triggers read real state but none of them reads a per-event resolution_quality signal today. It needs one authored trigger clause — "a settlement resolution_quality Key below threshold, on a Directive-bound seat, counts as a Duty failure" — before §5 can be called wired.

name: Event→Parliament/Social-Contest ripple is AT-RISK
statement: The document's own §13 self-audit rates the §6.2 edge (a resolution-quality Key feeding a Parliamentary Censure motion's opening Ob) AT-RISK: canon's Parliament/contest resolver has a "Define stakes" step but no input hook reading an external Key, so "opening Ob from Key magnitude" is the spec's own proposal, not a found dependency — the one place the document caught itself reaching for a resemblance instead of a read/write dependency. It must be earned (author a stakes.source_key input) or weakened to "a motion may cite the resolution Key as narrative predicate only."

name: Faction-Action ripple routes through the existing Mandate aggregation
statement: A run of well-handled Crises unlocks an expansion/Muster window; a run of mishandled ones forces a defensive posture — this ripple is real specifically because it routes through the existing canon Mandate = Σ settlement L/PS aggregation (settlement_layer §1.5) rather than requiring a new faction-level Key-aggregate track.

name: 'Mandate' names at least two incompatible formulas in the corpus
statement: This document cites Mandate = Σ settlement L/PS (settlement_layer §1.5) as "ALREADY CANON" and the aggregation backbone for the faction ripple. A separate ruling in the same corpus (governance_consolidation_v1 D4) retired a DIFFERENT formula also named Mandate — round(7T/(T+6)) (§1.8) — as a discredited "collapse carrier," and explicitly directed a rename "to end the two-Mandates collision." Whether the Σ L/PS formula cited here is the surviving Mandate name or part of the same collision is not resolved in this document.

name: Cross-scale aggregation chain — four scales, bidirectional
statement: The substrate's cross-scale aggregation reuses the Key's existing scale_signature stamp: an individual's Standing/consolidation_progress aggregates via patron/clientele edges into settlement L/PS/Prosperity/Order/Π, which aggregates into faction Mandate/Treasury (Treasury = Σ settlement Prosperity×10), which aggregates to peninsula-scale correlated shocks. The aggregation is bidirectional — a peninsula shock pushes Π down into every settlement simultaneously, which pushes down into individual response burdens, which push back up through resolution Keys into faction Mandate.
formula: Treasury = Σ settlement Prosperity × 10

name: Territory is the one genuinely unbuilt aggregation scale (open ruling R-3)
statement: Of the four management scales, Territory is named as the one genuine architectural gap — the "connective tissue between settlements" (shared AP pool, route network) with two candidate mechanics (BYZ-6, IT-5) both held needs_jordan. This document's own position: Territory should be authored as the connective-tissue scale, not "a bigger settlement" — flagged as the highest-leverage open ruling (R-3) in the document.

name: Open ruling R-2 — can an NPC contest a player-held seat?
statement: Because the resolution-quality signal makes NPCs demotable/promotable on the same Standing ladder the player climbs, an open ruling (R-2) asks whether a well-handled event lets an NPC contest a seat the player holds. The architecture supports either answer behind one flag, player_seats_are_contestable, described as the sharpest "every action pays what it buys" stakes call in the design.

name: Open ruling R-4 — event-deck band-cliff discreteness
statement: The resolution diagnostic run on the Π-weighted event-deck draw passed 4 of 5 NERS-adjacent properties but flagged one finding: the deck's band thresholds are discrete cliffs (Π 7→8 flips the draw from Intrigue-band to Crisis-band), a continuous input crossing a discrete boundary that jumps the outcome class. Open ruling R-4 asks whether this is an intended dramatic threshold or should be softened with a transition band.

name: Two proposals independently found defective by the NERS audit, both diagnosed the same way
statement: Two of twelve proposals authored into canon from the same research pass were separately found MERGE-defective: SE-JP1 (Goningumi collective-liability cells, 5-household partition) collides with settlement_layer §4.5's 1-2 Local-Actors/settlement granularity — it added a lever below the granularity the settlement model supports; CHN-9 (Kaochengfa) is a patron-scoped instance of the general §5 standing bridge authored as its own standalone toggle rather than a three-line configuration of the shared primitive.
baseline_ref: governance_consolidation_v1 §1 D3/D5 (related but distinct — D5 covers §1.0d specifically)

name: Architecture-compliance summary — no new Key types or resolvers needed
statement: A architecture-compliance pass found the standing bridge needs no new Key type and the card branches need no new resolver; five of eight loop edges are WIRED on current canon (event→ settlement, settlement→Mandate→faction, cross-scale stamping, event→FI, aggregation), two are HOOK-NEEDED (event→standing, arc-feedback→deck reweight), and one (event→Parliament) is AT-RISK. The one genuinely new engine in the loop is the Π-weighted event-deck draw itself, requiring formal resolution-diagnostic ratification.

name: FLAG vs VECTOR taxonomy — the governing classification
statement: The registry classifies every governance/politics/hierarchy type in the corpus as either a FLAG (a discrete, specific policy choice, non-accumulating) or a VECTOR (a continuous or multi- dimensional weighted quantity that accumulates/decays/aggregates/blends). The dominant real pattern is neither pure form but VECTOR-with-derived-FLAGS — a continuous meter that periodically throws a discrete FLAG event when it crosses a threshold (MS, CI, IP, Turmoil, Π, Accord all follow this shape) — meaning the same state variable typically needs both a Key (for the FLAG moment) and a separate continuously-readable mechanism (for the VECTOR body), since a Key is architecturally a one-shot typed emission, not a meter.

name: Five same-name/different-concept collisions across the scale hierarchy
statement: The registry's survey surfaced five distinct same-name, different-concept collisions not yet reconciled: Prosperity (Settlement 0-5 vs legacy per-Territory 1-7); Disposition (Personal −5..+5 vs Settlement Local-Actor −5..+5, different subject pool, no cross-reference found); Guild Favour/Favor (per-Territory 0-7 vs per-Settlement 1-7, different starting rule); Standing/ Reputation (faction-oscillating 0-5 vs a higher-range personal standing implied by "Standing-6+" gates used elsewhere); and Mandate (settlement-derived faction meter vs an unrelated CI-driven parliamentary meter — already flagged by D4 with a rename pending but not yet executed).

name: Legitimacy/Popular Support confirmed 100% inert in sim
statement: Legitimacy (L) and Popular Support (PS), the 0-7 settlement VECTORs that are the aggregation input to Faction Mandate, are confirmed inert in sim/ at 100/100 (`lps_inert_check`) — flagged as the single highest-priority open wiring gap in the entire governance/generation thread.
baseline_ref: master doc §7 item on P0.3/ED-FA-0004 L/PS gap (same underlying finding)

name: The consent/legitimacy gate wears three costumes (MERGE candidate)
statement: Three apparently distinct mechanics are the same underlying dynamic wearing different costumes: scale_hierarchy_v1 §4's claim that L/PS modulates whether an imposed governance type "sticks," faction_behavior_v30's pre-existing Legitimacy/Popular-Support build/erode dynamic, and faction_layer_v30 §5.9's compliance(L) tax-yield formula. Political-cascade consent, faction-Mandate aggregation, and tax compliance are flagged as one dynamic in three presentations — a strong candidate for one canonical consent-gate formula with three read-sites.

name: Weighted-cascade-with-noise — a recurring design-grammar pattern
statement: Three separate mechanics — the governance-type cascade (Country→Duchy→Province→Territory→ Settlement), the α-weighted Conviction Cascade through an NPC hierarchy, and Territory/Public Temperament's population-weighted drift under Strain — all follow the same template independently: weights bias, noise chooses, the result propagates both top-down and bottom-up.

name: Rank decoupled from formal office — convergent cross-civilization pattern
statement: Five independent historical-precedent research lanes (Byzantine, Chinese, Japanese, Habsburg, Italian) independently generated the same structural pattern — a character's political rank can decouple from their formal office — which is why the roster docket promotes power_base (patronage/merit/kinship/bureaucratic/military/purchased/ideological) to the organizing field of the whole Ascendancy layer. Paired symmetrically: a patron's fall drags their clients down too — one of eight general downfall shapes underlying ~96 historical cases, independently NERS- validated.
baseline_ref: catalogue §9.3 (the same eight-mechanism roster research, M1-M8 table)

name: The Field/Gauge gap — Keys model FLAGs well, VECTORs poorly
statement: A Key is architecturally a typed, targeted, one-shot emission — exactly right for every FLAG, but structurally the wrong shape for a VECTOR's continuous body (L/PS, Π, MS, Accord don't "emit," they ARE, continuously, between emissions). The armature half-recognizes this but has no named general primitive for a continuously-read, continuously-written scale-tagged value that Keys deposit deltas into and that decays between deposits. A Field (or Gauge) primitive is proposed — sharing scale_signature/targets[] discipline with Key but persistent, with a required decay_fn and aggregate_fn — but this is a grounded sketch, not a ratified architecture change.

name: OF-3 decay() deferral — still outstanding, now with working templates
statement: The Key & Echo Armature's generic decay() function (OF-3) was deferred by Jordan's 2026-07-07 ruling. This registry's §2.7 survey of seven cross-cutting global clocks finds two already have fully-specified decay math (MS: logarithmic recovery + 8-point hysteresis + distance falloff; Turmoil: an explicit per-Accounting decay pair) while three have none at all (CI, IP, Church Attention Pool are pure accumulators or one-directional), offered as evidence the OF-3 deferral is overdue for revisiting.

name: Ascendancy consolidation_progress — NERS-validated strongest keep
statement: consolidation_progress (0-5, a power_base-specific weighted VECTOR formula tracking an NPC's rise within the Ascendancy layer) was independently NERS-validated this session as the single strongest KEEP across the whole governance-compendium review, scoring 92/100 on downfall- exploitation criteria.

name: Faction Scale derived-value system
statement: Each of five faction stats produces one derived value via a fixed multiplier: Mandate → Legitimacy (×20, 0-140), Wealth → Treasury (×100), Military → Levies Available (×2, a non-spendable ceiling on active unit count), Influence → Reputation (×15), Stability → Discipline (×10). There is no shared 0-100 master scale across faction meters — each multiplier is independently sized to its own interaction frequency.
formula: Legitimacy=Mandate×20; Treasury=Wealth×100; Levies=Military×2(ceiling); Reputation=Influence×15; Discipline=Stability×10

name: Faction derived-value income/drain tables and stat-damage threshold rule
statement: Each faction derived value has seasonal income and event-triggered drains. The governing rule (§8.2): no game event directly modifies a 1-7 faction stat except through derived-value depletion (reaching 0 and staying there at the next Accounting converts to −1 on the underlying stat) or an explicit major structural event (faction collapse, coup, CI=100 Mass Seizure, Occupation, Parliamentary Outlawry, Generational Shift, Turmoil≥7, decisive battle loss, unit destruction) — the dividing line is "bad quarter" (derived drain) vs "fundamentally weakened" (stat damage).

name: Legitimacy/Popular Support are per-settlement, not a faction-level Mandate split
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-05-30 (LPS-1 → LPS-2e) that Legitimacy and Popular Support are PER-SETTLEMENT values (0-7, settlement_layer §1.8), not a faction-level split of Mandate; faction Mandate is instead their size-weighted aggregate, and the faction "Legitimacy" meter (Mandate×20) is only the displayed aggregate of that.
baseline_ref: governance_type_registry — L/PS confirmed 100% inert in sim (H7A-086, cross-referenced gap)

name: Settlement Scale derived values (PENDING, uncanonicalized)
statement: A settlement-scale derived-value layer is architecturally supported but not canonicalized: Prosperity → Local Economy (×50), Defense → Garrison Strength (Defense×20 + FortLevel×30), Order → Public Order (×20). Multipliers and interaction design are explicitly pending settlement_v30 development.
formula: Local Economy=Prosperity×50; Garrison Strength=Defense×20+FortLevel×30; Public Order=Order×20

name: Renown ↔ derived-value governance-failure bridge
statement: When a player holds a governance position (Standing ≥3), specific faction derived-value drains caused by governance failure convert into fixed Renown penalties: Accord drop in governed territory (Discipline −20) costs Governor Renown −1; Treasury reaching 0 while faction officer (Wealth −1 at Accounting) costs Counselor+ Renown −1; a battle loss in governed territory (Discipline −15) costs Governor Renown −1; faction Stability reaching 0 (collapse) costs any Member Renown −2. Capped at −2 Renown/season, does not decay below 0.
formula: Accord drop: Discipline−20→Renown−1; Treasury=0: Wealth−1→Renown−1; battle loss: Discipline−15→Renown−1; Stability=0: collapse→Renown−2; cap −2/season
baseline_ref: player_agency_v30 §5.4 Governance Responsibility (same underlying mechanic — see H7A-098 gap)

name: Renown/governance-failure bridge citation mismatch (§8.3 vs §10.3, v1 vs v30)
statement: player_agency_v30.md §5.4 cites its Renown-governance-failure rule as sourced from "derived_stats_v1 §8.3." The actual live document is derived_stats_v30.md, and the matching content lives at §10.3, not §8.3 (§8.3 in this document is a related but distinct list of faction structural stat-damage triggers). The citation is stale on both filename generation and section number.

name: Settlement combat-defense feedback loop
statement: A settlement's Garrison Strength responds directly to personal-combat outcomes when the player defends it: a repelled attack grants +10 (Overwhelming: +20 plus Public Order +5), a lost defense costs −10, and the settlement falling during player defense zeroes Garrison Strength and forces a Defense-stat check at the next Accounting. This chain (personal combat → settlement derived value → faction derived-value income) is described as the most complete personal-to- faction feedback loop in the corpus.
formula: win defense: +10; win Overwhelming: +20 & Public Order+5; lose defense: −10; settlement falls: Garrison→0 + Defense check Ob2

name: Faction-scale stat-modification conversion registry
statement: A 2026 audit (PP-680) reclassified 51 faction stat ±1/±2 references into CONVERT (routine fluctuation, now a derived-value drain — e.g. "Battle Partial: Stability −1" became "Discipline −15") versus KEEP (structural event, stays direct — e.g. decisive battle loss margin≥2 stays "Military −1"; Coup/Occupation/Generational Shift stay direct; a decisive Memory-genre social- contest win still grants faction Mandate +1 directly).

name: B12 resolution — Territory/Province hierarchy ruling
statement: Jordan ruled directly (2026-07-13, third pass) that the Territory/Province naming question is NOT a collision: the hierarchy is Settlement → Territory (new tier) → Province (multiple territories, formed only while sharing a common faction holder, replacing PP-726 §2.3's fracturing rule) → Duchy → Country, plus a bidirectional noisy governance-type cascade where each tier's authority sets the tier below's type, with L/PS as the consent/resistance modulator. This explicitly overrules valoria_political_hierarchy_v30.md (PP-726) §1/§2.3, now superseded.

name: PR#127 empirical confirmation of three governance_consolidation rulings, sharpened severity
statement: A 19-adapter empirical harness against real executing settlement/ledger code confirmed and sharpened three governance_consolidation_v1 D-rulings: D3 (Compact-as-Debt) — writing "Compact" through the real ledger silently corrupts the schema 100/100 trials, reclassified from "naming drift" to "live schema-corruption bug"; D5 (§1.0d merge) — across 3 regimes × 500 trials, G606 alone drives 100% of terminal recalls even under the most lenient §1.0d tuning tested; E5 (L/PS inert) — confirmed at the same 100/100 rate the design doc asserted only qualitatively.
baseline_ref: governance_consolidation_v1 D3/D5/E5 (H7A-056/H7A-059/H7A-086, this is the empirical confirmation)

name: D6 (NEW) — the G606 wiring-model fork, genuinely open pre-ruling
statement: Empirical testing surfaced a fork in HOW the suspicion/recall spine's clock advances: the integrated-campaign reading (advances on every non-compliant season — recall dominates near-totally) vs. the event-deck-engine reading (advances only on a specific card draw — recall cascades almost never fire). These are two meaningfully different felt games, not two implementations of the same spec, and D5's resolution cannot fully specify how the signal advances without this fork being ruled — Jordan resolved it as D6 (cumulative, conditioned on the E11 decay counter).

name: The Π term alone does not de-fang the death spiral (E1 sequencing overrule)
statement: Four independent measurements all converge that the unaugmented Π-restoring term, ported exactly as specified, still pins 298/300 settlements at the pressure ceiling — it does not de-fang the death-spiral pattern alone, challenging governance_consolidation_v1's framing of E1 as "just a port, no new design." Recommended fix: collapse E1 with E3 (subsistence floor) and E7 (positive-feedback recovery path) into one bundled deliverable.

name: B2 resolution — S-006/Goldenfurt identity kept, full 37-settlement geography resync
statement: Jordan ruled S-006 keeps the name Goldenfurt, then broadened the mandate to "reconcile all geography stuff with bias towards recency." Executed same day: valoria_geography_v30.yaml's settlements dict, found running an entirely stale pre-PP-726 36-settlement scheme, was migrated to all 37 settlements matching settlement_layer_v30.md's current table, with all 17 provinces' settlement lists and stale S-ID references corrected. Verified: 37 settlements, zero orphans, every province↔settlement and adjacency edge consistent.

name: The Ascendancy roster system is validated-ready but unauthored as canon
statement: The NERS review's single strongest validated claim (92/100 on downfall-exploitation) is the Ascendancy roster system (power_base + consolidation_progress), independently confirmed ready to author into canon as PROPOSED text without being blocked on any open Phase 0-5 workplan item.

name: E8/E9/E10 named foundation gaps under promote-ready proposals
statement: Three new items surfaced needing authoring before adjacent promote-ready proposals can be trusted: E8 (IT-2 Condotta's Aspetto ×0.5 Military clause must be reconciled against all four real faction.Mil read sites in code — live in 83/100 trials); E9 (a Ministry priority-action economy must be authored before HAB-4's tested 30/35/35 split can generalize); E10 (HRE-2 Chapter Capture needs an explicit acquisition cost — as pitched it is an 81%-favorable uncosted bet over a 10-season tenure).

name: B11 — engine_clock is unauthored and blocks the Territory-scale Relay Tier/Beacon Network
statement: engine_clock has no home design document and this is confirmed (100/100) as the sole blocker on Part 41's Relay Tier/Beacon Network content — described as "the single strongest new-state case in the corpus" — and by extension on any cross-settlement Territory-scale mechanic ever firing at runtime. This is called out as the one item in the reconciliation meeting the "loud, not silent" held-back-content bar.

name: The three-scale conflict engine (Peninsula/Province/Settlement) — likely superseded terminology
statement: This CANONICAL (2026-04-19) document specifies a three-scale governance hierarchy — Peninsula (strategic map) → Province (territory cards) → Settlement (infrastructure/governor contest) — with a fixed per-season resolution order Settlement→Province→Peninsula. A later ruling (scale_hierarchy_v1.md, 2026-07-13) established a different five-tier hierarchy (Settlement→ Territory→Province→Duchy→Country) explicitly overruling a three-tier model — this document's own three-scale terminology is not addressed by that later ruling and the relationship is unverified from either document alone.

name: Five starting settlement-governance friction points
statement: Five provinces begin the game with non-aligned settlements that fire fragmentation checks from season 1 without any triggering event: T1 Valorsplatz (Crown vs Church, Cathedral district), T8 Gransol (Hafenmark vs Guilds, Market Quarter), T14 Ehrenfeld (Crown vs Löwenritter, Barracks garrison), T4 Grauwald and T13 Oastad (Varfell vs Restoration Movement, covert Lodge vs overt Shrine). Each is framed as a historical governance-tension archetype (Investiture Controversy, feudal-vs-merchant-republic, Einhir restoration by conquest vs organizing).

name: Bishop Appointment — Church's settlement-scale territorial expansion path
statement: Ecclesiastical Appointment is a Church Domain Action available when a settlement has a Church building ≥ tier 2 and either no governor or a governor Disposition ≥+2 toward Church; it rolls Influence vs Ob 1. Success installs a bishop-governor, redirecting Prosperity/Order to Church, fracturing the containing province, adjusting settlement Accord by the territory's Piety Track level, and forcing the province controller to consolidate or accept. It generates no Casus Belli, unlike military Seizure, and operates prior to CI-driven Mass Seizure.
formula: Ob 1, Influence pool; no Casus Belli

name: Graduated Löwenritter Autonomy — four-stage progression
statement: A binary coup mechanic is replaced by a four-stage progression: Loyal → Restless (Crown Stability≤3, 4+ seasons without military action, or a lost province; garrison offensive use costs +1 Ob) → Autonomous (Crown Stability≤2, Ehrenwall's Disposition <0, or 4+ stalled seasons; garrison stops responding, Crown Military reduced by the garrison, PI −1) → Split (Crown attacks Löwenritter, is eliminated, or 4+ stalled seasons; T14 becomes an independent faction, PI −3, Crown PV −3). Stages 1-3 are reversible; only Split is irreversible without reconquest.
formula: Loyal→Restless→Autonomous→Split; each stage has named trigger and reversal conditions for stages 1-3

name: Niflhel Dissolution — faction retired, functions redistributed to settlement-level phenomena
statement: Niflhel is struck as a coordinated faction; every function it performed is preserved but made systemic: Black Markets (automatic at Order≤1 or ungoverned: Wealth +0.5, Accord −0.5, disappearing at Order≥3), Intelligence Brokers (independent profit-motivated NPCs, discoverable, killable/bribable/turnable), and Thread Exploitation Sites (harvestable, at the cost of further RS degradation). Former Niflhel-operative NPCs become independent settlement-tied actors.
baseline_ref: CLAUDE.md §4 naming-gate cross-reference (Niflhel strike confirmed propagated per MASTER-vocab §5.4)

name: Royal Assassination Fuse — one event, three divergent faction-restructuring outcomes
statement: One assassination fires deterministically at a randomized S8-S12 season unless the player investigates and stops it during a visible S1-S7 fuse; the target (Lenneth, Torben, or Almud) is fixed at game start. Each target produces a structurally different faction outcome: Lenneth's death triggers a revenge arc hardening Einhir policy and advancing RM; Torben's death forces a military extraction of Elske compounding a Varfell provocation with an Altonian crisis; Almud's death installs the pro-Einhir Lenneth, inverting Crown's factional identity into a Church heresy target.

name: Tensions Deck (rescoped to 6 cards, draw 1)
statement: The Tensions Deck was rescoped from an 8-10 card, draw-2 model to 6 cards drawn once, each a fuse (condition set at S0, event fires S8+) amplifying one of the five starting friction points: Royal Crisis, Feldmark Famine, Cardinal Independence, Guild Fracture, Einhir Incident, Ministry Crisis. Explicitly a variability modifier, not an ignition necessity — the five structural friction points alone already generate early-game conflict.

name: Aggregate-Up Transform — faction stats are read-only aggregates, never write targets
statement: Ratified canon (2026-07-02, formalizing IV.2 law 2) establishes that faction_stat[s] has no setter: it equals AGGREGATE_s(settlement/territory stats over holdings) plus decaying national_ event_modifier_k contributions read from the Key log — every write terminates at a settlement/ territory substrate cell or a Key-log entry, never the faction stat itself. This makes the existing domain_echo.compute_domain_echo() implementation (a direct faction-stat delta) a named defect — its amount/cap tables are reusable, but the destination must change.
formula: faction_stat[s] = AGGREGATE_s(settlement/territory stats) + Σ_k national_event_modifier_k

name: A Key targeting a faction observer must carry empty stat_deltas
statement: Because the Key substrate's generic apply step writes stat_deltas to every named observer without distinguishing a pure-derivation faction from a legitimately direct-written personal actor, any Key naming a faction in targets[] MUST carry stat_deltas: {} for that target — the magnitude rides in payload, read at derivation time by the registered consumer. This is a standing authoring discipline, not a self-enforcing schema property.

name: OF-7 — deferred-apply target amendment, RATIFIED
statement: Jordan's 2026-07-07 consolidated ratification (ED-IN-0026) ratified an amendment (OF-7) to the Key substrate's §4.1 step 4: a Key may declare a deferred-apply target whose stat_deltas are collected at emission (logged live, cause-linked, replayable) but whose actual state-write executes only at ACCOUNTING_BOUNDARY. A rejected cheaper alternative (holding the whole Key undrafted until the boundary) was rejected because it would break same-tick causes[] chaining, skip observer memory formation, and misdate emitted_at.

name: D.6 double-count risk on the up/down aggregation loop, HIGH PRIORITY unruled
statement: A national event-modifier's down-targeted settlement stat_deltas may overlap the very settlement stats that AGGREGATE_s reads to derive faction_stat[s] — if they overlap, the same scene outcome is counted twice. Confirmed by adversarial review as a live driver of non-convergence; the termination/convergence guarantee is explicitly conditional on Jordan ruling the two are disjoint. Unresolved as of this document.

name: The eight cross-scale down-seams closure worklist
statement: Eight specific emitter→consumer Key-delivery seams need targets[]/scale_signature/stat_deltas population: domain_actions→npc_behavior (×3), domain_actions→piety_track (×2), domain_actions→ settlement_economy (×1), faction_politics→npc_behavior (×4), peninsular_strain→npc_behavior (×1), peninsular_strain→settlement_economy (×1), peninsular_strain→settlement_layer (×2), scenario_authoring→settlement_layer (×1).
baseline_ref: scale_transitions_v30 §12.4 (H7A-035, same down-seam finding, four family groupings vs eight numbered rows)

name: The one-Key-N-targets fan-out rule
statement: A single strategic Key affecting N sub-scale actors is emitted exactly once with all N entries in its targets[] array — never as N separate re-entrant emissions. The termination guard's cascade_depth counter increments only when a consumer of an already-drained Key emits a NEW Key in response, never on the width of a single Key's targets[] array, so legitimately wide fan-out cannot trip the re-entrancy cap.

name: Stability Crisis hysteresis (ED-749) is ruled but the sim doesn't comply
statement: scale_transitions_v30 §4.3.2 already rules the Stability Crisis perpetual-scene risk via ED-749 hysteresis (edge-triggered, re-arms only after Stability≥3 held 2 Accountings, scoped to the player's faction) — but the live implementation re-evaluates fresh every tick with no hysteresis state and iterates ALL factions. Characterized as a sim compliance bug, not an open design question; whether OTHER level-conditioned §4.3.2 triggers have their own hysteresis is an open hygiene-audit item.

name: Church settlement infrastructure — four independent axes
statement: Church presence in a settlement is four INDEPENDENT stacking axes rather than a linear progression: Religious Building (None/Chapel/Church/Cathedral, mutually exclusive, Cathedral destroyable only by Mass Battle), Templar Station (binary, +1 CI/season, can interrupt rival Domain Actions), Inquisitor Base (binary, Surveillance Zone raising RM organizing Ob), and Church Governor (binary, de facto Church territory, removable only by Mass Battle/Mandate Challenge Ob6+/RM Overwhelming). Max combined per-settlement Seizure Ob modifier is −6.
formula: Base Seizure Ob = 10 − PT − infrastructure modifiers (floor 1); max per-settlement modifier −6

name: CI=100 Mass Seizure Declaration
statement: When CI reaches 100, every territory with a Church-building settlement is targeted for simultaneous Seizure, each resolving independently at Ob = 10 − PT − infrastructure modifiers (floor 1); the Declaration fires as a mandatory Zoom-In scene giving all factions one Emergency Session season to respond. CI=100 is Church's theocracy bid, not automatic victory — seized territories start at Accord 1 (or 2 if PT≥3), meaning Church must actively govern what it seizes.

name: RM identity ruling — Community Organizing is political, not Thread-mechanical
statement: Restoration Movement is ruled to NOT believe threadwork is real — its "Community Organizing" action is political organizing using social stats, producing sociological PT reduction and explicitly no MS change, co-movement, or Thread mechanical effect at all. When RM discovers its governance nodes coincide with real Threadweaving sites, three named NPC arc paths exist (Embrace/Denial/Schism), each with a different downstream faction alignment.

name: Phased Altonian invasion (IP escalation)
statement: Altonian invasion escalates in three IP-gated phases: Phase 1 (IP≥100) opens one border territory; Phase 2 (IP sustained ≥85 for 3 seasons) adds two territories and establishes an Altonian Governorate (Mandate 2/Military 4/Stability 3) plus an activated Underground Network; Phase 3 (IP sustained ≥80 for 3 more seasons) adds a third corridor and raises the Governorate to Mandate 3/Military 5/Stability 4, with all Domain Actions +2 Ob in occupied territories. Named retreat thresholds exist per phase.
formula: Phase1: IP≥100; Phase2: IP≥85×3 seasons; Phase3: IP≥80×3 more seasons; retreats at <85/<75/<60

name: Three named Altonian repulsion paths
statement: Altonia can be permanently repelled via three named paths, each freezing IP afterward: Military (two consecutive Overwhelming mass-battle wins → full withdrawal, IP resets to 60, capped below 80 for 10 seasons), Diplomatic (Elske Loyalty≥6 + contest vs Vanguard Commander Ob4 while IP<80 → IP drops to 40, OW: 20 + 20-season pact), Resistance-during-Occupation (Underground Network Mandate3 + Governorate Accord0 + battle win → IP resets to 30). Any path permanently resolves the threat for the campaign.
formula: military: 2×OW→IP=60,cap80×10seasons; diplomatic: Loyalty≥6+contest Ob4→IP=40(OW:20+pact20); resistance: Network Mandate3+Accord0+battle win→IP=30

name: Elske residency / Löwenritter autonomy null-intersection ruling
statement: An apparent intersection between Crown Princess Elske's Altonian marriage-residency and the Löwenritter Graduated Autonomy track was investigated and ruled largely NULL: Elske's residency is governed by her Altonian husband's house regardless of Crown-Löwenritter relational stage, with exactly one edge case (Crown Stability≤1 + Löwenritter Split) where Altonia's own diplomatic calculus — already covered by existing IP/Vanguard mechanics — decides whether to recall her.

name: Five Warden paths to political relevance
statement: The Wardens (a ~8-15 person informal network at game start) have five named paths to political relevance, each producing a structurally different faction shape: Recruited by Varfell (institutional branch), Recruited by RM post-revelation, Recruited by the player (built from scratch), Recruited by Lenneth/Crown (Thread stewardship as royal function), or Independent/ crisis-driven (MS≤20, Mending Sanctuaries enforced by Thread capability — "the hardest and most distinctive path"). If activated, Wardens use consensus governance (stat = average Spirit of active Menders) and win via demonstrated stewardship, not conquest.

name: Early-game ignition analysis is entirely superseded
statement: This ANALYSIS document proposed three ignition mechanisms to solve a diagnosed "no fire starters at game start" problem: an 8-card Tensions Deck (draw 2), a Niflhel Fabricated-Intelligence Provocation, and a Löwenritter Martial Honor Pressure entry, plus a six-mechanism historical taxonomy. It concluded no new faction was needed. The entire proposed mechanism set was explicitly SUPERSEDED 2026-04-19 by conflict_architecture_proposal.md, which instead dissolved Niflhel entirely, rescoped the deck to 6 cards/draw 1, moved assassination to an S8+ fuse, and identified settlement governance friction itself as the actual ignition system. The six- mechanism historical taxonomy is retained as valid reference material even though the mechanical proposals built on it are dead.

name: New Key types proposed for major settlement/world state-transition events
statement: New Key types were proposed to cover gateless major world-state transitions: state.settlement_ revolt (Order→0), mechanical.settlement_captured (undefended auto-capture), mechanical. settlement_surrendered (siege Order→0, gateless), state.settlement_stat_collapse, state. legitimacy_drift (L/PS mean-reversion), mechanical.ci_milestone_crossed (40/55/65/80/100), mechanical.theocracy_unification_declared (CI=100), mechanical.era_transition (MS/IP world-state gates, gateless), mechanical.second_calamity ("the game's only true terminal"), and mechanical. ip_milestone_crossed (IP 60/80/90, stranded prose).

name: ED-SE-0002 Accord-stacking fork, deferred to SE lane, not this document's ruling
statement: A genuine unresolved fork exists between scale_transitions_v30 §5.5 (Accord Domain Echo does NOT stack with a same-territory Govern action) and peninsular_strain's own §2.7 strain model (which DOES stack). Jordan's 2026-07-07 ruling pass explicitly declined to resolve this from the IN lane, deferring it as SE-lane's own call — this armature's Accord echo row carries only the cap, not a stacking rule, specifically to remain neutral pending that ruling.
baseline_ref: scale_transitions_v30 §5.5 (H7A-023, same Accord Echo mechanic — this adds the unresolved stacking conflict)

name: ER-2 resolution-band symmetry adopted across combat/contest kernels
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-07-07 (5.12) that a genuine no-default fork — combat's degree() carrying an ER-2 continuity correction and a fixed 2·Ob Overwhelming bar that saturates with pool size, versus the shared contest-path degree() having neither — should resolve symmetrically: BOTH extend across the whole shared resolution substrate, rather than picking one kernel's convention. This is a direction ruling only; the actual resolver-math execution was deferred to its own ED pending its own regression pass.

name: The Key primitive — universal event schema
statement: Every consequential event in the engine is represented as a Key — a typed, validated, append-only record with required fields id/type/source_actor/emitted_at/causes[]/targets[] (each carrying role, impact_vector on 4 Conviction axes, and stat_deltas)/scale_signature/ symbolic_dimensions/visibility/time_horizon/permanence/payload. Save state equals initial conditions plus the Key log; replay is deterministic re-execution of that log. No system maintains a private event channel.

name: The 4-axis Conviction/symbolic-dimension space
statement: The Key substrate projects every event's symbolic content onto four named axes — hierarchical (rank-bearing vs egalitarian), sacred (numinous/oath-binding vs secular/contractual), instrumental (calculative/transactional vs principled/deontological), traditional (precedent- respecting vs progressive/reformist) — used both as a Key's symbolic_dimensions and its per-target impact_vector. A 5th axis is permitted as a future extension if calibration finds the 4-axis simplification load-bearing, but is deferred unless required.
formula: interpretation(npc,key) = Σ_axes npc.armature_position[axis] × key.symbolic_dimensions[axis] × key.impact_vector[npc.id][axis]

name: PP-686 faction integration via Keys — L/PS and Mission/Cascade triggers
statement: Faction-scale state machinery is specified to consume Keys directly: Mission outcome scoring reads da_outcome.* Keys, faction Cascade re-resolution triggers on state.succession and a leader's state.scar_acquired, Public Expectation strictness reads the full observed Key stream, and Legitimacy/Popular-Support updates via the standard update rule rather than a bespoke procedure.

name: Domain Action outcome Key family — five subtypes classify every strategic action
statement: Every Domain Action's outcome is one of five registered Key subtypes carrying a mission_ alignment classification: da.public_governance (visible administrative action), da.covert_ betrayal (covert action against ally/mission, visibility flips dramatically on an `exposed` bool), da.diplomatic_alliance (treaty formation, INDELIBLE per "Renaissance convention: treaties carry permanent weight even on later abrogation"), da.antinomian_action (always mission_ alignment=penalty, carries a 1-3 role_violation_severity), and da.economic_intervention (tax/grant/regulation/dispossession).

name: state_transition family — Standing, Coup, and Succession Key types
statement: Three registered Key subtypes cover faction-personnel state changes: state.standing_change (trigger ∈ promotion/demotion/succession/exile/death, magnitude 1-3, INDELIBLE), state.coup_ attempted (challenger vs incumbent, outcome success/failure/inconclusive, "high expectation_ weight contribution regardless of outcome"), and state.succession (succession_mode ∈ normal/ contested/emergency/imposed, explicitly triggers an immediate mechanical.cascade_resolution event with triggered_by=succession).

name: Four new settlement/world-state Key types registered but zero live emit sites
statement: Four Key types registered 2026-07-29 (ED-IN-0014) for major world-state events — mechanical. settlement_captured, mechanical.era_transition, mechanical.second_calamity (explicitly "the only true campaign terminal"), and mechanical.theocracy_unification_declared — are all DECLARE-ONLY: their triggering gates have no evaluator in the live loop, victory/ has no sim/ subfolder at all (zero runtime), and consuming_systems is intentionally left empty after a correction (ED-IN-0096) removed a falsely-declared articulation subscription with no matching live subscription code.
baseline_ref: key_echo_armature_v1 §3 (H7A-131, same proposed types — this adds their actual DECLARE-ONLY registered status)

name: victory_v30's CANONICAL status for §5 contradicts module_contracts.yaml's gap_note
statement: module_contracts.yaml's victory entry gap_note states the module's doc status is "DESIGN — pending Varfell Path B decision (ED-311) — not CANONICAL," but victory_v30.md's own header lists ED-311 as CLOSED and marks itself CANONICAL for every section except an explicitly-superseded list that does NOT include §5 (the era-transition section this Key type covers). Logged per CLAUDE.md §0.1 point 5 rather than corrected, since resolving it is contracts-lane territory.

name: scene.accord_echo is wired end-to-end but organically dormant
statement: The Accord Domain Echo Key (distinct from and co-firing alongside the §5.2 faction-stat Domain Echo Key from the same resolved scene) is genuinely WIRED as of 2026-07-29: echo_transport builds and emits it, routes the write through the deferred-apply scheduler to land at accounting_boundary(), and articulation.py subscribes to it with an end-to-end test. It nonetheless never fires in any seeded campaign because no live producer anywhere ever sets echo['scene_outcome'] — a reachability gap on the emit side, not a wiring gap.
baseline_ref: scale_transitions_v30 §5.5 (H7A-023, the same Accord Echo mechanic — this adds current wiring/reachability status)

name: T-07 Turmoil → Accord Erosion → Governance Collapse
statement: A named mechanical throughline chains battles → Strain accumulation → threshold effects (Strain 3: Mandate checks; 5: Accord −1; 7: Accord −1 in all non-capitals; 9: Accord capped at 2 + RS −1/season) → Accord erosion → harder governance → more instability → more battles, closing a positive feedback loop. Since Universal victory requires Accord ≥2 everywhere, Strain 9+ makes victory achievable only by ending the war.
formula: Strain 3: Mandate check; 5: Accord−1; 7: Accord−1(non-capitals); 9: Accord cap 2 + RS−1/season

name: T-15 Player Progression and T-25 Generational Arc
statement: T-15 (Player Progression) chains Standing 0 → Renown accumulation → settlement governance → provincial authority → faction emergence, framed as the game's answer to "why does my character matter." T-25 (Generational Arc) chains a 30-year campaign through a Generational Shift clock (+1 per 5 years) that ages original faction leaders (−1/−2/−3 to their highest attribute) and fires succession, so by campaign end the player's own generation IS the leadership class.

name: T-20 The Two Contests — structurally unresolvable resource competition
statement: The game's central strategic architecture: a sovereignty contest (territorial control, faction stats, victory conditions) structurally competes with a survival contest (MS maintenance, WC advancement, expedition support) for the identical resource pool. A player optimizing sovereignty risks substrate Rupture; a player optimizing survival sacrifices political position; the tension is deliberately unresolvable, requiring both to be managed with insufficient resources for either.

name: This unratified proposal's Domain Echo Reference Table conflicts with the later ratified table
statement: This unratified critique/proposal specifies a detailed per-action-type Domain Echo Reference Table (twelve action-type rows, each with distinct OW/Success/Partial/Failure outcomes and named target stats) and calls it "the single most important deliverable... should be committed immediately." The later RATIFIED scale_transitions_v30 §5.2 instead adopted a much simpler universal degree-keyed table (±2/±1/0/−1) applying uniformly across action types. The two tables were never reconciled; the simpler ratified version appears to have superseded this proposal's granular one without an explicit supersession citation.

name: Counselor Negotiation Output (unratified)
statement: A proposed (unratified) mechanic specifies what happens when a Standing-3+ player wins a social contest against their faction leader: a won contest produces a Faction Priority Adjustment — Success downweights the contested AI priority one level for one season; Overwhelming persists it two seasons and gives the leader a Conviction Wound; a loss leaves the Duty unchanged, costs Disposition −1, and grants the leader's faction +1D on its next Domain Action.

name: Parliamentary Intent scene action (unratified)
