statement: A proposed (unratified) mechanic lets a Standing-3+ player declare "Parliamentary Intent" as a Personal-Phase scene action (no faction-hand card consumed) converting personal-scale investigation/diplomacy outcomes into parliamentary capital: Evidence at Complex threshold against a rival adds +1D to that faction's next Ratification roll; a successful Diplomacy scene with a neutral faction adds +1D to the player's faction's Diplomacy pool on any Treaty initiated that season.

name: Occupation state generates a distinct Resistance Scene subtype (unratified)
statement: A proposed (unratified) mechanic specifies that an Occupied territory generates a distinct Scene Slate subtype, Resistance Scenes, as Priority-1 entries for any character of the displaced faction operating there; the Scene Graph always includes a resistance-figure Anchor node, an Evidence node, an Observation node, and a Mandate-gated Access node. A faction_layer §2.5 Resistance Check can be initiated as a free Accounting action from within such a scene.

name: 'What must not change' constraints binding on faction/territory design
statement: Two protected design elements bear directly on faction/territory design: the Accord Gate on Conquest (occupied/conquered territories are locked at Accord 1 and cannot contribute to Universal Victory, "makes conquest require governance without a 'no attacking' rule," must not be softened) and Domain Echo directionality (Echo flows personal→strategic ONLY; the strategic layer affects the personal layer exclusively through Scene Slate generation and Zoom-In triggers, never through Echo — "confusing these channels would make the system circular and unpredictable").

name: The zoom-system architecture supersedes three-mode branching (CANONICAL no-GM collapse)
statement: The videogame collapses TTRPG/BG/Hybrid mode-branching into two simultaneous scales (Strategic, Personal) connected by a zoom system with no mode switch: mandatory Zoom-In triggers, elective Season-Slate scenes, and Domain Echo replace all prior session-boundary/mode-transition machinery. This document rules "There is no GM. All resolution is engine-handled... All ambiguous rulings in the design docs that say 'GM decides' must be resolved to deterministic rules or authored content" — and provides a formal five-type resolution register (Authored / Deterministic / AI-driven / Player choice / Default).

name: scale_transitions_v30's literal GM language was never run through this document's own resolution register
statement: This CANONICAL document explicitly discards "GM adjudication" and requires every "GM decides"- type phrase to be resolved via its register. scale_transitions_v30.md — a companion CANONICAL document — still contains the literal phrases "GM adjudication" (§1 mode table) and "GM recognises faction scope" (§3.2) unresolved, confirming both are live violations of this document's own no-GM discipline rather than merely stylistic leftovers.

name: Faction/NPC-behavior mode collapse
statement: Faction Layer's Hybrid treaty/diplomacy system (§8.3) and Grand Debate (fires as a Zoom-In event) are ruled the videogame's canonical faction-diplomacy path; Officer Fate auto-resolves when not zoomed into. NPC Behavior's strategic-scale faction-priority-tree AI runs every season, translated to/from personal-scale NPC behavior at Zoom boundaries; every "GM decides NPC reactions" instance is ruled to become an NPC Stance-Triangle + Conviction decision tree.

name: This document's '36 settlements' figure predates the later 37-settlement canonical count
statement: This document (2026-04-17) states "36 settlements are data" for the Settlement Layer mode collapse. A much later resync (ners_vsg_reconciliation_v1 §5 item 3, 2026-07-13) migrated the geography YAML to a canonical 37-settlement table. This document was never updated to reflect the settlement-count change.

name: The auto/manual resolution fidelity doctrine — calibration constraint and forks
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-07-08 (ED-SC-0013) that every Scene Slate event has a resolution-fidelity spectrum: Played / Witnessed / Auto, precedented by Football Manager. Three of four forks were resolved: (A) one engine at two fidelities — auto is the same contest kernel run headless, played run interactively; (B) the escalation predicate is simply the existing Scene Slate triage; (D) both forced and chosen scenes coexist, Slate-marked mandatory events forcing a scene, overflow falling to Witness Mode. Fork C (calibration tolerance) was left open.
baseline_ref: scale_transitions_v30 §8.1 (H7A-002 mentions this ruling; this adds the full fork resolution)

name: Calibration constraint (fork C, still open)
statement: Across fidelities, a slate event's outcome distribution must be consistent on matched inputs to prevent "mode-shopping" — picking whichever fidelity yields the better strategic-layer consequence. The lean stated (not yet ruled numerically): unbiased MEAN is a hard constraint, but variance may be looser for auto; the actual tolerance number is deferred to a not-yet-built parity harness, the acceptance gate for the ED-SC-0011 zoom-in-expansion work.
formula: E[auto outcome|event] ≈ E[played outcome|event]

name: The shipped Parliamentary auto-resolver violates the slate-specificity principle
statement: The first shipped auto-resolver (the faction-scale §10 Parliamentary vote) is a generic per-season roll rather than the resolution of a specific motion drawn from the Scene Slate — violating the doctrine's core principle. The chief unbuilt implication is to event-parameterize the auto-resolver so it resolves the actual named motion each season. The provisional parliamentary derivation (lowest-Stability proposes, highest-Mandate is establishment, others abstain) that shipped ON by default is explicitly NOT ratified as canon.

name: Generational Transition — full PRESERVE/TRANSFORM/RESET/BREAK/TRANSFER taxonomy
statement: On PC death or Portrait Retirement, world state partitions into five categories: PRESERVE (all faction/derived/clock/settlement/territory/NPC-to-NPC state persists), TRANSFORM (Legacy Conviction transforms; Resources partially inherit as floor(predecessor/2)+new starting), RESET (Disposition-toward-PC, Standing, Coherence, TS, Truth, Wounds, Stamina, Momentum, Exposure, skills and attributes all restart fresh), BREAK (all Knots rupture with strain to the NPCs; companion relationships fire a departure scene), and TRANSFER (Active Obligations pass to the new character via the faction, inheriting countdown and violation conditions; Renown resets to 0 but a predecessor's Renown≥7 grants +1 starting Renown).
formula: Resources = floor(predecessor/2) + new_character_starting; Renown: reset 0, +1 if predecessor Renown≥7

name: Tensions Deck pairwise validation — all 15 combinations pass
statement: All 15 possible pairings of the 6-card Tensions Deck were validated against a three-part test (belligerent, target, opportunity/obligation) — all 15 pass, each card appears in exactly 5 pairs, and no faction is uninvolved in more than 5 of the 15 pairs. The weakest pair (C5+C6, two purely internal-suppression crises, no direct attack) is flagged as an intentionally "cold start" scenario giving the player more room to set their own agenda.

name: PP-675 Three-Scale Resolution Model is a third rival to the corpus's territory-hierarchy models
statement: This PROPAGATED patch (PP-675) specifies a bottom-up three-layer season resolution — Settlement (resolves first) → Province (fragmentation, Accord as floor-average of settlement Order, PV) → Peninsula (clocks, victory) — matching conflict_architecture_proposal.md's later Peninsula/ Province/Settlement model. Both predate and differ in tier-count from the eventually-ruled five-tier Settlement→Territory→Province→Duchy→Country hierarchy; none of the three documents cross-references the others' scale-count.

name: Bishop Appointment full degree table (PP-675)
statement: This PROPAGATED patch specifies the Church Ecclesiastical Appointment action's full degree table (Overwhelming/Success install a bishop-governor, Partial leaves the governor with Church Stability −1, Failure alerts the controlling faction with no Casus Belli), framing this as "the pre-Seizure accumulation path" with Mass Seizure at "CI 60+" as the capstone — a different CI threshold than campaign_architecture_v30's later CI=100 Mass Seizure Declaration for the same escalation relationship.

name: RM Settlement Emergence threshold hardened to Order=0 exactly
statement: A propagated fix (B2-2) hardened RM's Settlement Emergence trigger from "Order ≤ 1" to "Order = 0 exactly" (plus PT≤1 and Disposition toward Vossen ≥+3), because Order≤1 fired too early and produced deterministic RM growth; Order=0 represents complete governance collapse and creates genuine variance.
formula: RM Emergence: Order=0 (hard) AND PT≤1 AND Disposition(Vossen)≥+3

name: Faction-splinter succession asset split — Influence now splits 60/40 alongside Mandate
statement: A propagated fix (B2-3) changed faction-succession splinter asset division: Influence, previously unsplit, now splits 60% (round down) to the winner and 40% to the splinter with the remainder lost, matching Mandate's existing split — because leaving Influence whole made the Mandate floor have zero effect on splinter viability.
formula: Influence split: winner 60%, splinter 40% (round down each), remainder lost

name: Secession candidate restriction — subnational-held settlements cannot secede further
statement: A propagated fix (B2-1) restricted Fragmentation-Check Secession candidates to settlements controlled by a national faction; settlements already held by a subnational faction (RM, Wardens) or marked Uncontrolled cannot secede further — if every non-Seat alien settlement in a province is subnational, the would-be Secession Failure instead produces only an Order drop.

name: NPC Recruitment procedure
statement: A four-step NPC recruitment procedure: Identify a target, Approach (Charisma×2+History+3, Ob=floor(NPC's highest Disposition/2)+1), Offer (one incentive lowering Ob by up to 2, a "Strong Hook" dropping it to Ob 1), then Resolution. Failure warns the target with no retry for 2 seasons; Success recruits and costs the current faction Mandate −1; Overwhelming recruits with the new NPC's Disposition +2 and brings Evidence.
formula: Approach: (Cha×2+H+3), Ob=floor(highest Disp/2)+1; Success: current faction Mandate−1

name: Crown Decree Mandate-gate patch (PP-NPC-01)
statement: A patch (PP-NPC-01) gates Crown Decree on Mandate ≥3 specifically to prevent a death spiral where the Crown NPC AI issues Decrees at low Mandate, fails, and loses further Mandate — a self-reinforcing collapse loop the patch closes by disallowing the action below the threshold.
formula: Crown Decree requires Mandate ≥ 3

name: Territory-scale value ranges (0-4, balanced at 2) — possible collision with settlement-layer's 0-5/0-7 ranges
statement: This CANONICAL registry defines four per-territory values on a 0-4 range balanced at 2: Accord (0 Revolt through 4 Aligned, gating Prosperity contribution and Battle bonuses), Piety (0= Restoration pole, 4=Solmund pole, Church Seizure Ob=6−Piety), Prosperity (gates Wealth and muster Size), and Fort Level. This 0-4 range is distinct from — and not cross-referenced against — settlement_layer's later Settlement-scale Prosperity/Order/Defense (0-5) and Legitimacy/PS (0-7) ranges, raising the same kind of collision the governance_type_registry's §2.8 table catalogues for other tracks.
formula: Accord 0-4 (0:Revolt,1:Resistant,2:Compliant,3:Supportive,4:Aligned); Prosperity→Muster Size: 0-1=Size2, 2-3=Size3, 4=Size4

name: Faction card-hand system — per-faction domain-action decks with expertise bonus
statement: Each of four national factions has a distinct 6-card Domain Action hand with a named expertise bonus: Crown (Legionary expertise), Church (Senator expertise), Hafenmark (Consul/Prefect expertise), Varfell (Tribune expertise); most cards have a 1-season cooldown, Pontifex/Prefect/ Colonist cooldown 2 seasons, Recess has none.

name: Faction-specific personnel/political tracks roster
statement: A named roster of faction-specific tracks: VTM (Varfell, 0-5), Warden Cooperation (shared, 0-3), Warden Recognition (Varfell, 0-4), Torben Loyalty (Crown→Löwenritter, 0-7, starts 3), Elske Loyalty (Crown, 0-7, starts 4), and Coup Counter (Löwenritter, hidden, 0-4) — with Altonian diplomacy, RDT, Patience Counter and Intel Advancement Counter explicitly struck.

name: Only 1 of 8 declared cross-scale handoff pairs is production-reachable
statement: A code-verified trace confirms handoff_rules.apply_handoff — the mechanism realizing scale_ transitions_v30 §3's eight named handoffs — is production-reachable for exactly ONE of its 8 declared (from_scale, to_scale) pairs, (Scene, Faction), via a two-entry dispatch dict that both map to the same pair; the other 7 handoff rules exist only as test-exercised code, never reached by any live dispatch call in a seeded campaign.
baseline_ref: scale_transitions_v30 §3 (H7A-004 through H7A-010, the eight handoffs)

name: The Thread Domain Echo leg has zero callers anywhere
statement: domain_echo.compute_thread_echo — the code implementing scale_transitions_v30 §5.6's Thread Domain Echo — has ZERO callers anywhere in the corpus, including tests; it is entirely dead code despite being fully implemented.
baseline_ref: scale_transitions_v30 §5.6 (H7A-024, the Thread Domain Echo mechanic)

name: npc_ai.py, the engine's dedicated NPC-decision module, is a fully orphaned stub
statement: engine/autoload/npc_ai.py's two declared entry points (select_action, evaluate_priority_stack) are both unconditional typed no-ops AND are never called by any production code — the live season-loop dispatch calls faction_take_action directly instead, bypassing npc_ai entirely, even though npc_ai's own module docstring names faction_action as a dependency (the dependency direction is backwards from what's documented).

name: The live parliamentary vote derivation and only-one-live-termination-guard finding
statement: Code-verified facts: (1) the parliamentary auto-resolver's `_derive_vote` mechanically picks the proposer as the faction with lowest Stability and the establishment side as the faction with highest Mandate, skipping the vote entirely if fewer than two eligible factions exist; (2) of the substrate's two documented termination guards, the cascade-depth cap and the B1 no-sync- re-entry gate are BOTH structurally unreachable in production — only the per-tick emissions cap is a live guard.

name: The Church Tribunal is implemented twice, sharing canon but no code
statement: The Church Tribunal exists as two independent code implementations — once as a Social Contest kernel proceeding and once inside the faction lane (tribunal.py::run_excommunication_tribunal) — sharing the same canon prose but zero shared code between the two implementations.

name: The per-settlement Mandate/Treasury pipeline has no step in the live accounting cascade
statement: The ratified per-settlement Mandate/Treasury pipeline (LPS-1/LPS-2e) has no corresponding step anywhere in run_accounting's cascade — the gap is recorded in that module's own port-blocking note. This is the accounting-cascade-level confirmation of the L/PS-inert finding captured elsewhere.
baseline_ref: derived_stats_v30 §14.1 footnote (H7A-095, the LPS-2e ruling and its inert-in-sim status)

name: Two uncoordinated settlement-scale entity families built at world-gen, cross-validated by nothing
statement: World-creation builds two uncoordinated settlement-scale entity families from two different data sources within the same create_world call, cross-validated by nothing but a report-only probe that only measures the resulting divergence rather than reconciling it.

name: A contract-layer wiring cycle spans factions/npcs/characters/social_contest
statement: A structural wiring cycle in the contract layer spans four subsystems — factions, npcs, characters, and social_contest — as measured by a 2026-08-06 vector audit's structure-metrics pass.

name: settlement_economy is a phantom module with an open retire-vs-merge decision
statement: The settlement_economy module is a "phantom" contract entry (declared, no corresponding real code/edges) with an explicitly open Jordan decision on whether to retire or merge it; a related item (ED-SE-0005) is noted resolved only for the settlement-action half, not the module- disposition half.

name: Hybrid Gap Resolutions is a pre-videogame, GM-dependent design layer
statement: This document resolves 17 tabletop "hybrid mode" design gaps (session structure, cross-system handoff batching to a Cascade phase, fog-of-war display bands, board-order→scene triggers, Wealth/Resources stress formula, PC death→faction Crisis, faction collapse→personal consequences) from a 2026-03-26 session, predating the no-GM videogame architecture. Nearly every resolution explicitly assigns judgment to "the Game Master" — directly the kind of language videogame_mode_spec.md later rules must be resolved to deterministic/AI-driven/ authored mechanics before implementation. None of these 17 resolutions appear to have been re-derived for the engine.
baseline_ref: videogame_mode_spec.md §3/§4 (H7A-150/151, the no-GM resolution register and GM-adjudication discard)

name: Campaign Modes (TTRPG/BG/Hybrid session structure) is GM-dependent, superseded
statement: This UNVERIFIED skeleton specifies three-mode session pacing, endgame indicators, and mode-specific rule-branching, explicitly titling one section "The Game Master as Rendering Engine" and repeatedly assigning judgment to "the Game Master" — the same class of GM-dependent design videogame_mode_spec.md rules must be resolved and explicitly discards wholesale. None of this document's concrete session-pacing numbers were carried forward into the ratified no-GM architecture.
baseline_ref: videogame_mode_spec.md §0/§4 (H7A-150, no-GM ruling and discard list)

name: The 'empty' §3.3 and §8 sections have unmerged, GM-dependent infill content
statement: The live scale_transitions_v30.md skeleton's §3.3 (Personal→Scene/Contest) and §8 (Scope Shift Rules) have empty bodies (flagged as ED-IN-0049's gap). This companion infill file — from the same 2026-04-13 atomization, never reintegrated into the skeleton — actually specifies both: §3.3 states a personal roll may open or Appeal a formal Contest; §8 specifies a once-per-round free scope-shift with a second shift in the same round costing +1 Inspiration. Both pieces use GM-dependent language ("GM makes final scope determination," "Ties: Agility. Further ties: GM") inconsistent with the later no-GM ruling — so the "empty section" framing is technically wrong (content exists), but that content is itself stale and was never re-derived as a deterministic rule.

name: Peninsular Sovereignty (GD-1 sole victory condition)
statement: All factions share one victory path: control all 15 playable territories (directly or via effective hegemony), Accord ≥ 2 in all directly-controlled territories, and Turmoil ≤ 6, sustained for 2 consecutive Accountings. Effective hegemony counts a rival's territory if that rival is Treaty-bound, Submitted, or institutionally dominated (Mandate ≤ 1 vs hegemon Mandate ≥ 5).
formula: held >= 15 AND all(held.accord >= 2) AND Turmoil <= 6, sustained 2 seasons

name: Faction-specific victory conditions — struck by GD-1
statement: Jordan ruled 2026-05-17 (GD-1, canon/02_canon_constraints.md) that Peninsular Sovereignty is the ONLY faction victory. Every faction-specific condition set previously in victory_v30.md §0.1, §3.1-§3.6, §4, and §8 (Crown Peninsula Sovereignty/Dominion, Church Solmundan Orthodoxy and Mass Seizure declaration-as-victory, Hafenmark Dynastic Assertion, Varfell's three Paths, RM Cultural Revolution, Löwenritter Regency, all co-victory pairings, RM Founding-as-victory) is struck and preserved only as supersession-trail evidence; they now describe HOW a faction pursues the one universal goal, not alternate endpoints. No `faction_specific_victory()` function may exist in code.
status_evidence: engine/autoload/victory.py:1-20 (module docstring: 'peninsular_sovereignty is the SOLE victory function per GD-1')

name: Turmoil clock has zero write sites — GD-1 gate is structurally a no-op
statement: `world.clocks['Turmoil']` is initialized once to 0.0 at world creation and read by `victory.check_peninsular_sovereignty` as the sole gate on the GD-1 Political-Stability clause (Turmoil ≤ 6). No code anywhere writes to it. `ps_ok` is therefore unconditionally True for the life of every campaign, and the Turmoil clause of the sole win condition never actually constrains a win. This is independently recorded in `references/module_contracts.yaml`'s own `peninsular_strain` entry and tracked open under ED-WR-0004 (ruled: wire Turmoil writes via peninsular_strain).

name: VICTORY_THRESHOLD dead parameter
statement: `mc_v18.DEFAULT_PARAMS['VICTORY_THRESHOLD']` is declared with value 11 but never read by any production code path — the live GD-1 gate is `engine/autoload/victory.py`'s own module constant `VICTORY_THRESHOLD = 15`, a completely different, unwired owner. Pinned live by a falsifier test that sweeps the dead param 11→999→1 and shows win_share never moves.
status_evidence: engine/mc_v18.py:50-62 (dead DEFAULT_PARAMS entry); engine/autoload/victory.py:27 (the real constant)

name: Undocumented fallback winner formula (non-GD-1 path)
statement: When no faction satisfies GD-1 sustained-2-season Peninsular Sovereignty by the season cap, `mc_v18.run_campaign` computes a fallback winner entirely outside `engine/autoload/victory.py`: among parliamentary factions with territories, it scores held-territory count against `ALL_PLAYABLE_15` plus `Faction.L` plus `len(Faction.territories)`, and takes the max. This formula is undocumented in `references/module_contracts.yaml`'s victory entry, which lists only the GD-1 resolver.
formula: score = held_count + Faction.L + len(Faction.territories)

name: Four world-state era victory gates declared but unimplemented
statement: `references/module_contracts.yaml` declares four world-state-era gates on the `victory` module — `g_ms0` (MS=0 → Post-Calamity Era), `g_ms5` (sustained MS≤5 → Second Calamity), `g_msrec` (MS recovery), `g_diss` (all-factions-dissolved → Anarchy Era) — corresponding to victory_v30.md §5 / peninsular_strain_v30.md §6.4's World-State Transitions. None appear in `engine/autoload/victory.py`, whose only exported checks implement GD-1 alone. A repo-wide grep for the era-transition strings ("Post-Calamity", "Second Calamity", "Anarchy Era", "Phased Occupation") returns zero `.py` matches anywhere in the tree.

name: CI starting-value mismatch — design 28 vs code 30.0
statement: Every governing design surface (clock_registry_v30.md, victory_v30.md §7 "Starting CI: 28", peninsular_strain_v30.md) states Church Influence starts at 28. The executing code seeds it at 30.0. Per §0.05, code is the mechanism — the campaign genuinely starts CI at 30, not 28 — but no document records the divergence, and a session computing "seasons to CI threshold X" from the design prose would be off by 2 from turn one.

name: PI and Strain clocks are fully dead
statement: `world.clocks['PI']` and `world.clocks['Strain']` are seeded at world creation (game_state.py:338) and have no reader or writer anywhere else in the codebase, production or test. Both clocks appear in design docs (Political Influence per victory_v30.md conditions; Strain as peninsular_strain_v30's original name for the Turmoil track before its 2026-04-29 ED-743 rename) but carry zero live mechanical weight.

name: Turmoil (Strain) global pressure track
statement: Global track, range 0-10, starting 0, public. Advances from per-territory Accord ≤ 1 held by any playable faction (+1/territory, capped +3/season), faction elimination (+2 one-time), and territory Revolt (+1/event). Decays -1/season when no territory-instability advance occurred, plus -1 per active Treaty pair (capped -2/season), plus -1 for a public diplomatic resolution (max one/season). Thresholds gate escalating effects: 3-4 Legitimacy -25 all factions; 5-6 Accord -1 in one territory; 7-8 Accord -1 all non-capital + Mandate check; 9-10 Accord capped at 2, MS -1/season additional.
status_evidence: engine/autoload/game_state.py:338 (the field exists as a clock, but no code implements this accrual/decay model — see H7B-003)

name: Accord seasonal accounting steps (4c/4d/4e) never wired
statement: §7's Step 4c (per-territory Accord-1-without-garrison degrades to 0; Accord-0 Revolt fires Popular Uprising or the territory goes Uncontrolled; garrisoned-2-quiet-seasons passive normalisation) and Step 4d (Turmoil threshold-effect application) are specified as mandatory Accounting steps. `run_accounting`'s own docstring enumerates exactly 6 live steps (CI, MS year-end, insurgency triggers, insurgency promotion, NPC ecology, Accord-drift probe) — none of which is Accord degrade/Revolt/Turmoil-threshold. A repo-wide search for "Popular Uprising" or "passive normal" in any `.py` file returns nothing.

name: Institutional Pressure (IP) track — stub
statement: Altonian Imperial Pressure world-track, 0-100, starting 20, rising. Design specifies a held-instability trigger (0-1 Accord≤1 territories → +0; 2-3 → +1; 4-5 → +2; 6+ → +3 per Accounting) plus CI≥60-sustained (+2/season) and faction-elimination (+2 one-time) sources, feeding the Phased Occupation Era (victory_v30.md §5.2). Both of the module's declared entry points are unconditional typed no-op stubs with zero production callers.

name: Accord per-territory attribute and its Prosperity/legitimacy gate
statement: Per-territory attribute, range 0-3 (Aligned/Compliant/Resistant/Revolt), modifying effective Prosperity and gating whether the territory's value counts toward victory's territory-control clause (only counts at Accord ≥ 2). Accord 1 = zero Prosperity contribution + Govern Ob +1 + garrison requirement; Accord 0 = territory becomes Uncontrolled at next Accounting.
formula: Accord 3=full Prosperity+defender+1D; 2=full Prosperity; 1=0 Prosperity, Govern Ob+1; 0=Uncontrolled
status_evidence: engine/autoload/game_state.py (Territory.accord field exists and is read/written by faction actions — see H7B-013 for the write-model split); no seasonal degrade cycle exists — see H7B-010

name: Two uncoordinated Accord write models (province vs. territory-continuous)
statement: Two write paths for "provincial Accord" coexist in the live tree without reconciliation: `registry.province_accord` (floor(mean settlement Order), a read-only aggregate) and `Territory.accord` (game_state.py's own continuous field, written directly by parliamentary_transfer.py:344 and mass_seizure.py:293, bypassing settlement Order entirely). `accounting.py` ships a report-only drift probe (`_probe_province_accord_drift`) that measures but never resolves the divergence; reconciling the two models is tracked as the SE lane's highest-priority open item (OI-37).

name: Church Mass Seizure — one-shot territorial acquisition
statement: Church may declare a one-shot Mass Seizure at CI ≥ 60, with declaration probability rising from 1% (CI 70) to 100% (CI 100, forced) per season. On declaration, every territory with a Church building becomes a simultaneous Seizure target; the Church gets exactly one attempt ever. Baseline_ref: catalogue names this BUILT and notes "produces no victory directly" (GD-1).
formula: P(declare) = clamp(((CI-60)/40)^3.3, 0, 1); Pool = Influence + floor(CI/15); Ob = max(1, 10 - PT - infra_mods)

name: Church Seizure Ob formula — three incompatible variants across the corpus
statement: Three distinct Church Seizure obstacle formulas exist in the design corpus for the same mechanic. `conviction_track_v30.md` §2 (2026-04-05, oldest): Ob = 2 + Fort Level + max(0, 3-PT). `peninsular_strain_v30.md` §5.2 cites an intermediate superseded "7-PT" formula before landing on "Formula A". The formula actually confirmed by simulation (2026-04-29) and the one the executing code implements is Ob = max(1, 10 - PT - infrastructure modifiers). Only the third is live; the first two are dead prose that a session citing conviction_track_v30.md in good faith would get wrong.
status_evidence: systems/factions/sim/mass_seizure.py:229 (the live formula, matching victory_v30.md §3.2 / peninsular_strain_v30.md §5.2's 'Formula A')

name: conviction_track_v30.md is the territorial Piety Track doc, not personal Conviction
statement: Despite living in `systems/characters/` and sharing a filename stem with the personal-scale Conviction Scar mechanic, `conviction_track_v30.md` is titled "Valoria BG — Piety Track & Church Victory Redesign" and is entirely about the territory-level Piety Track (PT), Church Seizure Ob, CI generation, and the (now GD-1-struck) faction-specific victory conditions — the same subject as victory_v30.md and peninsular_strain_v30.md, not the personal belief-system mechanic in conviction_track_v1.md. The file's own §1 note records the intended rename (conviction_track_v30.md → piety_track_v30.md) as deferred and never executed. A session resolving "Conviction" canon via filename alone lands on the wrong document.

name: Revolt → Insurgency → Faction emergence pipeline (GD-3)
statement: Jordan-directed handoff ruling (canonized 2026-05-17, canon/02_canon_constraints.md §B GD-3): new factions emerge from territorial neglect via a 4-stage progression — world-level RM PT decay (background) → Latent RM (ambient influence) → Insurgency (territory-holding, non-parliamentary) → Promoted Faction (parliamentary or extra-parliamentary). Insurgencies can invade ANY faction including the one whose neglect spawned them, and a Promoted Faction IS eligible to win via Peninsular Sovereignty with no parliamentary-status gate on victory eligibility.

name: Insurgency formation trigger (Stage 3)
statement: An Insurgency forms when 2+ contiguous territories are at Uncontrolled status, sustained for 2 consecutive seasons. It starts non-parliamentary (Legitimacy 1.0), can hold and invade territory, and is a valid invasion target, but cannot vote, sign formal Crown Treaties, or initiate Parliamentary Transfer. This is one of the few campaign-live governance mechanics — it runs every season via accounting.
formula: trigger: |contiguous_uncontrolled_group| >= 2, sustained 2 seasons

name: Insurgency promotion to Faction (Stage 4)
statement: An Insurgency promotes to a formal Faction when Legitimacy ≥ 3, it holds 2+ territories, and Accord averages ≥ 4 across holdings — sustained 2 consecutive seasons. Average PT < 3 across held territories produces an anti-Church, extra-parliamentary RM-variant; PT ≥ 3 produces a generic parliamentary candidate. The status flag is permanent once set. This runs every season via accounting, iterating every open insurgency.
formula: promote if L>=3 AND territories>=2 AND avg(Accord)>=4, sustained 2 seasons; status = extra-parliamentary if avg(PT)<3 else parliamentary

name: InsurgencyRecord.Legitimacy is never incremented — Stage-4 promotion is dead code in practice
statement: `InsurgencyRecord.L` is set once at formation (1.0, INSURGENCY_STARTING_L) and never written anywhere else in the tree — no faction action, event, or accounting step increments an insurgency's Legitimacy. `check_insurgency_promotion` requires L ≥ 3 to promote and runs every season for every open insurgency, but since L can never rise above its starting value, no insurgency can ever promote to a Faction in a live campaign, despite the mechanic being correctly implemented and correctly wired. This is distinct from the H7B-013-adjacent world-gen "starting legitimacy is silently discarded" finding in the personnel-muster baseline, which is about Faction.L, not InsurgencyRecord.L.
status_evidence: systems/world/sim/insurgency_pipeline.py:69-93 (InsurgencyRecord definition, no writer of .L beyond __init__); systems/world/sim/insurgency_pipeline.py:218-221 (the L>=3 gate that can never pass)

name: RM PT decay / Latent RM emergence (Stages 1-2) — stub
statement: Stage 1 (world-level RM PT decay at 0.35 chance/arc per eligible territory) and Stage 2 (Latent RM ambient-influence emergence, triggered on Warden's Accord ≤ -2 + 3 territories at PT ≤ 1 + MS ≤ 50) are both specified in canon but implemented as unconditional typed no-op stubs. Their cited canon sources (a designs/audit balance-audit file and restoration_movement_v30.md) resolve to nothing in the working tree — `designs/` was retired 2026-07-19 and no restoration_movement-named design doc exists anywhere outside the .py file.

name: Insurgency/Promoted-Faction dissolution (4-path model) — ratified, unbuilt
statement: Jordan ratified (ED-881, 2026-05-29, RAND-precedent-validated) that both a Stage-3 Insurgency and a Stage-4 Promoted Faction dissolve via the first of four paths to trigger, in order: military defeat (territory count → 0, or L<1.0 AND territories<2), sponsor withdrawal (Legitimacy decays -0.5/season once an external sponsor faction is lost), amnesty/negotiated settlement, or persist (stalemate). Sponsor withdrawal is documented as the historically dominant defeat path. No dissolution function of any kind exists in `systems/world/sim/insurgency_pipeline.py` — an InsurgencyRecord, once created, has no code path that ever removes or dissolves it.
status_evidence: systems/world/sim/insurgency_pipeline.py:1-267 (no dissolve/collapse function of any kind for InsurgencyRecord)

name: NPC Population Engine — 5-axis genome record
statement: A generated NPC carries five axes: Stance (per active issue, 1-5), Worldview (1-2 canonical Convictions), Affiliation (faction + affiliation_loyalty 0-3 + hidden allegiance), Compromise Profile (Economic/Informational/Political/Personal/Nothing), and Volatility (1-5), plus generation provenance (deviation roll, arc-vector eligibility).

name: NPC affiliation_loyalty (0-3) vs canonical Disposition (-5..+5) scale collision
statement: `NPC.affiliation_loyalty` is a 0-3 integer scale, distinct from the canonical Relation edge (Disposition, -5..+5) that every other cross-scale reader — fieldwork, faction Cascade — uses for the same "how does this person feel about this faction/person" concept. This is already tracked as the personnel-muster baseline's "REL Disposition reconcile" work item (Disposition wins, retire affiliation_loyalty 0-3), gated on the P0.2 registry loader landing first. Still present, unreconciled, as of this read.
baseline_ref: research/personnel_muster_integration_master_v1.md §2.1 table row 'edge -> person/faction'; §11 build order 'REL reconcile Relation'

name: generate_npc has no world-gen or season-tick call site
statement: `generate_npc` is fully implemented (two-tier archetype+deviation generation per Territory Social Ecology) but is never called at world-gen or on a season-tick trigger anywhere in production. `engine.mc_v18._faction_actions_callback` records the absence explicitly via a named `stubwire.stub_resolve('generate_npc(world-gen|season-tick)', ...)` call rather than inventing a trigger, because no canon head names either an initial population count or a per-season generation rate. `npc_counter` stays at 0 for a full seeded campaign.

name: NPC territory-level stance drift (simulate_npc_actions)
statement: Every season, all NPC pairs within a territory sharing a common Conviction in `worldview` and holding adjacent Stance on some active issue roll a Volatility check; on pass, both NPCs' Stance shifts one step toward each other on one shared issue. Runs over `world.npcs`, which is empty in every live campaign because nothing populates it (H7B-025), so this mechanic is correctly built but campaign-inert by construction.
status_evidence: systems/world/sim/npe.py:353-401 simulate_npc_actions; called every season from systems/overview/sim/accounting.py:138-139

name: Generated-NPC Conviction roster mismatch — fixed
statement: Until the 2026-08-24 suite-07 reconciliation, `npe.py` hardcoded eight Conviction names (Faith, Order, Reason, Justice, Survival, Loyalty, Truth, Power) as its own `CONVICTIONS` tuple, five of which (Justice, Survival, Loyalty, Truth, Power) appear in no conviction taxonomy anywhere in the corpus, so a generated NPC's `worldview` could never be scored by the 13x4 conviction-axis matrix or the contest styles. This is now FIXED — both `npe.py` and `systems.characters.sim.conviction` read the single owner, `references/descriptor_registry.yaml:conviction_roster`, via `engine.substrate.descriptors`.
status_evidence: systems/world/sim/npe.py:78-91 (current: CONVICTIONS = descriptors.CONVICTIONS, with the retired 8-name tuple preserved in a comment as the record of the defect)

name: 13-Conviction taxonomy (PP-684)
statement: The canonical personal- and faction-scale value-frame roster: Faith, Authority, Order, Scholastic, Utility, Equity, Liberty, Precedent, Community, Identity, Warden, Virtue, Honor. Each NPC holds a vector-valued weighting across this set (structured concentration, see H7B-029) rather than a single label; Self-Other orientation is tracked as a separate orthogonal scalar (-1..+1) for whom an actor's actions benefit.
status_evidence: engine/substrate/descriptors.py:175 CONVICTIONS (single owner, read by conviction.py, npe.py, and the contest armature)

name: Structured concentration — Conviction weighting model (PP-684)
statement: An NPC's Convictions are weighted, not chosen singly: 1-3 primary Convictions carry a combined weight of 0.6-0.8, and a distributed set of cultural-background Convictions (from a named cultural template) carries the remaining 0.2-0.4. This replaced the legacy single-primary model.
formula: sum(primary_weights) in [0.6, 0.8], 1-3 entries; sum(cultural_background_weights) in [0.2, 0.4]
status_evidence: systems/characters/sim/conviction.py:44-59 (the roster and single-owner comment reference PP-684 by name, but weighting is not itself typed/enforced in conviction.py — it lives in the NPC registry, not code)

name: Per-Conviction Scar accumulation and crisis mechanic
statement: Under PP-718 (2026-05-10), Conviction Scars accumulate per-Conviction, not aggregate: an NPC with 3 primaries can be Scarred on each independently. 0 Scars = default; 1 = destabilises; 2 = weight may shift + Resonant Style activates on that axis permanently; 3+ = Conviction crisis on that axis, and the engine rolls a d6 crisis table per major decision engaging it (1-2 habitual regression, 3-4 lateral pivot to next primary, 5 Self-Other-orientation override, 6 relational pull toward last PC interaction).
formula: crisis fires at scars[conviction] >= 3, per-Conviction, not aggregate

name: PP-718 ruling — per-Conviction Scars, not aggregate
statement: Ratified Class-B system extension (full N-M-M-T-Q vetting protocol, PASS on every stage): under PP-684's structured-concentration model, Conviction Crisis fires when ANY single Conviction accumulates 3+ Scars, not when an aggregate Scar counter (summed across all of an NPC's primaries) crosses 3. The legacy aggregate reading was a single-primary-model artifact that made multi-primary NPCs crisis no faster than single-primary ones, silently defeating the point of structured concentration at the crisis layer.
status_evidence: systems/characters/sim/conviction.py:229-233 (thresholds are per-conviction keyed, matching the ruling)

name: Conviction mechanics have zero production campaign reachability
statement: `apply_conviction_scar`'s only caller, `knots.apply_knot_loss`, itself has zero production callers anywhere in the tree — reached only by its own unit tests (engine/tests/test_knots_ed912.py). `beliefs.social_success`'s only caller, `contest_legacy_stub.run_contest`, is dead code with zero callers anywhere (production dispatch migrated off it to the promoted contest kernel). `add_belief`, the sole production constructor of a `Belief`, also has zero callers — a live campaign can never contain a `Belief` object, so `revise_belief`/`social_success` would always hit their "not found" branch even if reached. The mechanic is correctly implemented (H7B-030) but unreachable end-to-end in a seeded campaign today.
status_evidence: systems/characters/characters_flow_skeleton_v1.md:143-144 (traced callers); systems/fieldwork/sim/knots.py:349-363 (the one real call site, itself uncalled)

name: Close-Knot conviction scar — corrected roster collision (ED-912)
statement: CLOSED 2026-08-24. `knots.apply_knot_loss` called `apply_conviction_scar(conviction='Loyalty')` — a name from `npe.py`'s (then-wrong, 8-name) roster and absent from conviction.py's own nine canonical names at the time — so every call silently took the unknown-name no-op branch and returned magnitude 0, while the caller's own `consequences['conviction_scar']` reported 1. A ratified mechanic (ED-912 §6.1) was a no-op that no test could observe, because the covering test asserted only the caller's announcement dict, never the actual ConvictionState store. Fixed by the descriptor-registry single-ownership change (H7B-027/H7B-028): the caller now passes 'Honor', and an unknown conviction name raises loudly instead of silently no-op'ing.
status_evidence: systems/fieldwork/sim/knots.py:361-363 (now conviction='Honor'); systems/characters/sim/conviction.py:205 (now raises on unknown name); engine/tests/test_knots_ed912.py:141 (falsifier that reads the ConvictionState store, not just the announcement)

name: Southernmost Awareness (SA) — faction stat
statement: A faction-scoped 0-7 (or 0-10 with active research infrastructure) stat measuring institutional knowledge of the Southernmost/Einhir substrate. Starting values at game start (245 AG): Crown 0, Church 0, Hafenmark 1, Varfell 2, Restoration (NPC faction) 3. Gates a ladder of faction actions from mere Parliamentary discussion (SA 1) to faction-directed Repair strategy (SA 5).
formula: starting SA: Crown 0, Church 0, Hafenmark 1, Varfell 2, RM 3
status_evidence: no code implements a southernmost_awareness field or reader anywhere in engine/ or systems/ (repo-wide grep, zero hits)

name: Miraculous Event — SA/Accord world-effect mechanic
statement: Proposed trigger: when a Mending at Ob ≥ 6 succeeds within Proximity ≤ 2 of T15 Askeheim, a Miraculous Event fires with a radius scaled to the Mending's Ob (local/regional/peninsular). Every faction with presence in affected territories gains SA +1 (one-time per event); affected territories gain +1 Accord at next Accounting and a one-time -1 Proximity-Rating modifier for RS-band lookup. The event grants awareness that something changed, not thread knowledge itself, and each faction interprets the cause differently (Church: miracle; Hafenmark: divine communion; Varfell/RM: Einhir heritage) — none requires falsehood, each requires suppressing one piece of evidence.
formula: SA += 1 per present faction (one-time); Accord += 1 at next Accounting; Proximity modifier -1 until next Accounting
status_evidence: systems/world/sim/miraculous_event.py:28-33 (trigger_miraculous_event is an unconditional typed stub, zero production callers)

name: miraculous_event_v30.md CANONICAL vs its own source document DRAFT
statement: `miraculous_event_v30.md` (an atomized extract of solmund_master_document.md §19-29) declares itself `## Status: CANONICAL`. Its own source, `solmund_master_document.md`, declares the identical content `## Status: DRAFT — all content PROVISIONAL pending Jordan editorial approval` and lists nine open editorial items gating exactly this material (Baralta direct communion, two-witness-traditions, the Miraculous Event trigger itself, SA-gated thresholds). Per §0.05, neither status line is a mechanism — the code (H7B-035) is an unconditional stub either way — but the two documents assert contradictory ratification states for the same prose, and a session trusting the atomized copy's header would treat unratified design as settled.

name: Territory adjacency graph (source table)
statement: The 17-territory map with starting control, Fort level, sub-region, and adjacency listing is the authored source for the contiguity graph that `systems.settlements.sim.adjacency.ADJACENCY` encodes and that `insurgency_pipeline._contiguous_uncontrolled_groups` BFS-walks to detect 2+-contiguous-Uncontrolled-territory insurgency triggers (H7B-018).

name: Four-Cardinal Church structure and cardinal-specific event mechanics
statement: The Church of Solmund's four Cardinal arms (Fortitude/Military, Justice/Judicial, Prudence/Economic, Temperance/Knowledge), each with a named NPC holder, carry attached designed-canonical event mechanics: Jarnstal Drift (a private 0-3 counter incrementing on unauthorised Templar deployment, at 3 splitting Church Military control away from the Confessor), Olafsson-Broker Exposure, Klapp Awakening, and Prudence Crisis. None of these named-character counters or event triggers appear anywhere in the executing code.
status_evidence: repo-wide grep for Jarnstal/Olafsson/Klapp/Prudence Crisis across engine/ and systems/*.py returns zero hits

name: Motion of No Confidence — Crown deposal mechanic
statement: A two-step deposal procedure: (1) a Parliamentary Vote, Influence vs Crown Mandate; (2) Holy See concurrence, where the Confessor chooses to concur or refuse. On Crown loss + Confessor concurrence: Crown Mandate → 1, Stability -3, and a succession sequence (Torben if loyal and available; otherwise IP +10; otherwise interregnum with Crown actions +2 Ob). On Confessor refusal: CI +3, Thread Tension +2. The clause gives the Church a structural veto over Crown regime change. Zero code implements this.
formula: step1: Influence vs Crown Mandate; step2: Confessor concur/refuse; deposal -> Crown Mandate=1, Stability-3
status_evidence: repo-wide grep for 'no_confidence'/'Motion of No Confidence' across engine/ and systems/*.py returns zero hits

name: Named Character Event Cards — governance-crisis pattern
statement: A catalogue of eight faction-specific crisis event cards, each firing on a state-threshold trigger and offering a counter-play cost: Constitutional Crisis (Crown Mandate ≤ 1 or loses 3+ territories in one season, auto-fires the Motion of No Confidence above), Ministry Collapse (Crown Stability ≤ 2, cascading Law/Taxation/Guilds/Prosperity effects), Guild Schism, Guild Forum Revolt, Prudence Crisis, Jarnstal Independence, Olafsson Exposure, and Lions' Table Mutiny. All are DESIGN-authority (working document), none is code.
status_evidence: repo-wide grep for 'Constitutional Crisis'/'Ministry Collapse'/'Guild Schism' across engine/ and systems/*.py returns zero hits

name: Court Parliament and governance body structure
statement: Five nested governance bodies: Imperial Court (advisory, informal power arena), Court Parliament (recommends policy, nominates Ministers/Rectorates/Magistrates), Ministries (execute government services), Rectorates (judicial execution), Praefectures (local governance/regional administration). Marked explicitly "Reference — not mechanics" in the source document.

name: World-State Transitions (Post-Calamity / Occupation / Anarchy Eras)
statement: Three campaign-terminal-adjacent world states, none producing a faction win/loss (GD-1 binding — "No shared loss. No fade to black."): Post-Calamity Era (MS=0, faction acquisition suspended 3 seasons, doubled Mending, 10-season recovery window to MS 20), Occupation Era (IP ≥ 100 sustained, phased Altonian invasion across three geographic corridors, +2 Ob to occupied-territory Domain Actions), and Anarchy Era (all factions Stability 0, direct personal-scale governance, Founded Organization faction-formation path). The only true campaign terminal is Second Calamity, 10 seasons sustained at MS ≤ 5. See H7B-006 for the corresponding contract-declared-but-unimplemented gates.
status_evidence: see H7B-006; none of the three era names appear in any executing .py file

name: Warden Cooperation (WC) — the world-survival contest's endgame lever
statement: A 0-3 track distinct from and complementary to Turmoil/Peninsular Sovereignty — it is the mechanism of "Contest 2" (does the world survive), where WC 3 (RS +2/season via active Edeyja Mending) is documented as the only viable endgame path to prevent Rupture. WC and political sovereignty compete for the same faction-action budget, which is the stated strategic tension.
status_evidence: no code reference to a WC/warden_cooperation field found in engine/ or systems/*.py

name: Personal-scale Knot-to-political-stakes design pattern
statement: Character Histories systematically ties each Lifepath stage's Knot to a named political stake — e.g. a Crown-heartland origin's Knot is "a parent whose safety drops with the Crown's Mandate," a Church-Investigator vocation's Knot is a past investigation subject whose fate the PC controlled. This is a content/authoring pattern connecting the personal-combat lifepath system to faction-scale governance stakes, not itself a governance mechanic; the bulk of character_histories_v30.md (skill trees, Ob modifiers, combat dice bonuses) is out of this lane's scope.

name: Askeheim/MS world-survival victory interaction
statement: victory_v30.md §6 states that ignoring T15 Askeheim trends MS toward 0 and triggers a second Calamity, and that "multiple victory conditions require MS thresholds" so a faction that ignores MS risks losing to Rupture regardless of territorial control. Given that the sole live victory path (H7B-001) checks only territory count, Accord, and Turmoil — with no MS clause — and Turmoil itself never accrues (H7B-003), the stated MS-risk-to-victory coupling described in prose does not exist in the executing GD-1 check at all.
status_evidence: engine/autoload/victory.py:52-101 (no MS read anywhere in check_peninsular_sovereignty)

name: Officer/Ascendancy naming resolution
statement: Part 40 proposes resolving the "officer" term collision with mass-battle's auto-generated unit commander by naming the rise-to-power system "Ascendancy" and its roles Retainer/Patron/Advisor. This exact resolution already stands in the baseline as a settled vocabulary table.

name: Patronage chains (M1)
statement: An NPC's rank climb is gated on an `upward_patron` edge plus a derived `clientele_breadth` score; the mechanism collapses top-down when the patron falls, decaying clientele_breadth and freezing advancement.
formula: advance: +f(clientele_breadth, upward_patron.Disposition), frozen if upward_patron stalls; downfall: patron falls -> clientele_breadth decays / cohort auto-purges
baseline_ref: cross_scale_action_catalogue_v1.md §9.3 (M1 row, line 825) — top-line summary already there; this record adds the driver/vulnerability formula, which the baseline does not carry

name: Credentialed merit (M2)
statement: Advancement requires clearing a two-stage gate (objective competence plus a discretionary sponsor bond); the bond persists after the exam, and the whole track is undone by a later rewrite of the credential criteria rather than by a rival's direct action.
formula: advance: +1 if two-stage credential gate + tutoring-investment cleared (else capped); downfall: credential_criteria rewrite re-tests the holder out

name: Kinship / marriage alliance (M3)
statement: Power rides a blood-tie rather than an office, advancing on marriage/betrothal/heir-birth Keys; it fails via a generational flip or demographic lapse — one Disposition-flip or a missed marriage voids a multi-season investment at the last step.
formula: advance: on marriage/betrothal/heir-birth Keys (A8/H1); pays a recurring rank-independent bonus once the tie holds; downfall: generational flip / demographic lapse

name: Court proximity / favoritism (M4)
statement: Informal Royal-Intimacy outperforms formal Standing (the favorite/valido shape) and collapses binary rather than graduated — loss of intimacy or the patron's death is total, often violent. Unlike the other seven mechanisms, M4 has no corresponding `power_base` enum value (the enum lists patronage/merit/kinship/bureaucratic/military/purchased/ideological, seven values for eight mechanisms) — court favoritism is instead carried by the auxiliary meters (`shadow_standing`, Royal-Intimacy), an internal inconsistency the document does not itself flag.

name: Bureaucratic chokepoint control (M5)
statement: Power accrues from sitting on a routing/access path (correspondence, seals, adjudication) without a vested office; it is undone by a single bypass channel or by succession, since authority-by-proxy has zero transferability.
formula: advance: +f(Keys successfully filtered/routed); resets to 0 if the patron falls; downfall: single bypass channel or succession

name: Purchased office / venality (M6)
statement: Rank, or a toll-post athwart it, is bought directly with Treasury; the resulting legitimacy has no loyalty reserve and evaporates the instant a rival offers something money cannot buy.
formula: advance: instant on Treasury spend; writes purchased_legitimacy/Exposure; downfall: no loyalty reserve suppresses the Coup Counter buffer

name: Armed retinue / military power-base (M7)
statement: A personal, self-loyal force is built outside the formal ladder; it falls to a coalition purge or a subordinate-flip because the ruler routes around the strength rather than matching it. This is the category the corpus flags with the highest officer/political-rank naming-collision density (~20 of 96 entries).
formula: advance: +f(retinue.leverage/autonomy, self-financing Keys); downfall: coalition purge or subordinate-flip

name: Ideological / moral authority (M8)
statement: Standing-independent legitimacy (prophetic, jurisprudential, credentialing-body) accrues without a ladder entry; it cannot be bought or demoted, only outcompeted in its own currency or purged by covert violence.
formula: advance: +f(aggregate scene.witness/scene.gossip) feeding moral_authority/renown; downfall: counter-authority in the same currency, or covert violence

name: power_base field (the Ascendancy organizing enum)
statement: A proposed enum field on the NPC sheet — {patronage, merit, kinship, bureaucratic, military, purchased, ideological} — that simultaneously types an NPC's climb driver, its downfall shape, and whether a Dismissal against it is enforceable. The document calls it "the single most load-bearing addition" in the whole roster proposal.

name: ConsolidationEngine — one engine, three scale-bindings
statement: A single ambition-engine-derived `ConsolidationEngine` with a `scale_binding` field in {settlement, court, lineage} reuses the goal/method/timeline/progress/trajectory grammar across three entity scopes. The settlement binding stays blocked on the unbuilt settlement registry; the court binding (Standing ladder + Knots graph, both already existing) is proposed as shippable without it; the lineage binding is Jordan-gated.

name: Shared rank space + bounded auxiliary meters
statement: Proposes NPCs climb the same Standing ladder as the player (not a parallel NPC-only ladder), with parallel-track pressures (moral_authority, renown, shadow_standing, service_rank, Dignity, custody_bonus) modeled as a bounded, named set of off-ladder auxiliary meters that substitute-in or force ratification, rather than as competing seat-spaces. This is explicitly the resolution to the corpus's recurring "how many parallel status/power tracks" tension (needs_jordan item 3), but is itself unratified.

name: player_seats_are_contestable toggle
statement: Whether an NPC can actually depose or supersede the player at a rank the player holds is left as a single design-taste toggle; the architecture supports either setting. The document's own inclination is yes, gated behind a coalition threshold, so the player is only deposable once over-consolidated past ordinary challenges.

name: Autonomous Ascendancy loop (advance + threshold card)
statement: Each Accounting, consolidation_progress advances via a power_base-typed driver (seven distinct formulas, one per power_base value); at threshold an "Ascendancy card" fires with a power_base-appropriate menu (claim office, betray patron, expose secret, install successor, capture the gate, cohort capture, convert to asset, press a banked claim, force ratification, purge predecessor, seize Mandate custody), emitted through the Key substrate.

name: gap" — Lineage/clan-scope object above NPC lifespan
statement: The Accounting-cascade tick needs an entity above a single NPC's lifespan to model multi-generation cases (Wang Mang's dynastic_leverage across five reigns; malikane family Entrenchment). Called "the single biggest structural ask" of the roster proposal; whether Valoria wants clan-scale actors at all is left as a scope call.

name: gap" — Coalition / joint ambition object
statement: Ambitions today are strictly per-NPC; a multi-NPC joint ambition object is needed for the Night-of-the-Long-Knives-style Coalition Purge (G6) and the Thermidor-style procedural purge (G9). Called "the clearest new-mechanic requirement" in the entire downfall set.

name: gap" — Peninsula-scale renown aggregation
statement: A jurisprudential/doctrinal `renown` track must sum witness/gossip Keys across many settlements an NPC never administers, requiring an aggregation scope above any single settlement — a gap the document calls out explicitly by name in its own framing.

name: gap" — Mandate custody separable from possession
statement: Physically controlling a Mandate-bearing figure without deposing them (Cao Cao's "support the Son of Heaven") needs `custodian_id` distinct from `holder_id`, so custody grants a legitimacy bonus while base Standing is untouched. Called "the sharpest genuine architectural gap" of the whole roster set.

name: gap" — In-transit Key interception
statement: The engine has no mechanism for one NPC intercepting another NPC's Keys before they resolve (correspondence-filtering chokepoint roles); every chokepoint-control entry in the corpus needs this primitive and none currently has it.

name: gap" — Dormant/conditional and hidden-visibility Ledger tags
statement: Two proposed new Ledger-tag capabilities are unbuilt: a tag that sits inert until a specific Key fires (`trigger_condition: succession`, for succession-cascade purges) and a tag with a hidden/concealed visibility flag that only becomes legible after an exposure Key (e.g. embezzlement Debt invisible until `audit_exposed`).

name: gap" — co_leadership state and mutable office succession_rule
statement: Part 2's succession model treats Leadership as a single binary state and offices as static slots; the corpus needs an intermediate co_leadership/shared-rule state (Romanos I Lekapenos) and a mutable per-office succession_rule (Carolingian hereditary lock-in), neither of which exists today.

name: Organization entity (own Standing ladder + AP pool)
statement: A proposed new entity type — a member roster on its own Standing ladder (parallel to, not nested inside, faction Standing), an Org AP pool, and an optional Org Treasury — representing a membership that is dispersed across settlements it does not own (guilds, orders, chartered companies). No existing state can express a body holding land or members the faction doesn't administer.

name: Territory entity (roster + governance-mode + command-split flags)
statement: A proposed new entity — a roster of settlements plus an appointed-administrator identity, a Governance-Mode flag (Local/Appointed), and a civil/military-split flag — representing a cluster held as an aggregate. This is the object the document identifies as answering both the previously-open BYZ-6 (Consolidated Command) and IT-5 (Legation Split) design questions.

name: gap" — inter-settlement propagation lever contingent on unauthored temporal model
statement: Relay Tier (0–3, propagation speed) and Beacon Network (0–3, alarm hop-radius) are named "the single strongest new-state case in the corpus," but both presume Valoria has inter-settlement latency for a turn structure to gate — a temporal model that does not exist (`engine_clock` carries `doc: null` per CLAUDE.md §6). The lever cannot be evaluated until that gap closes.

name: Shared cross-settlement Reserve Pool
statement: A treasury-like store, distinct from any single settlement's walled Treasury, that moves surplus between settlements (Inca Qollqa, Song Ever-Normal rollout). The internal interest/replenish logic is explicitly left underspecified — "a design intent, not a spec."

name: The Grant Ledger (revenue rights held by a third party)
statement: A ledger recording revenue rights over a settlement bundle held by an entity that is neither the settlement nor the whole faction (an Ottoman-timar-style grant-holder). Named the literal seam between settlement and faction scale.

name: Muster tag (land-tenure-for-defense)
statement: A proposed Ledger-tag family giving a permanent Defense floor with no ongoing Treasury upkeep, paid for by a permanent Prosperity-growth tax; it auto-answers Levy directives with troops instead of Treasury, but is Disposition-contingent — a garrison whose loyalty collapses can flip the tag to Grudge and defect.
formula: permanent Defense floor; no AP/Treasury upkeep; permanent Prosperity-growth reduction; flips to Grudge/refusal if garrison Disposition collapses

name: Cordon-Complete chain-topology flag
statement: A binary/tiered aggregation flag over a defined settlement chain (Hadrian's Wall, the Belgorod Line) that pays a bonus only while the chain is geographically unbroken; one member settlement dropping below threshold removes the bonus for the whole territory.

name: BYZ-6 / IT-5 concrete resolution shape (command-split flag + per-verb permissions table)
statement: The two previously open-ended "needs_jordan (undefined)" multi-settlement proposals now have a concrete proposed shape — a command-split flag on the Territory entity (Consolidated Command = "consolidated" setting, historically the dangerous one) and a per-verb authority-tier permissions table (Split Verb Authority, the Venetian rettori pattern) rather than an all-or-nothing legation. Still an open Jordan ruling, now a choice among specified options rather than an open design problem.

name: power_base as scale-action eligibility filter; consolidation_progress as the spent/reset resource
statement: Proposed integration rule between the Ascendancy roster system and the four-scale action menus — power_base type gates which scale-actions a character can initiate (e.g. no Raise a Standing Corps without a military basis), while consolidation_progress is the currency faction-scale structural reorgs raise, spend, or reset on a rival. Explicitly self-flagged as reading cleanly off `initiator_level` fields but not yet checked against the Ascendancy doc's own power_base semantics — needing canon-guard review before adoption.

name: gap" — Organization economy unspecified
statement: The Organization entity's resource loop is undefined — what "Org AP"/"Guild Capacity" numerically is, and how Org Treasury relates to member dues, responsions tithes, and assay fees. Called "the single biggest authoring gap" behind the whole Organization scale, including the org-scale Fugger Audit-Branch circuit-breaker (see H8A-060).

name: Territory Reach-Cap trigger (the one required number)
statement: A settlement-count or AP-load threshold past which a Territory's own Order/Π aggregates start representing "the governor can't reach everyone," forcing a Partition/Redistrict rather than an indefinite decline; explicitly flagged as the one place in the whole four-scale proposal where a bare number is unavoidable, and it is left unspecified per CLAUDE.md §5.

name: Four-scale characteristic-tension framing (Organization / Settlement / Territory / Faction)
statement: Proposes that Organization, Settlement, Territory and Faction are not four sizes of one thing but four different kinds of managed object, each with its own intrinsic tension (Organization: unity vs dispersion; Settlement: bounded budget vs compounding pressure; Territory: reach vs uniformity vs local autonomy; Faction: control vs the cost of centralization) — the framing used to derive which of the ~72 catalogued historical proposals needs new state versus a verb option on an existing scale.

name: Proactive-menu and reactive Crisis-card system must ship as one loop
statement: Several proactive-governance levers (intendants, forced annexation-compensation, standardization) are historically load-bearing for collapse (the Fronde, the Satsuma rebellion). If stacked Grudges from using them do not auto-seed Crisis-family cards, the game gets the centralizing upside with none of the historical downside — an explicitly named risk if the two systems ship sequentially rather than together.

name: Parent-verb re-indexing scheme over the event-card corpus
statement: Re-indexes the ~94-card historical event catalogue (organized by event) into the inverse view organized by parent verb — the eight base settlement verbs (Develop, Fortify, Keep Order, Hold Court, Sponsor, Treat, Levy, Investigate) plus Directive and a NEW bucket — so a designer can ask "what can a governor do, and which verb does it hang off of."

name: gap" — four unresolved reskin/duplicate mechanic clusters
statement: The source catalogue did not collapse four same-mechanic/different-name clusters: the standing famine-buffer facility (Ever-Normal Granary vs Civic Granary), the currency-clearing Directive (Recoinage vs Currency Reset), the convoy/fleet timing-exposure mechanic (Storm-Season Staging/Withdrawal vs Flota Scheduling), and the general "Crisis-gated post-loss unlock" pattern (Lighthouse, Purpose-Built Galleon, Coalition Fortify Pool) — each flagged as needing consolidation before a Godot implementer re-derives the same gate three times independently.

name: Court Officer Disposition (Keep Order lever against bribed defection)
statement: A proposed Keep Order/Treat lever that shores up a high-rank officer's loyalty specifically to deny a rival faction the Rival Cohort opening for a bribed defection or coup, motivated by the Battle of Plassey / Jagat Seth bankers case.

name: Succession-configuration Directive family (Oath, Fratricide, Partible, Elective)
statement: Four proposed succession-shaping mechanics under the Directive bucket: Extract Succession Oath (a fifth, oath-based heir claim basis that taxes defectors with Grudge/Reputation:Oathbreaker), Fratricide Law (strips all losing claimants rather than let them persist as splinters), Partible Succession (a durable founding-time config that maximizes dynastic footprint but permanently disables peaceful succession rows), and Elective Succession (routes contested succession to an electoral tally instead of pure strength/Standing math).

name: Convene Consulta / Convene Rival Assembly
statement: Two paired succession-contest mechanics — Convene Consulta tallies Standing+Disposition+Influence for a majority-wins Regency succession, bypassing the dice resolver; Convene Rival Assembly lets a losing claimant convene their own legitimating assembly and Defy the verdict, overriding a unified resolution into a permanent split.

name: Settle & Confiscate (post-Conquest personnel/land replacement)
statement: A proposed post-Conquest domain action forcing subnational faction-roster replacement and land reallocation after a "quarter denied" atrocity (Siege & Sack of Drogheda), writing a fresh Outlawed tag that raises future Grudge/Intrigue generationally.

name: Trade Writ (Levy cap on untaxed lineage wealth)
statement: A proposed Levy method capping an untaxed lineage's independent Wealth at a Disposition cost, or driving it underground (Outlawed + Grudge) if the target Rejects — motivated by the Kongo Civil Wars.

name: Hard-won lesson" unlock class (Crisis-gated post-loss unlock)
statement: A named general design pattern behind three separate proposed mechanics (Lighthouse, Purpose-Built Galleon, Coalition Fortify Pool): a mitigation is unlocked only after its associated crisis has fired once and been survived — "you must suffer the loss once before the mitigation becomes purchasable.

name: Embargo (Directive targeting a third faction)
statement: A proposed Directive type whose Comply/Bargain/Defy fork is resolved not by the settlement it targets but by the enforcing settlement, over how much of its own trade to sacrifice to damage a third faction's economy; Bargain grants a License Exception (a callable Debt chit).
formula: trigger: target holds bloc-network trade-dependent Prosperity AND hegemon Grudge-tagged toward it AND hegemon cross-faction Standing >= target's, mid-high Pi

name: Multilateral / Coalition Embargo
statement: A coalition-issued variant of Embargo (H8A-043) gated through Ministry/Consulta, whose defining feature is that it structurally removes the Bargain branch entirely — the response collapses to a binary Comply (capitulate) or Defy (Muster into war).

name: Recall (disband an appanage grantee's independent military)
statement: A proposed Directive targeting a grantee holder (not a settlement) that disbands their independently-held military; its Defy branch is diagnostic — refusal to disband confirms the grantee intends to convene a rival legitimating assembly and is itself the signal a succession is about to permanently fracture.

name: Quarter (forces Force-method Keep Order, overriding the governor)
statement: A sibling Directive to the canon Host type, coercively forcing Force-method order-keeping on a settlement for its duration and overriding the governor's own Consent/Clergy preference; ignoring the resulting Petition strain escalates to a Boston-Massacre-style Crisis that ratchets the governor's own future menu toward more coercion.

name: Nationalize Charter (crisis-gated Quo Warranto bypass via arbitration)
statement: A proposed, not-confirmed-as-enum-member Directive-shaped action seizing a Charter outside the normal 16-season Quo Warranto window once the holder's leverage has independently eroded; resolution routes through Ministry/Consulta arbitration that can override the battlefield outcome rather than the campaign deciding it.

name: Sovereign Bargain (rank-gated Bargain amendment, Standing-6+ only)
statement: Not a new Directive type but a rank-gated amendment converting an open-ended reprisal spiral under an active Suppress-family occupation into a bounded, fires-once Compact indemnity; available only to a Standing-6+ actor, so an ordinary governor cannot invoke it.

name: Reconciled Directive enum (6 canon + 6 proposed)
statement: Consolidates the live canon Directive enum (Extract, Tax, Suppress, Install, Host, Cede — verified current against `research/cross_scale_action_catalogue_v1.md` §2.3) against six PROPOSED additions (Embargo, Multilateral Embargo, Recall, Quarter, Nationalize Charter, Sovereign Bargain), with an open question of whether the last two should be full enum members or amendments on existing Directives.

name: gap" — active_directive is an unconstrained string in code, not the enum any design doc describes
statement: The live `Settlement.active_directive` field is typed `str | None` with no enum enforcement anywhere in `systems/settlements/sim/registry.py`, while three design surfaces (the canon 6-type enum, Part 43's proposed 6-type expansion, and `settlement_generator_v1.md`'s "expanded taxonomy") all assume a closed, validated Directive type set. Per CLAUDE.md §0.05, code is the mechanism — and the code currently enforces nothing.

name: gap" — a later design doc already cites Part 43's proposed Directive types as if adopted
statement: The 2026-07-13 `settlement_generator_v1.md` (PROPOSAL, one day after this compendium) draws "Directive priors from the expanded taxonomy (Extract/Tax/Suppress/Install/Host/Cede + Embargo/Recall/Quarter)" as though Part 43's proposed additions were already settled, despite both documents carrying only PROPOSED status and neither having flipped a `## Status:` line.

name: Standing crisis-defusing institution — the class definition
statement: Defines a proposed object class — a build-once facility/office/charter that must exist before its trigger fires, is family-scoped (lowers draw-weight for a whole crisis family, not one card), is self-consuming or ring-fenced from the ordinary Treasury/AP cycle, and works by decoupling a defensive function from the pressure that would otherwise starve it.

name: Water Board (ring-fenced flood-defense levy)
statement: A chartered institution — explicitly "a win condition, not an automatic grant," earned via cross-settlement Petition pressure after a catastrophic flood — funded by its own levy that is ring-fenced from Directive diversion, so a war-funding choice cannot starve flood defense.

name: Ever-Normal Granary (StockLevel auto-consume against famine)
statement: A Develop facility upgrade that accumulates a StockLevel meter via Sponsor spend in good seasons and auto-draws it when a drought/famine Crisis fires, capping severity and blocking the rebel-Ambition follow-on; decays if Treasury is diverted to Muster/Conquest instead.

name: Coalition Fortify Pool (multi-faction pre-funded siege defense)
statement: Multiple factions jointly pre-fund a threatened settlement's Fortify ahead of a known existential-siege Crisis; surviving unlocks further cross-faction pooling, so investment and survival compound across crisis cycles.

name: Loop-property recoverability classifier
statement: Reads the event catalogue's per-card "Loop" prose clause as a latent classifier sorting every crisis card into RECOVERABLE (blunted, denied escalation, survivable) versus TERMINAL (a one-way ratchet, a permanent cap, a self-reinforcing/inheritable spiral) — and finds the discriminating variable is almost always a single bit: was a standing institution built before the trigger fired.

name: gap" — the institution library covers world-state axes but not the Standing/rank axis
statement: Cross-walking the standing-institution catalogue against the 2026-07-12 stress test's 8 doom-loop patterns finds every material-axis doom-loop (Prosperity, Order, Treasury, Defense, Pi) has a named circuit-breaker institution, but none of the three Standing/rank-axis doom-loops (the universal 7/7 demotion spiral, patron-lapse un-shielding, undefined Suspicion->Recall threshold) can be broken by any facility — their fix is resolution-substrate tuning, not an institution to build. Called the "load-bearing result" of the whole synthesis.

name: gap" — Ledger tag-family proliferation across five new proposed families
statement: The corpus now proposes five additional Ledger-tag families (Compact, Concession, Outlawed, Capital-Posture, and a new Muster family) atop the existing set, with Muster/Compact flagged as possibly collapsible and Concession/Capital-Posture overlapping at frontier entries; a consolidation pass is called for before any of the five ship. This directly compounds the code-vs-design Ledger divergence recorded separately (H8A-081).

name: Fugger Audit-Branch (org-scale circuit-breaker for hidden corruption)
statement: An organization-scale institution reusing the Investigate resolver inward on the org's own branch officers, converting a hidden, silently-compounding embezzlement risk into a visible, scheduled one. Named as the pre-built circuit-breaker for the stress test's Clerk-Corruption "loaded gun" doom-loop, but not yet wired to the settlement Clerk-Capacity loop it would defuse.

name: Decoupling-vs-coupling design test for a proposed institution
statement: Proposes a falsifiable design test — a candidate standing institution is only a genuine circuit-breaker if it names the specific coupling it severs (e.g. flood funding decoupled from the war Directive); if it breaks no coupling, it is a stat bump, not a defuser.

name: Jordan's standing abstraction ruling (food-supply meters fold into Prosperity)
statement: Jordan's standing ruling is that food-supply and similar granular resource meters can abstract into Prosperity rather than requiring dedicated tracked stats; this Part is explicit that it does not override that ruling and treats it as the default for every proposed stat below. Verified consistent with the live tree — `Settlement` in registry.py carries no SiltLevel/StockLevel/OreGrade/etc. fields.
status_evidence: systems/settlements/sim/registry.py:55-84 (no granular resource-meter fields present, consistent with the ruling)

name: Depth-layer track-vs-abstract decision framework
statement: A three-question test for whether a proposed environmental stat should be tracked explicitly or folded into Prosperity: is the fuse cross-settlement (a Prosperity number can't carry info between settlements), is it multi-decade (outlives the governor who caused it), and does a proposed institution need a legible gate to check against.

name: RisingWaterLevel — the one stat the abstraction ruling cannot absorb
statement: A hidden cross-settlement tag where an upstream settlement's Scour choice silently raises a downstream settlement's flood risk, invisible to that settlement's own governor until a delayed Crisis fires. Applying the framework in H8A-062, this is the one proposed stat where abstraction to Prosperity genuinely breaks the mechanic, since Prosperity is local by construction and the entire dramatic point is that the downstream sheet shows nothing wrong.

name: gap" — StockLevel is blocked on an unresolved binary adopt/reject decision, not a granularity spectrum
statement: Unlike the other seven proposed stats, StockLevel cannot be "a little bit tracked": either food supply stays fully abstracted to Prosperity and Ever-Normal Granary becomes a flat method with no separate meter, or the granary mechanic is adopted whole-cloth with its own tracked StockLevel — a half-tracked meter that exists but doesn't really gate anything is explicitly called worse than either pure option.

name: SiltLevel — conditional tracking recommendation (province-tier only)
statement: Recommends tracking SiltLevel only where a province-tier institution (Water Magistracy) consumes it as a shared veto gate; single-settlement harbor siltation with no cross-settlement lagoon can abstract to a Prosperity-trajectory modifier instead.

name: Verified — 58-proposal partition matches the index's claimed counts
statement: Counted directly against the register's own tables (§3.2a–d): 12 authored into PR#119, 9 promote-ready unlanded, 23 needs-Jordan, 14 cut, summing to 58 — an exact match to `00_index.md`'s claimed 12/9/23/14 partition. Unlike Part 42's verb count, this claim verifies clean.

name: IT-3 "Sforza Gambit" reinstatement — bounded force-seizure/emergence resolver
statement: A cut proposal (mercenary-captain converts a condotta into sovereignty when his employer destabilizes) that a 2026-07-12 stress test reproduced end-to-end with no resolver to cover it — the single strongest reinstatement candidate of the four, and the register's

name: VEN-SE-4 "Dedizione" reinstatement — mid-tenure negotiated extraction cap
statement: A cut proposal (negotiated submission treaty preserving local privilege for legitimacy at an extraction cap) that recurred as a partial fix across four of seven stress-test seeds; its stated duplicate (SE-5) only fires at annexation, not mid-tenure, so the shape it fills is genuinely unfilled elsewhere.

name: VEN-SE-7 "Sindici Inquisitori" reinstatement — roving Π-suppression audit floor
