statement: The Key substrate offers two emission channels — deferred-apply (sched.emit(key, apply=fn), writes state at accounting_boundary()) and log-only (sched.emit(key), writes nothing) — plus a subscription channel (sched.subscribe); articulation.py is the only production .subscribe() call site in the tree, and every one of its 13 subscribed callbacks is a stubwire.stub_resolve no-op.

name: The Cascade Emission Path Is Switched Off by Default and Has Never Run in Production
statement: schedule_emission() (the B1 cascade path, OF-B1) has zero production callers; the only references outside keys.py are in tests/valoria/test_key_substrate.py, and DEFAULT_CASCADE_DEPTH_MAX = 0 means a cascade emission during drain would raise TerminationBreach under default parameters if it ever ran — the cascade half of the substrate is not merely unused, it is switched off by default.

name: Only 5 of 55 Key Types Are Ever Emitted in Production, Two of Them Silently
statement: Four call sites carry five live-emitted type_ids (scene.accord_echo, scene.contest_resolved, scene.combat_resolved write state via apply=; da.public_governance and scene.battle_concluded are log-only) — 9% of the 55 declared types. Both log-only emits sit inside swallowing try/except blocks that re-raise only under VALORIA_STRICT_KEYS, so under a payload defect they silently log nothing by default.

name: Subscription and Emission Were Wired Independently and Barely Overlap
statement: Of the 13 type_ids articulation.py subscribes to, 11 are never emitted by any live producer; of the 5 live-emitted types, only 2 (scene.combat_resolved, scene.accord_echo) are subscribed, and scene.contest_resolved — one of the three types that actually writes state — is subscribed by nobody. No join test exists asserting every live-emitted type has a live subscriber.

name: The Registry Grew Around World Events, Not Entity State Changes
statement: mechanical_event (world events) has 12 members against state_transition (entity state changes)'s 7 physical / 9 logical members; 7 of 8 proposed keys in this register land in state_transition, and 11 of 12 identified broken throughlines (faction lifecycle, standing, conviction resolution, project formation, treaty, affiliation, province coherence, territory revolt) break at the consumer-or-state end, not the producer end — the engine can say what happened and largely cannot record or hear it.

name: scene.accord_echo Is the One Fully Closed Key-Driven State-Write Loop
status_evidence: engine/cross_scale/echo_transport.py:345; engine/tests/test_accord_echo.py enforces the causes[] honesty rule
formula: scene resolves -> emit_scene_echo -> Key(scene.accord_echo, scale=[settlement], targets=[{actor_id: sid, stat_deltas:{order: delta}}]) -> sched.emit(key, apply=_apply) -> accounting_boundary() -> Settlement.order written
statement: The only path in the tree where a Key emission changes settlement-scale state end to end: a resolved scene emits scene.accord_echo, which writes Settlement.order at the accounting boundary and carries causes=[upstream_key_id] honestly (empty only when no real upstream Key exists). Every proposed key in this register should be read against this as the working template.

name: TN7 Domain-Action / Directive Resolver-Odds Table (d_sigma)
formula: P = p_success(base_Ob, pool, net_sigma), TN7; net_sigma from advantage levels: minor .25 / moderate .5 / strong .75 / major 1.0 (negative = disadvantage)
statement: Exact governor-verb/Directive resolution probabilities computed directly from sim/autoload/sigma_leverage.py's p_success() closed-form (a continuous normal-CDF, not the deck's design-stated linear "+10%/pt" model) — e.g. base_Ob 3, pool 7, +major advantage resolves at 78%, not the ~90% a linear reading would suggest.

name: Settlement-Season Stress Test Method (7-Seed Agent-Driven Playout, Depth-3 Failure Tracing)
statement: A 13-agent Workflow ran 7 diverse seeds x 5 seasons of PR#119's provisional governance mechanics (12 comparative-governance items, a governance-ripple substrate, a 58-card event deck) as an agent-driven mechanical play-out — there is no executable settlement-season engine, so the resolution engine acted as the ruleset directly — tracing every major roll's failure branch to depth 3, then cross-checked every parseable roll against the actual engine code.

name: Tragic-Downfall Demotion Spiral Confirmed by Two Independent Methods (Pattern A)
statement: The agent-narrative stress test's Pattern A (any negative-Need/positional resolution_quality Key accumulates to a Demotion whose Appeal then fails — universal 7/7 seeds) is independently confirmed by a completely different, EXECUTED methodology: the prior 500-seed x 120-season settlement_mgmt_stress_01 run found IP/CI/Turmoil pinned near ceiling, near-universal faction elimination (mean 3.6 of 4), Flourishing crowded out (3.7/seed vs 659 revolts/seed), and Domain Echo firing max-depth 100% of the time. Two independent methods converging on "the system is biased to death-spirals" is the single strongest result across both exercises, and is a direct NERS P-iii/P-iv constraint (unrecoverable failure, no underdog floor) on any new governance proposal. The 500-seed run's own test harness (tests/sim/settlement_mgmt_stress_01/) no longer exists in the working tree (sim/ retired 2026-07-21) and its numbers cannot be independently re-verified from disk today; they are recorded here as the reconciliation doc reports them.

name: Pi Death-Spiral (No Circuit-Breaker) — General Mechanic Still Unfixed, Goldenfurt-Specific Fix Verified Live
status_evidence: systems/settlements/goldenfurt_slice/sim_build_spec.md:139 (`[verify fix CG-1] BIDIRECTIONAL: +1 toward 3 when Pi<3, -1 when Pi>3`), verified present in the current tree
formula: pre-fix: decay_toward(3) only pulls down (pins toward 0 when Pi<3); Goldenfurt fix CG-1: sign(3-Pi)*min(1,|3-Pi|), a bidirectional restoring term
statement: The stress test's Pattern B (Pi climbs past the R-4 7->8 band cliff and pins with no Grudge decay and no circuit-breaker, producing a self-sustaining death spiral in ~6/7 seeds) reproduces a mis-signed Pi decay term already caught and fixed as CG-1 in the Goldenfurt governance vertical slice (verified present in the current tree), but that fix lives in one narrative fixture's spec, not in a general engine-wide Pi mechanic — whether the general settlement-season Pi homeostat carries the same bidirectional restoring term is unconfirmed.

name: Recall/Suspicion Death-Spiral Fix Shipped for the Goldenfurt Slice (G606 v1.1)
status_evidence: systems/settlements/goldenfurt_slice/README.md:75 ("Fixed in v1.1... the G606 recall death-spiral (a Submit to audit escape + Konrad-capped +1/season)"), verified present in the current tree
statement: The stress test's Pattern G (Suspicion accrues toward Recall at an undefined threshold, sometimes ruled by fiat) is already fixed for the Goldenfurt slice specifically: G606 ships a Submit-to-audit escape (always available, -2 suspicion) and a Konrad-capped +1/season advance, with the suspicion increment defined as +1 per Defy, capped +1/season — but this fix, like CG-1, is scoped to one narrative fixture rather than confirmed as the general recall mechanic.

name: Seggio Force-Seizure "Terminal Lock" Overstated — a Violent Removal Path Exists, a Political One Does Not
statement: The stress test's CRITICAL finding (§3.3c Seggio Council has no force/seizure resolver, making a heresy investigation unadjudicable for a full arc) is overstated: infrastructure.py implements a seizure_ob_modifier and settlement_adjacency_v30 + the mass-battle layer provide Siege/Assault as a violent removal mechanic (Goldenfurt's G603 confirms removal "needs a Mass Battle / Mandate Challenge"). The residual, real gap is narrower: the non-violent "Mandate Challenge" political removal path is a forward reference (political_hierarchy §2.4 names it, defines no procedure) — downgraded CRITICAL to MEDIUM.

name: Mandate-Saturation Finding Tested a Formula the Code Does Not Implement
statement: The stress test's Pattern H (Mandate = round(7T/(T+6)) saturates and masks peripheral collapse) tested settlement_layer §1.8 prose the code does not implement; the built aggregation is floor-average Order plus summed Prosperity, and peripheral collapse is actually carried upward by province fracturing (political_hierarchy §2.3), not by a Mandate number. Separately, L/PS are declared-but-inert in code (ED-FA-0004, port-blocking), so the whole L/PS->Mandate machinery the seeds leaned on was not wired at all at the time of the stress test.

name: Ruling — Compact Is a Debt Subtype, Not the Ledger's 6th Family (Resolves the Compact-vs-Leverage Collision)
status_evidence: systems/settlements/sim/ledger.py:30 (TAG_KINDS = {Precedent, Grudge, Debt, Reputation, Leverage}, verified directly — no Compact member)
statement: ED-IN-0046 D3 (RATIFIED 2026-07-13) rules that PR#119's proposed 'Compact' ledger tag models as a recurring Debt subtype, not a 6th ledger family — resolving, one day after it was raised, the settlement-season stress test's flagged collision between PR#119's Compact and the built 5th ledger family, Leverage. The ruling is superseded here as `superseded` on the ORIGINAL collision claim only; see H9-068 for a live, unresolved re-emergence of the same naming conflict in a later document.

name: Gap — The Most Current Baseline's Own "Five Tag Families" Table Contradicts the Ruled Taxonomy and the Built Code
status_evidence: systems/settlements/sim/ledger.py:30 (verified directly: TAG_KINDS has Leverage, not Compact)
statement: cross_scale_action_catalogue_v1.md §2.4 (dated 2026-08-27, more current than either the stress test or the ED-IN-0046 ruling) lists "The Ledger of Consequence — five tag families (P5)" as Precedent/Grudge/Debt/Reputation/Compact — omitting Leverage and reinstating Compact as a top-level family. This directly contradicts both the built code (ledger.py's TAG_KINDS has Leverage, not Compact) and ED-IN-0046 D3's own ruling (Compact = Debt subtype). The three-way disagreement (ruling vs code vs the newest reference doc) is live and unresolved as of the current tree.

name: Ruling — Retire Section 1.8 Mandate as the Cross-Scale Collapse Carrier
statement: ED-IN-0046 D4 (RATIFIED 2026-07-13) rules YES to retiring settlement_layer §1.8's Mandate formula as the collapse carrier and renaming the faction Mandate meter — a direct, one-day-later ruling on the settlement-season stress test's Pattern H finding (Mandate saturation masks peripheral collapse, H9-066) that the stress test itself did not know about. Whether the retire action has since been executed in code was not independently re-verified.

name: Bind-the-Cells Actor Collision Sharpened to Three Conflated Granularities
statement: The stress test's §1.3b vs §4.5 "actor-cap" collision (a frontier settlement cannot populate the 5-household cells Bind-the-Cells requires) is confirmed and sharpened: three distinct granularities are conflated — §4.5 Local Actors (a count-per-settlement-type, "1-2"), named NPC dossiers (Goldenfurt carries 9; registry.py's npc_ids is uncapped), and the 5-household population cells Bind-the-Cells needs, which no layer models at all. The fix is a missing population-granularity layer, not a raised actor cap.

name: Territory-Scale Governor AP Economy Is Undefined
statement: A multi-settlement territory governor's AP-triage premise (stress test S6) rests on an unspecified rule: political_hierarchy §2.5 makes governance explicitly per-settlement (a faction can appoint different Governors to different territories within the same province), no multi-settlement AP aggregation exists in canon, and march_layer is an army movement budget, not a governor's action-point pool. Consistent with baseline audit finding G1 (province aggregation "can never fire" absent a registry, since partially closed by registry.py).

name: Two Unreconciled Season-Event Architectures for Settlement Governance
statement: settlement_mgmt_stress_01 (the 500-seed executed run) used a predicate-sweep event model — events as pure functions of settlement state, co-firing, chaining via shared state, no deck — while governance_play_redesign/Goldenfurt/PR#119's grounded event deck uses a stateful card deck (Pi-weighted draw, cooldowns, forced queue, seeds: chaining); these are two different engines for "what happens to a settlement each season," and ratifying deck content without deciding which architecture is canonical risks authoring into the losing one.

name: Two Unreconciled Action-Point Models for Settlement Governance
statement: settlement_mgmt_stress_01 (the 500-seed executed framework) has no AP economy at all (discrete predicate-gated handlers), while governance-redesign/Goldenfurt use AP = 2 + facility_tier (+1 Seat/Cathedral) — the same architecture fork as H9-072, on the action-economy axis specifically.

name: Settlement Type-Taxonomy Drift (8 Canonical Types vs 9-11 in Use) Is Still Live
status_evidence: systems/settlements/settlement_layer_v30.md:160 (verified directly: base(Type) lists Seat/City/Cathedral/Town/Fortress/Port/Village/Mine/Outpost — 9 types including Village, which the doc's own canonical §1.2 8-type list and its :858 count-by-type table both omit)
statement: Canon's §1.2 8 settlement types (Seat/City/Town/Fortress/Port/Cathedral/Mine/Outpost) diverge from a real 9-11-type set used elsewhere in the same document and in the §2.1 registry (adding Village, Fortress-City, Cathedral-City); cross-confirmed by the pre-existing baseline audit (H3) and the 500-seed framework (F1, the structural root of 7 of its findings). Independently reproduced against the current tree: settlement_layer_v30.md:160 lists Village alongside the canonical 8 while its own :858 count-by-type table does not.

name: PR#119 Faction-Standing Items Rest on Inert L/PS Substrate
baseline_ref: cross_scale_action_catalogue_v1.md §9.2 item 3 ("no holdings model below a list of territory ids"; ED-FA-0004 named open there too)
statement: PR#119's §1.0b/c/d faction-standing items and the §1.8 Mandate feedback all read L/PS (Legitimacy/Popular Support at per-settlement grain), which are declared-but-inert in the sim (ED-FA-0004, port-blocking) — these items can be ratified as design prose but have no implementation substrate, which is worth stating plainly so "ratified" is not mistaken for "implemented."

name: Locked Extraction/Survey/Encabezamiento Has No Subsistence Floor or Reversal Verb
statement: §1.3a's Survey/Assessment lock (assessing a settlement's base Prosperity for taxation) writes/ locks correctly but has no subsistence floor, an ~8-season cooldown that outlives the triggering crisis, and no verb that reverses it once Prosperity falls post-lock — a deterministic strip, not a probabilistic risk, once a locked settlement's Prosperity declines. Compact-vs-Directive precedence is also undefined.

name: Bind the Cells Reliably Inverts Order Into a Revolt Accelerant
statement: Where Bind-the-Cells does run, Collective-Liability reliably converts the Order-management tool into a revolt engine: one infraction triggers whole-cell Collective Liability (Disposition -1), stacking to 3 fires a Cell Revolt Crisis (Order collapse, PS collapse, secession-class in one seed) — measured in ~6/7 seeds where the mechanic could fire at all.

name: Appeals Against a Demotion Essentially Never Succeed (0/6 Across Seeds)
statement: Standing-Appeal contests against a Demotion resolved 0/6 across the 7-seed sample at roughly 20-31% odds versus a Std-7 adjudicator, often with Reputation penalties stacked on top; if the Appeal window is intended as a real remedy rather than a formality, the adjudicator Ob is miscalibrated too high.

name: Demotion Spiral Is Near-Deterministic Given Canon's Roll Cadence
statement: A governor faces 3-4 major rolls per season at roughly 40-60% each (ground-truth-verified: mid dice_pool rolls are ~55%, not the ~48% agents initially assumed); over 5 seasons, never logging the 3 failures that trip a §1.0a Demotion is statistically negligible, making the tragic-downfall arc the current default outcome rather than an edge case (Pattern A, 7/7 seeds universal).

name: No Character Attribute Block Bound in the Settlement-Season Seed/Roster Spec
statement: Every governor pool size in the stress test was engine-assigned because no seed/roster spec binds personal-scale character attributes (Cognition/Charisma/History/etc); reconciliation against existing work narrows this to a test-harness gap rather than a canon hole, since Attributes are a personal-scale (PC) concern and the Settlement schema itself is fully defined.

name: Parliament Is a Division-Only Stub With No Agenda Control
statement: S5 Parliament resolves as a single pooled roll (a division) with no agenda control, no speaking order, no veto, no drafting right, no enactment clock and no session slots; upload 1 argues that in most real assemblies "the vote is a formality" — in Valoria's built parliament it is the only thing that exists.

name: Succession Contest Is a Real Selection Mechanism, but Benches Are Never Constituted
status_evidence: systems/social_contest/sim/faction.py:93-95 (succession split ratios computed; consequences explicitly unmodelled)
statement: The Succession Contest's graduated split-ratio mechanism is a real, ahead-of-the-uploads selection system, but its adjudicating bench is never constituted from named NPCs (a _default_panel is hardcoded), investiture confers nothing mechanically, and the split's downstream consequences are computed and explicitly left unmodelled.

name: LedgerTag — The Corpus's One Real "Record" Primitive
statement: LedgerTag (Precedent/Grudge/Debt/Reputation/Leverage) is deduped, TTL-aware, swept on season boundaries, and lives on the Settlement rather than the governor so it survives succession — the single-owner primitive this repo already has for "a record that guards a later transition," per CLAUDE.md §0's core composition rule.

name: Social Contest Writes Bespoke Stat Deltas Instead of Composing on LedgerTag
statement: Every wired social-contest output is a stat delta; a Decisive win could emit a Precedent, an Obligation could be a Debt (Compact was already ruled a Debt subtype, ED-IN-0046 D3), and a violation could emit a Grudge onto the existing LedgerTag primitive, but none of this composition exists — the contest system re-implements a rule (durable consequence) that already lives once, one subsystem over.

name: tribunal.py Deleted the Only Canonical Record-Guard in the Corpus
statement: Canon's Excommunication prerequisite ("2 prior Tribunal convictions OR documented Obligation violation") was deleted from tribunal.py's formal_grounds_check as "a personal-scale concept not yet ported," removing the one place in the corpus where a prior Record actually gated a later transition.

name: A Personal Contest Win Can Bind an Entire Faction With No Authority Check
statement: social_contest_v30.md:310-312 lets a personal contest win bind an entire faction with no check that the orator could actually bind anyone and no repudiation path except breach; faction_politics_v30.md:74 consumes Obligations in its demotion table for an object (Obligation with scope/limits) that has no producer anywhere.

name: Faction Opposition Has No Aims, Red Lines, Concession Curve, or Patience — the AI Cannot Concede
statement: The social-contest move vocabulary (advance/hard/shift/support/pass/evidence/rebut) has no concession move, so the AI opponent cannot concede; Faction.fixed_lean is a hardcoded red line, but since no side-payment verb exists at all, "unbuyable" is unfalsifiable — nothing is buyable, so obstruction can never end for a negotiated reason.

name: PP-349 Church Shield / Niflhel Ob Formula Are Scripting Drift Over an Existing Config Field
statement: §9.7's bespoke Niflhel Ob formula and PP-349's Church shield are entity special-cases where a config field already exists — Faction.parliamentary=False (systems/social_contest/sim/parliamentary_vote.py:25-27) — the same class of scripting drift CLAUDE.md §10 names, and both are re-keyable onto that flag rather than hardcoded per faction.

name: Faction Opposition Model Needs an FA-Lane Co-Owner
statement: The proposed opposition model (aims, unbuyable red lines, threat-as-concealed-value, concession curve, patience) for social-contest AI factions is filed as SC-lane work but is explicitly named as needing an FA-lane co-owner, since the fields it would add (aims, patience) belong on the Faction object the FA lane owns, not on the contest kernel.

name: Two Competing Roadmaps for the Same Governance/Social-Contest Subsystem Are Unreconciled
statement: HANDOFF_SC.md and CURRENT.md still carry "Stage 4 - four games - next" as the live, Gate-0-ratified plan for this subsystem, while a separate CIP-numbered proposal programme covers the same subsystem as a different roadmap; no filed document reconciles the two, and closing that gap is itself an un-filed needs-Jordan item.

name: The Duality Doctrine's Own "Chief Build Implication" Is Uncovered by Any Filed Proposal
statement: The Auto/Manual Resolution Duality doctrine names event-parameterizing the auto-resolver (so it resolves specific slate motions rather than a generic per-season roll) as its own chief build implication; checked against all filed CIP-0..12 proposals, nothing covers it.

name: Ratification Collisions — Several Contest-Reduction Proposals Touch Already-Ratified Items
statement: Three kill-list items (K2, K3, K9) and the proposed genre kill each touch a Jordan-ratified item (ED-1060 pending, ED-1062, ED-1056); under CLAUDE.md §2 none can land as routine work, so they are filed as recommendations with their reductive case stated rather than executed.

name: Parliamentary Bridge — Verified Live Every-Season Motion Mechanic
status_evidence: engine/mc_v18.py:151-152 (parliamentary vote call, ECHO_TRANSPORT-flag-gated); engine/cross_scale/parliamentary_bridge.py:82-97 (_derive_vote, verified directly); systems/social_contest/sim/parliamentary_vote.py:206-218 (verified directly)
formula: proposer = argmin(faction.Sta) among eligible parliamentary factions with territories; establishment = argmax(faction.L) among the rest; Total Victory at track>=9 or <=1 -> world.factions[dominant].adjust('L', -1 * MULTS['L'])
statement: parliamentary_bridge derives a two-pole Parliamentary motion every season from live faction state (lowest-Stability faction proposes on the Projection genre, highest-Mandate faction defends on Memory) and mc_v18 runs it each season, gated only by the ECHO_TRANSPORT flag (default ON since a 2026-07-08 Jordan ruling); a Total Victory writes back an Legitimacy/Mandate penalty directly to world.factions. Verified directly against the current tree at each cited path.

name: Bug — Parliamentary "One-Season" Mandate Penalty Is Applied Permanently
status_evidence: systems/social_contest/sim/parliamentary_vote.py:206-218 (verified directly: `-1 * MULTS['L']`, comment says one-season, no restoration path); engine/autoload/season_manager.py (verified directly: only advance_season/check_arc_boundary, no temporary-modifier facility exists)
formula: world.factions[dominant].adjust('L', BG_VOTE_TOTAL_VICTORY_MANDATE_DELTA * MULTS['L'])  # = -20 granular Legitimacy, permanent
statement: Every §10 Total Victory strips 20 granular Legitimacy from the losing dominant faction with a code comment reading "[one-season penalty; temporary-modifier restoration deferred to season_manager]", but engine/autoload/season_manager.py has no temporary-modifier facility at all (only advance_season and check_arc_boundary) — verified directly against the current tree, the penalty is permanent against a spec that says one season.

name: The Parliamentary Topic Generator Derives Who, Never What
statement: _derive_vote (parliamentary_bridge.py) derives who raises a topic from world pressure (lowest-Stability proposes, highest-Mandate defends) but derives no what — the Motion's only content is motion_id=f"parl_s{season}" plus a fixed genre pair, so the identical contentless motion fires every season; a topic needs identity, a raising condition, and a retirement rule, consumed on resolution.

name: Emergency-Council/Parliamentary Churn Is Insufficient — a Low-Stability Faction Replays the Same Contest Forever
statement: Between two firings of the same council/parliamentary body, the only non-noise deltas are Legitimacy (perturbed by the contest itself) and contingently Stability (movable only by other factions, and 3 of its 4 writers push it down); proceeding, policies, bench, evidence and question are all pinned, so a faction at Stability<=2 without Church absolution replays the identical contest before the identical bench every season to campaign end.

name: ledger_add Overwrites Prior Reputation Tags, and Ledgers Have No Faction Holder Dimension
statement: ledger_add treats Reputation as SINGLE_VALUED by kind, ignoring the `key` field, so every prior Reputation tag is deleted on insert; separately, LedgerTag instances live on one Settlement only (no holder/faction dimension), and factions have no ledgers at all, so a faction-scale Record cannot be expressed on the existing primitive without extension.

name: NPC-as-Adjudicator Socket Exists but Nothing Populates It
statement: An adjudicator carries a ratified 4-axis Conviction vector (armature_position) whose STYLE_AXIS already maps three of four canonical Resonant Styles onto judge behaviour, but nothing populates the vector from an NPC sheet — the default is near-uniform (0.34/0.33/0.33), so judge identity is inert until authored data exists. systems/social_contest/sim/faction.py:39 already demonstrates the correct derivation-adapter pattern (deriving an Adjudicator from faction stats).

name: Adjudicator Bench Positions Are Keyed by Ephemeral Python Object Identity
statement: ArmatureConfig keys a bench adjudicator's position by id(adjudicator) — ephemeral Python object identity — which cannot survive a save and is defeated even within one session because fresh Adjudicator objects are constructed per call; the fix is to key by actor_id, the namespace targets[].actor_id already uses.

name: Knot-Betrayal Rupture Is Unfireable in Principle — EvidenceItem Has No Provenance Field
statement: check_knot_rupture implements canon's "public citation of extracted private Knot counsel is immediate rupture, -3 Disposition" rule correctly, but has zero callers outside its own module and one test, and is unfireable in principle rather than merely unwired: EvidenceItem carries only ground/weight/appeal with no provenance field, so the kernel cannot distinguish extracted Knot counsel from any other evidence to trigger the rupture on.

name: conviction.py's CONVICTIONS Tuple Is Neither the Canonical 13 Nor the Legacy Set (Breaks PP-724's Scar Rules Too)
statement: conviction.py's CONVICTIONS tuple mixes retired labels under a comment claiming it is the canonical 13; the only live caller passes 'Loyalty', which is in no set, so the call silently no-ops while reporting conviction_scar=1. PP-724's relational-edge break rules scar Honor and Authority — both canonical, both missing from this same gate — so a faithful PP-724 implementation would silently no-op through the identical hole; fix belongs on the gate, not the call site.
